decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction
decls.doc: The submodule of functions on `G` that are constant under conjugation.
decls.statement: def ClassFunction (k : Type u) (G : Type v) [Semiring k] [Group G] : Submodule k (G → k)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.mem_iff
decls.doc: A function is a class function exactly when it is invariant under conjugation.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_iff {f : G → k} :
    f ∈ ClassFunction k G ↔ ∀ g h : G, f (h * g * h⁻¹) = f g

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.eq_of_isConj
decls.doc: Class functions take the same value on conjugate elements.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_of_isConj (f : ClassFunction k G) {g h : G} (hgh : IsConj g h) :
    f.1 g = f.1 h

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.toConjClasses
decls.doc: Evaluate a class function on a conjugacy class.
decls.statement: def toConjClasses (f : ClassFunction k G) : ConjClasses G → k

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.toConjClasses_mk
decls.doc: Evaluating the induced function on the class of `g` gives the value at `g`.
decls.statement:
theorem toConjClasses_mk (f : ClassFunction k G) (g : G) :
    toConjClasses f (ConjClasses.mk g) = f.1 g

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.ofConjClasses
decls.doc: Pull a function on conjugacy classes back to a class function on the group.
decls.statement: def ofConjClasses (f : ConjClasses G → k) : ClassFunction k G

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.ofConjClasses_apply
decls.doc: Pulling back a function on conjugacy classes evaluates it on the class of `g`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofConjClasses_apply (f : ConjClasses G → k) (g : G) :
    (ofConjClasses f).1 g = f (ConjClasses.mk g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.equivConjClasses
decls.doc: Class functions on `G` are linearly equivalent to functions on its conjugacy classes.
decls.statement: def equivConjClasses : ClassFunction k G ≃ₗ[k] (ConjClasses G → k)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.equivConjClasses_apply
decls.doc: The linear equivalence is given by `toConjClasses`.
decls.statement:
theorem equivConjClasses_apply (f : ClassFunction k G) :
    equivConjClasses f = toConjClasses f

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.equivConjClasses_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse linear equivalence is given by `ofConjClasses`.
decls.statement:
theorem equivConjClasses_symm_apply (f : ConjClasses G → k) :
    equivConjClasses.symm f = ofConjClasses f

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.finrank_eq_card_conjClasses
decls.doc: The dimension of the space of class functions is the number of conjugacy classes.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_eq_card_conjClasses [Finite (ConjClasses G)] :
    Module.finrank k (ClassFunction k G) = Nat.card (ConjClasses G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.ofCharacter
decls.doc: The character of a representation is a class function.
decls.statement:
def ofCharacter {V : Type w} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (ρ : Representation k G V) : ClassFunction k G

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.ofCharacter_apply
decls.doc: The class function of a representation evaluates to its character.
decls.statement:
theorem ofCharacter_apply {V : Type w} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (ρ : Representation k G V) (g : G) :
    (ofCharacter ρ).1 g = ρ.character g

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.ofFDRep
decls.doc: The character of a finite-dimensional bundled representation is a class function.
decls.statement: def ofFDRep (V : FDRep k G) : ClassFunction k G

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.ofFDRep_apply
decls.doc: The class function of a bundled finite-dimensional representation evaluates to its character.
decls.statement:
theorem ofFDRep_apply (V : FDRep k G) (g : G) :
    (ofFDRep V).1 g = V.character g

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum
decls.doc: The sum in `k[G]` of the elements in the conjugacy class `C`.
decls.statement: def classSum (k : Type*) [Semiring k] (C : ConjClasses G) : MonoidAlgebra k G

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum_eq_sum
decls.doc: A class sum is the sum of the basis elements in its conjugacy class.
decls.statement:
theorem classSum_eq_sum {k : Type*} [Semiring k] (C : ConjClasses G) :
    classSum k C = ∑ x : C.carrier, MonoidAlgebra.of k G x

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum_coeff
decls.doc: The coefficient of `g` in the class sum of `C` is `1` if `g` lies in `C`, and `0` otherwise.
decls.statement:
theorem classSum_coeff {k : Type*} [Semiring k] (C : ConjClasses G) (g : G) :
    (classSum k C).coeff g = if ConjClasses.mk g = C then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.conjugateCarrierEquiv
decls.doc: Conjugation by `g` permutes every conjugacy class.
decls.statement: def conjugateCarrierEquiv (g : G) (C : ConjClasses G) : C.carrier ≃ C.carrier

decls.name: TauCeti.conjugateCarrierEquiv_apply
decls.doc: `conjugateCarrierEquiv g C` sends `x` to its conjugate `g * x * g⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjugateCarrierEquiv_apply (g : G) (C : ConjClasses G) (x : C.carrier) :
    (conjugateCarrierEquiv g C x : G) = g * x * g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum_commutes
decls.doc: A class sum commutes with each group element in the group algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem classSum_commutes {k : Type*} [Semiring k] (C : ConjClasses G) (g : G) :
    classSum k C * MonoidAlgebra.of k G g = MonoidAlgebra.of k G g * classSum k C

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum_mk_one
decls.doc:
The class sum of the conjugacy class of `1` is the unit of the group algebra: that class is the
singleton `{1}`.
decls.statement:
theorem classSum_mk_one (k : Type*) [Semiring k] :
    classSum k (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum_mem_center
decls.doc: Every class sum lies in the center of the group algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem classSum_mem_center (k : Type*) [CommSemiring k] (C : ConjClasses G) :
    classSum k C ∈ Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)

decls.name: TauCeti.centerToClassFunction
decls.doc: The coefficient function of a central group-algebra element, as a class function on `G`.
decls.statement:
def centerToClassFunction :
    Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₗ[k] ClassFunction k G

decls.name: TauCeti.centerToClassFunction_apply
decls.doc: The class function of a central element is its coefficient function.
decls.statement:
theorem centerToClassFunction_apply (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) (g : G) :
    (centerToClassFunction z).1 g = z.1.coeff g

decls.name: TauCeti.center_coeff_eq_of_isConj
decls.doc: The coefficients of a central group-algebra element agree on conjugate group elements.
decls.statement:
theorem center_coeff_eq_of_isConj (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G))
    {g h : G} (hgh : IsConj g h) :
    z.1.coeff g = z.1.coeff h

decls.name: TauCeti.centerToConjClasses
decls.doc: Read the coefficients of a central group-algebra element as a function on conjugacy classes.
decls.statement:
def centerToConjClasses
    (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) : ConjClasses G → k

decls.name: TauCeti.centerToConjClasses_mk
decls.doc: Reading the coefficient on the conjugacy class of `g` recovers the coefficient at `g`.
decls.statement:
theorem centerToConjClasses_mk (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) (g : G) :
    centerToConjClasses z (ConjClasses.mk g) = z.1.coeff g

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumCenter
decls.doc: Regard a class sum as an element of the center of the group algebra.
decls.statement:
def classSumCenter (C : ConjClasses G) :
    Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumCenter_coe
decls.doc: The underlying group-algebra element of a central class sum is the class sum.
decls.statement:
theorem classSumCenter_coe (C : ConjClasses G) :
    (classSumCenter (k := k) C : MonoidAlgebra k G) = classSum k C

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumCenter_mk_one
decls.doc: The class sum of the conjugacy class of `1`, as an element of the center, is `1`.
decls.statement: theorem classSumCenter_mk_one : classSumCenter (k := k) (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.ofConjClassesCenter
decls.doc:
Convert a function on conjugacy classes to the corresponding linear combination of class
sums.
decls.statement:
def ofConjClassesCenter (f : ConjClasses G → k) :
    Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ofConjClassesCenter_coeff
decls.doc: The coefficient at `g` of the class-sum expansion is the value on the class of `g`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofConjClassesCenter_coeff (f : ConjClasses G → k) (g : G) :
    (ofConjClassesCenter f : MonoidAlgebra k G).coeff g = f (ConjClasses.mk g)

decls.name: TauCeti.centerEquivConjClasses
decls.doc:
The center of a finite group algebra is linearly equivalent to the functions on conjugacy
classes, by taking coefficients.
decls.statement:
def centerEquivConjClasses :
    Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) ≃ₗ[k] (ConjClasses G → k)

decls.name: TauCeti.centerEquivConjClasses_apply
decls.doc: The forward map of `centerEquivConjClasses` reads the coefficients of a central element.
decls.statement:
theorem centerEquivConjClasses_apply
    (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) :
    centerEquivConjClasses z = centerToConjClasses z

decls.name: TauCeti.centerEquivConjClasses_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of `centerEquivConjClasses` forms the corresponding linear combination of class
sums.
decls.statement:
theorem centerEquivConjClasses_symm_apply (f : ConjClasses G → k) :
    centerEquivConjClasses.symm f = ofConjClassesCenter f

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumBasis
decls.doc: The class sums, regarded as central group-algebra elements, form a basis of the center.
decls.statement:
def classSumBasis :
    Module.Basis (ConjClasses G) k (Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G))

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumBasis_apply
decls.doc: A vector in the class-sum basis is the corresponding central class sum.
decls.statement:
theorem classSumBasis_apply (C : ConjClasses G) :
    classSumBasis (k := k) C = classSumCenter (k := k) C

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumBasis_repr_apply
decls.doc:
The coordinate of a central element in the class-sum basis is its coefficient on that
conjugacy class.
decls.statement:
theorem classSumBasis_repr_apply
    (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) (C : ConjClasses G) :
    (classSumBasis (k := k)).repr z C = centerToConjClasses z C

decls.name: TauCeti.instModuleFiniteCenterMonoidAlgebra
decls.doc: The center of a finite group algebra is finite as a module, with its class-sum basis.
decls.statement:
instance instModuleFiniteCenterMonoidAlgebra :
    Module.Finite k (Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G))

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_center_monoidAlgebra
decls.doc: The dimension of the center of a finite group algebra is the number of conjugacy classes.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_center_monoidAlgebra :
    Module.finrank k (Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) =
      Nat.card (ConjClasses G)

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumRow
decls.doc: The row of values of an algebra homomorphism out of the centre of `k[G]` on the class sums.
decls.statement:
def classSumRow (φ : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k) :
    ConjClasses G → k

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumRow_apply
decls.statement:
theorem classSumRow_apply (φ : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k)
    (C : ConjClasses G) : classSumRow φ C = φ (classSumCenter C)

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumRow_mk_one
decls.doc:
The class sum of the class of `1` is the unit of the centre, so every algebra homomorphism
takes the value `1` there: the row of an algebra homomorphism is normalized.
decls.statement:
theorem classSumRow_mk_one (φ : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k) :
    classSumRow φ (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumRow_injective
decls.doc:
An algebra homomorphism out of the centre of `k[G]` is determined by its values on the class
sums, because those are a basis.
decls.statement:
theorem classSumRow_injective :
    Function.Injective (classSumRow (G := G) (k := k))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsClassEigenrow
decls.doc:
A function on the conjugacy classes of `G` is a **common left eigenrow** of the
class-multiplication matrices when, for every class `Cᵢ`, it is a left eigenvector of
`classMultMatrix Cᵢ` with eigenvalue its own value at `Cᵢ`.

The row/`ᵥ*` orientation is the one pinned by `TauCeti.classMultMatrix`; the transposed matrix would
be needed for the column/`*ᵥ` convention.
decls.statement: def IsClassEigenrow (v : ConjClasses G → k) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isClassEigenrow_def
decls.doc:
`TauCeti.IsClassEigenrow` restated in its defining vector form, for consumers that want the
literal eigenvector equation without unfolding the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem isClassEigenrow_def (v : ConjClasses G → k) :
    IsClassEigenrow v ↔ ∀ Cᵢ : ConjClasses G,
      v ᵥ* (classMultMatrix Cᵢ).map (Int.cast : ℤ → k) = v Cᵢ • v

decls.name: TauCeti.vecMul_classMultMatrix_apply
decls.doc:
Acting with a class-multiplication matrix on a row vector from the left contracts the row
against the structure constants.
decls.statement:
theorem vecMul_classMultMatrix_apply (v : ConjClasses G → k) (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) :
    (v ᵥ* (classMultMatrix Cᵢ).map (Int.cast : ℤ → k)) Cⱼ =
      ∑ Cₖ : ConjClasses G, (structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : k) * v Cₖ

decls.name: TauCeti.isClassEigenrow_iff
decls.doc:
The eigenrow condition, unwound into the scalar identity
`∑ₖ aᵢⱼₖ v Cₖ = v Cᵢ * v Cⱼ` on the structure constants.
decls.statement:
theorem isClassEigenrow_iff (v : ConjClasses G → k) :
    IsClassEigenrow v ↔ ∀ Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G,
      ∑ Cₖ : ConjClasses G, (structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : k) * v Cₖ = v Cᵢ * v Cⱼ

decls.name: TauCeti.isClassEigenrow_zero
decls.doc:
The zero row is a common left eigenrow. This is why the correspondence with algebra
homomorphisms needs the normalization `v (ConjClasses.mk 1) = 1`.
decls.statement: theorem isClassEigenrow_zero : IsClassEigenrow (0 : ConjClasses G → k)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsClassEigenrow.mk_one_smul
decls.doc:
The value of a common left eigenrow at the class of `1` acts as an identity on the row: the
class-multiplication matrix at the class of `1` is the identity matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem IsClassEigenrow.mk_one_smul {v : ConjClasses G → k} (hv : IsClassEigenrow v) :
    v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) • v = v

decls.name: TauCeti.IsClassEigenrow.mk_one_eq_one
decls.doc:
Over a ring without zero divisors, a **nonzero** common left eigenrow is automatically
normalized: its value at the class of `1` is `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsClassEigenrow.mk_one_eq_one [NoZeroDivisors k] {v : ConjClasses G → k}
    (hv : IsClassEigenrow v) (hv₀ : v ≠ 0) : v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.eq_of_vecMul_classMultMatrix_eq_smul
decls.doc:
**The eigenvalue of a normalized common left eigenvector is forced.** If `v` takes the value `1`
at the class of `1` and `v ᵥ* Mᵢ = c • v` for some scalar `c`, then `c = v Cᵢ`: evaluating at the
class of `1` reads the eigenvalue off the row.
decls.title: The eigenvalue of a normalized common left eigenvector is forced

decls.name: TauCeti.isClassEigenrow_of_forall_exists_smul
decls.doc:
**A normalized common left eigenvector of the class-multiplication matrices is an eigenrow.**
Only the existence of *some* eigenvalue for each matrix has to be checked; the normalization forces
it to be the row's own value.
decls.title: A normalized common left eigenvector of the class-multiplication matrices is an eigenrow
decls.statement:
theorem isClassEigenrow_of_forall_exists_smul {v : ConjClasses G → k}
    (hv₁ : v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1)
    (h : ∀ Cᵢ : ConjClasses G,
      ∃ c : k, v ᵥ* (classMultMatrix Cᵢ).map (Int.cast : ℤ → k) = c • v) :
    IsClassEigenrow v

decls.name: TauCeti.isClassEigenrow_classSumRow
decls.doc:
**The values of an algebra homomorphism on the class sums form a common left eigenrow.** This
is the coordinate identity `TauCeti.classSumCenter_mul` pushed through `φ`.
decls.title: The values of an algebra homomorphism on the class sums form a common left eigenrow
decls.statement:
theorem isClassEigenrow_classSumRow (φ : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k) :
    IsClassEigenrow (classSumRow φ)

decls.name: TauCeti.map_mul_of_basis
decls.doc:
The linear extension of a row of scalars along the class-sum basis is multiplicative as soon as
it is multiplicative on the basis itself.
decls.statement:
theorem map_mul_of_basis
    {f : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₗ[k] k}
    (hf : ∀ Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G,
      f (classSumCenter Cᵢ * classSumCenter Cⱼ) = f (classSumCenter Cᵢ) * f (classSumCenter Cⱼ))
    (x y : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) : f (x * y) = f x * f y

decls.name: TauCeti.eigenrowAlgHom
decls.doc:
**The algebra homomorphism attached to a normalized common left eigenrow**: the linear extension
of `v` along the class-sum basis. Multiplicativity is the eigenrow condition read through the
coordinate identity, and it is unital because the class sum at the class of `1` is `1`.
decls.title: The algebra homomorphism attached to a normalized common left eigenrow
decls.statement:
def eigenrowAlgHom (hv₁ : v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1)
    (hv : IsClassEigenrow v) : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k

decls.name: TauCeti.eigenrowAlgHom_classSumCenter
decls.statement:
theorem eigenrowAlgHom_classSumCenter (hv₁ : v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1)
    (hv : IsClassEigenrow v) (C : ConjClasses G) :
    eigenrowAlgHom hv₁ hv (classSumCenter C) = v C

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumRow_eigenrowAlgHom
decls.statement:
theorem classSumRow_eigenrowAlgHom (hv₁ : v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1)
    (hv : IsClassEigenrow v) : classSumRow (eigenrowAlgHom hv₁ hv) = v

decls.name: TauCeti.isClassEigenrow_iff_exists_algHom
decls.doc:
**Normalized common left eigenrows are exactly the class-algebra homomorphisms.** A function `v`
on the conjugacy classes with `v (ConjClasses.mk 1) = 1` is a common left eigenvector of every
class-multiplication matrix, with eigenvalue `v Cᵢ` at `Cᵢ`, if and only if it is the row of values
of a `k`-algebra homomorphism `Z(k[G]) →ₐ[k] k` on the class sums.
decls.title: Normalized common left eigenrows are exactly the class-algebra homomorphisms
decls.statement:
theorem isClassEigenrow_iff_exists_algHom (hv₁ : v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1) :
    IsClassEigenrow v ↔
      ∃ φ : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k, classSumRow φ = v

decls.name: TauCeti.algHomEquivEigenrow
decls.doc:
**The algebra homomorphisms out of the centre of `k[G]` are the normalized common left
eigenrows of the class-multiplication matrices**, bundled as an equivalence: a homomorphism goes to
its row of values on the class sums, and a row extends linearly along the class-sum basis.

decls.name: TauCeti.algHomEquivEigenrow_apply_coe
decls.statement:
theorem algHomEquivEigenrow_apply_coe (φ : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) →ₐ[k] k) :
    (algHomEquivEigenrow φ : ConjClasses G → k) = classSumRow φ

decls.name: TauCeti.algHomEquivEigenrow_symm_apply_classSumCenter
decls.statement:
theorem algHomEquivEigenrow_symm_apply_classSumCenter
    (v : {v : ConjClasses G → k // v (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1 ∧ IsClassEigenrow v})
    (C : ConjClasses G) :
    algHomEquivEigenrow.symm v (classSumCenter C) = (v : ConjClasses G → k) C

decls.name: TauCeti.isIntegral_classSum
decls.doc: A class sum is integral over `ℤ` as an element of the center of `ℤ[G]`.
decls.statement:
theorem isIntegral_classSum {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]
    (C : ConjClasses G) :
    IsIntegral ℤ (classSumCenter (k := ℤ) C)

decls.name: TauCeti.leftMulMatrix_classSumCenter_apply
decls.doc:
**The structure constants are the matrix of multiplication by a class sum**, entrywise: the
matrix of left multiplication by `K_{Cᵢ}` on the centre of `k[G]`, in the class-sum basis, has
`(Cⱼ, Cₖ)` entry `aᵢₖⱼ`.
decls.title: The structure constants are the matrix of multiplication by a class sum
decls.statement:
theorem leftMulMatrix_classSumCenter_apply (Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) :
    Algebra.leftMulMatrix (classSumBasis (k := k)) (classSumCenter Cᵢ) Cⱼ Cₖ =
      (structureConstant Cᵢ Cₖ Cⱼ : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix
decls.doc:
**The class-multiplication matrix** of a conjugacy class `Cᵢ` of a finite group: the integer
matrix with `(Cⱼ, Cₖ)` entry the structure constant `aᵢₖⱼ`.

The transposed index order is fixed so that `classMultMatrix Cᵢ` is the matrix of left
multiplication by the class sum `K_{Cᵢ}` on the centre of the group algebra, taken in the class-sum
basis (`TauCeti.classMultMatrix_map_intCast`).
decls.title: The class-multiplication matrix
decls.statement: def classMultMatrix (Cᵢ : ConjClasses G) : Matrix (ConjClasses G) (ConjClasses G) ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_apply
decls.statement:
theorem classMultMatrix_apply (Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) :
    classMultMatrix Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ = (structureConstant Cᵢ Cₖ Cⱼ : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_map_intCast
decls.doc:
**The class-multiplication matrix is the matrix of multiplication by the class sum**: pushing
`classMultMatrix Cᵢ` into any commutative ring `k` gives the matrix of left multiplication by
`K_{Cᵢ}` on the centre of `k[G]`, taken in the class-sum basis.
decls.title: The class-multiplication matrix is the matrix of multiplication by the class sum
decls.statement:
theorem classMultMatrix_map_intCast (k : Type*) [CommRing k] (Cᵢ : ConjClasses G) :
    (classMultMatrix Cᵢ).map (Int.cast : ℤ → k) =
      Algebra.leftMulMatrix (classSumBasis (k := k)) (classSumCenter Cᵢ)

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_eq_leftMulMatrix
decls.doc:
The class-multiplication matrix over `ℤ` is itself a matrix of multiplication by a class sum,
namely in the centre of the integral group algebra `ℤ[G]`.
decls.statement:
theorem classMultMatrix_eq_leftMulMatrix (Cᵢ : ConjClasses G) :
    classMultMatrix Cᵢ = Algebra.leftMulMatrix (classSumBasis (k := ℤ)) (classSumCenter Cᵢ)

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_commute
decls.doc:
**The class-multiplication matrices commute pairwise.** They are the images of the class sums
under an algebra homomorphism out of the centre of `ℤ[G]`, which is commutative.
decls.title: The class-multiplication matrices commute pairwise
decls.statement:
theorem classMultMatrix_commute (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) :
    Commute (classMultMatrix Cᵢ) (classMultMatrix (G := G) Cⱼ)

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_injective
decls.doc:
**Distinct conjugacy classes have distinct class-multiplication matrices**: multiplication by a
class sum determines it, and the class sums are a basis of the centre.
decls.title: Distinct conjugacy classes have distinct class-multiplication matrices
decls.statement:
theorem classMultMatrix_injective :
    Function.Injective (classMultMatrix (G := G))

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_mk_one
decls.doc:
The class-multiplication matrix at the conjugacy class of `1` is the identity matrix: the class
sum of `{1}` is the unit of the group algebra.
decls.statement: theorem classMultMatrix_mk_one : classMultMatrix (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.classMultMatrix_mulVec
decls.doc:
**The class-multiplication matrix acts by multiplication by the class sum**: it sends the vector
of class-sum coordinates of a central element `z` to the coordinates of `K_{Cᵢ} * z`.

This `*ᵥ` action is the defining property of a matrix of left multiplication; it is not the pinned
eigenvector relation, which is a `ᵥ*` action on the central-character row vectors.
decls.title: The class-multiplication matrix acts by multiplication by the class sum
decls.statement:
theorem classMultMatrix_mulVec (k : Type*) [CommRing k] (Cᵢ : ConjClasses G)
    (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) :
    (classMultMatrix Cᵢ).map (Int.cast : ℤ → k) *ᵥ centerToConjClasses z =
      centerToConjClasses (classSumCenter Cᵢ * z)

decls.name: TauCeti.StructureConstantFiber
decls.doc: The type of factorizations of `g` with first factor in `Cᵢ` and second factor in `Cⱼ`.
decls.statement: def StructureConstantFiber (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) (g : G)

decls.name: TauCeti.instFintypeStructureConstantFiber
decls.statement:
instance (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) (g : G) :
    Fintype (StructureConstantFiber Cᵢ Cⱼ g)

decls.name: TauCeti.structureConstantFiberEquiv
TauCeti.structureConstant
decls.doc:
The number of factorizations `x * y = g`, for `x ∈ Cᵢ`, `y ∈ Cⱼ`, and any representative
`g` of `Cₖ`. This is independent of the representative by simultaneous conjugation.
decls.statement: def structureConstant (Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.structureConstant_mk
decls.doc:
The structure constant at the conjugacy class of `g` counts the corresponding
factorizations of `g`.
decls.statement:
theorem structureConstant_mk (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) (g : G) :
    structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ (ConjClasses.mk g) =
      ((Finset.univ ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter
        fun p : Cᵢ.carrier × Cⱼ.carrier => (p.1.1 : G) * p.2.1 = g).card

decls.name: TauCeti.classSum_mul
decls.doc: Multiplication of class sums is governed by the structure constants.
decls.statement:
theorem classSum_mul (k : Type*) [Semiring k] (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) :
    classSum k Cᵢ * classSum k Cⱼ =
      ∑ Cₖ : ConjClasses G, (structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : k) • classSum k Cₖ

decls.name: TauCeti.classSumCenter_mul
decls.doc:
**The coordinate identity**: multiplication of class sums inside the centre of the group
algebra expands in the class-sum basis with the structure constants as coefficients. This is
`TauCeti.classSum_mul` read in the centre, where the class sums are a basis.
decls.title: The coordinate identity
decls.statement:
theorem classSumCenter_mul (k : Type*) [CommSemiring k] (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) :
    classSumCenter (k := k) Cᵢ * classSumCenter Cⱼ =
      ∑ Cₖ : ConjClasses G, (structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : k) • classSumCenter Cₖ

decls.name: TauCeti.coeff_classSum_mul
decls.doc:
The coefficient of `g` in a product of two class sums is the structure constant at the
conjugacy class of `g`. This is the pointwise form of `TauCeti.classSum_mul`.
decls.statement:
theorem coeff_classSum_mul (k : Type*) [Semiring k] (Cᵢ Cⱼ : ConjClasses G) (g : G) :
    (classSum k Cᵢ * classSum k Cⱼ).coeff g =
      (structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ (ConjClasses.mk g) : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.structureConstant_comm
decls.doc:
**The structure constants are symmetric in their two class arguments**, because the two class
sums commute in the group algebra.
decls.title: The structure constants are symmetric in their two class arguments
decls.statement:
theorem structureConstant_comm (Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) :
    structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ = structureConstant Cⱼ Cᵢ Cₖ

decls.name: TauCeti.structureConstant_mk_one_right
decls.doc:
**The class of `1` is a unit for the structure constants**: because `K_{Cᵢ} · K_{[1]} = K_{Cᵢ}`,
the constant `aᵢ,[1],ₖ` is `1` when `Cₖ = Cᵢ` and `0` otherwise.
decls.title: The class of `1` is a unit for the structure constants
decls.statement:
theorem structureConstant_mk_one_right (Cᵢ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) :
    structureConstant Cᵢ (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) Cₖ = if Cₖ = Cᵢ then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.structureConstant_mk_one_left
decls.doc: The symmetric companion of `TauCeti.structureConstant_mk_one_right`.
decls.statement:
theorem structureConstant_mk_one_left (Cⱼ Cₖ : ConjClasses G) :
    structureConstant (ConjClasses.mk (1 : G)) Cⱼ Cₖ = if Cₖ = Cⱼ then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.card_inv_mul_sum_mul_smul
decls.statement:
theorem card_inv_mul_sum_mul_smul (c : k) (f₁ f₂ : G → k) :
    (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, f₁ g * (c * f₂ g) =
      c * ((Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, f₁ g * f₂ g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing
decls.doc: The normalized bilinear pairing of class functions on a finite group.
decls.statement:
def characterPairing :
    LinearMap.BilinForm k (ClassFunction k G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_apply
decls.doc: The defining formula for the character pairing.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_apply (f₁ f₂ : ClassFunction k G) :
    characterPairing f₁ f₂ =
      (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, f₁.1 g * f₂.1 g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_symm
decls.doc: The character pairing is symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_symm (f₁ f₂ : ClassFunction k G) :
    characterPairing f₁ f₂ = characterPairing f₂ f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_isSymm
decls.doc: The bilinear form underlying `characterPairing` is symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_isSymm :
    characterPairing (k := k) (G := G).IsSymm

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.isConj_inv_iff
decls.statement:
theorem isConj_inv_iff {x y : G} :
    IsConj x⁻¹ y⁻¹ ↔ IsConj x y

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.classIndicator
decls.statement: def classIndicator (x : G) : ClassFunction k G

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.classIndicator_apply
decls.statement:
theorem classIndicator_apply (x y : G) :
    (classIndicator (k := k) x).1 y =
      if ConjClasses.mk y = ConjClasses.mk x then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.card_conjClass_dvd_card
decls.statement:
theorem card_conjClass_dvd_card [Finite G] (x : G) :
    Nat.card (ConjClasses.mk x).carrier ∣ Nat.card G

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.card_conjClass_cast_ne_zero
decls.statement:
theorem card_conjClass_cast_ne_zero [Finite G] [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] (x : G) :
    (Nat.card (ConjClasses.mk x).carrier : k) ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_nondegenerate
decls.doc: The character pairing is nondegenerate when the group order is invertible in the field.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_nondegenerate [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] :
    characterPairing (k := k) (G := G).Nondegenerate

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_ofCharacter
decls.doc: The pairing of two representation characters is Mathlib's normalized character sum.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_ofCharacter
    {V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W]
    (ρ : Representation k G V) (σ : Representation k G W) :
    characterPairing (ofCharacter ρ) (ofCharacter σ) =
      (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, ρ.character g * σ.character g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_ofFDRep
decls.doc:
The pairing of two finite-dimensional representation characters is Mathlib's normalized
character sum.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_ofFDRep (V W : FDRep k G) :
    characterPairing (ofFDRep V) (ofFDRep W) =
      (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, V.character g * W.character g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_ofCharacter_eq_finrank
decls.doc: The character pairing computes the dimension of an intertwiner space.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_ofCharacter_eq_finrank {V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [FiniteDimensional k V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W] [FiniteDimensional k W]
    [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] (ρ : Representation k G V) (σ : Representation k G W) :
    characterPairing (ofCharacter ρ) (ofCharacter σ) =
      Module.finrank k (Representation.IntertwiningMap σ ρ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_ofCharacter_orthonormal
decls.doc: The character pairing of irreducible characters is Kronecker orthonormal.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_ofCharacter_orthonormal {V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [FiniteDimensional k V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W] [FiniteDimensional k W]
    [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] [IsAlgClosed k] (ρ : Representation k G V)
    (σ : Representation k G W) [ρ.IsIrreducible] [σ.IsIrreducible] :
    characterPairing (ofCharacter ρ) (ofCharacter σ) =
      if Nonempty (Representation.Equiv σ ρ) then (1 : k) else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_ofFDRep_eq_finrank
decls.doc: The character pairing computes the dimension of a morphism space in `FDRep`.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_ofFDRep_eq_finrank [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] (V W : FDRep k G) :
    characterPairing (ofFDRep V) (ofFDRep W) = Module.finrank k (W ⟶ V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing_ofFDRep_orthonormal
decls.doc: The character pairing of simple finite-dimensional representations is Kronecker orthonormal.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_ofFDRep_orthonormal [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (V W : FDRep k G) [CategoryTheory.Simple V] [CategoryTheory.Simple W] :
    characterPairing (ofFDRep V) (ofFDRep W) =
      if Nonempty (V ≅ W) then (1 : k) else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_sq_eq_card_of_algEquiv_pi_matrix
decls.doc:
**The sum of the squares of the matrix sizes is the order of the group**: both sides compute
the dimension of `k[G]`.
decls.title: The sum of the squares of the matrix sizes is the order of the group
decls.statement:
theorem sum_sq_eq_card_of_algEquiv_pi_matrix [Monoid G] [Finite G] [Fintype ι]
    (e : MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k) :
    ∑ i, d i ^ 2 = Nat.card G

decls.name: TauCeti.centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi
decls.doc:
**The center of the group algebra splits**: a Wedderburn presentation of `k[G]` with blocks
indexed by `ι` identifies `Z(k[G])` with the algebra `ι → k` of functions on the blocks.
decls.title: The center of the group algebra splits
decls.statement:
def centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi [Monoid G] [∀ i, NeZero (d i)]
    (e : MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k) :
    Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G) ≃ₐ[k] (ι → k)

decls.name: TauCeti.algebraMap_centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi_apply
decls.doc:
`centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi e` records, block by block, the scalar that a central element of
`k[G]` acts by: the `i`-th component of the image of `e` is that scalar matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem algebraMap_centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi_apply [Monoid G] [∀ i, NeZero (d i)]
    (e : MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k)
    (z : Subalgebra.center k (MonoidAlgebra k G)) (i : ι) :
    algebraMap k (Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k) (centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi e z i) =
      e (z : MonoidAlgebra k G) i

decls.name: TauCeti.centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of `centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi e` builds the central element acting on each
block by the prescribed scalar.
decls.statement:
theorem centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi_symm_apply [Monoid G] [∀ i, NeZero (d i)]
    (e : MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k) (f : ι → k) (i : ι) :
    e ((centerMonoidAlgebraAlgEquivPi e).symm f : MonoidAlgebra k G) i =
      algebraMap k (Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k) (f i)

decls.name: TauCeti.card_eq_card_conjClasses_of_algEquiv_pi_matrix
decls.doc:
**The number of Wedderburn blocks of `k[G]` is the number of conjugacy classes of `G`**: both
sides compute the dimension of `Z(k[G])`.

This is the numerical half of the count `#irreducibles = #conjugacy classes`; identifying the blocks
with the isomorphism classes of simple `k[G]`-modules is a separate statement.
decls.title: The number of Wedderburn blocks of `k[G]` is the number of conjugacy classes of `G`
decls.statement:
theorem card_eq_card_conjClasses_of_algEquiv_pi_matrix [Group G] [Finite G] [Fintype ι]
    [∀ i, NeZero (d i)] (e : MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k) :
    Fintype.card ι = Nat.card (ConjClasses G)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix
decls.doc:
**Maschke and Artin--Wedderburn for a finite group algebra**: over an algebraically closed field
whose characteristic does not divide `|G|`, the group algebra is a finite product of matrix algebras
of positive size.
decls.title: Maschke and Artin--Wedderburn for a finite group algebra
decls.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, NeZero (d i)) ∧
      Nonempty (MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_conjClasses
decls.doc:
The Wedderburn decomposition of `k[G]`, with its blocks indexed by the conjugacy classes of `G`
themselves, and with the degrees squaring to a sum of `|G|`.

The indexing is by an arbitrary bijection between the blocks and the conjugacy classes: the
statement asserts nothing about *which* class labels a given block.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_conjClasses :
    ∃ d : ConjClasses G → ℕ, (∀ i, NeZero (d i)) ∧ ∑ᶠ i, d i ^ 2 = Nat.card G ∧
      Nonempty (MonoidAlgebra k G ≃ₐ[k] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareRepEquiv
decls.doc:
The tensor square of the standard representation is equivalent to the product of its
symmetric and exterior squares.
decls.statement:
abbrev tensorSquareRepEquiv :
    (tensorPowerRep k n 2).Equiv
      ((symPowerRep k n 2).prod (extPowerRep k n 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareFDRepIso
decls.doc:
The tensor-square decomposition bundled as an isomorphism in `FDRep`. The product
representation is the direct sum of the symmetric and exterior squares.

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareFDRepIso_hom_hom
decls.doc:
The forward map of the bundled tensor-square decomposition is the natural representation
equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem tensorSquareFDRepIso_hom_hom :
    (tensorSquareFDRepIso k n).hom.hom =
      ConcreteCategory.ofHom (tensorSquareRepEquiv k n).toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareFDRepIso_inv_hom
decls.doc:
The inverse map of the bundled tensor-square decomposition is the inverse natural
representation equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem tensorSquareFDRepIso_inv_hom :
    (tensorSquareFDRepIso k n).inv.hom =
      ConcreteCategory.ofHom (tensorSquareRepEquiv k n).symm.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.char_tensorSquare_stdRep
decls.doc:
Over any field, the square of the standard character is the sum of the symmetric-square
and exterior-square characters.
decls.statement:
theorem char_tensorSquare_stdRep (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    Matrix.trace (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k) ^ 2 =
      (symPowerRep k n 2).character g + (extPowerRep k n 2).character g

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerRep
decls.doc: The one-dimensional representation of `GL n k` on which `g` acts by `det(g)^m`.
decls.statement: def detPowerRep (m : ℤ) : Representation k (GL (Fin n) k) k

decls.name: TauCeti.detRep
decls.doc: The determinant representation of `GL n k`.
decls.statement: abbrev detRep : Representation k (GL (Fin n) k) k

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerRep_apply
decls.doc: The determinant-power action is scalar multiplication by the indicated determinant power.
decls.statement:
theorem detPowerRep_apply (m : ℤ) (g : GL (Fin n) k) (x : k) :
    detPowerRep k n m g x = (↑((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det g) ^ m) : k) * x

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerRep_zero
decls.doc: The zero determinant power is the trivial representation.
decls.statement: theorem detPowerRep_zero : detPowerRep k n 0 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerRep_add_apply
decls.doc: Adding exponents composes the corresponding determinant actions.
decls.statement:
theorem detPowerRep_add_apply (m l : ℤ) (g : GL (Fin n) k) (x : k) :
    detPowerRep k n (m + l) g x = detPowerRep k n m g (detPowerRep k n l g x)

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerRep_comp_toGL
decls.doc: Every determinant-power representation restricts to the trivial representation of `SL n k`.
decls.statement:
theorem detPowerRep_comp_toGL (m : ℤ) :
    (detPowerRep k n m).comp Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.toGL =
      Representation.trivial k (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) k) k

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerFDRep
decls.doc: The determinant-power representation as a finite-dimensional representation.
decls.statement: abbrev detPowerFDRep (m : ℤ) : FDRep k (GL (Fin n) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.detFDRep
decls.doc: The determinant representation as a finite-dimensional representation.
decls.statement: abbrev detFDRep : FDRep k (GL (Fin n) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.detPowerRep_neg_apply
decls.doc: Negating the exponent makes the determinant scalar the inverse of the original power.
decls.statement:
theorem detPowerRep_neg_apply (m : ℤ) (g : GL (Fin n) k) (x : k) :
    detPowerRep k n (-m) g x = (↑((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det g) ^ m) : k)⁻¹ * x

decls.name: TauCeti.char_detPowerRep
decls.doc: The character of the determinant-power representation is the corresponding determinant power.
decls.statement:
theorem char_detPowerRep (m : ℤ) (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    (detPowerRep k n m).character g = (↑((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det g) ^ m) : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.char_detPowerFDRep
decls.doc: The bundled determinant-power character is the corresponding determinant power.
decls.statement:
theorem char_detPowerFDRep (m : ℤ) (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    (detPowerFDRep k n m).character g = (↑((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det g) ^ m) : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.char_detFDRep
decls.doc: The bundled determinant character is the determinant.
decls.statement:
theorem char_detFDRep (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    (detFDRep k n).character g = (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det g : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.diagGL
decls.doc: Coordinatewise units embed in `GL n k` as diagonal matrices.
decls.statement: def diagGL : (Fin n → kˣ) →* GL (Fin n) k

decls.name: TauCeti.diagGL_coe
decls.doc: The matrix underlying `diagGL t` is the diagonal matrix with entries `t i`.
decls.statement:
theorem diagGL_coe (t : Fin n → kˣ) :
    (diagGL t : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k) =
      Matrix.diagonal fun i => (t i : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.diagGL_apply
decls.doc: The entries of `diagGL t` vanish off the diagonal and equal `t i` on it.
decls.statement:
theorem diagGL_apply (t : Fin n → kˣ) (i j : Fin n) :
    diagGL t i j = if i = j then (t i : k) else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.det_diagGL
decls.doc: The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal entries.
decls.statement:
theorem det_diagGL (t : Fin n → kˣ) :
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det (diagGL t) = ∏ i, t i

decls.name: TauCeti.diagGL_injective
decls.doc: The diagonal embedding is injective.
decls.statement: theorem diagGL_injective : Function.Injective (diagGL (k := k) (n := n))

decls.name: TauCeti.stdRep_diagGL_apply
decls.doc: The standard representation acts at `diagGL t` by coordinatewise multiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem stdRep_diagGL_apply (t : Fin n → kˣ) (v : Fin n → k) (i : Fin n) :
    stdRep k n (diagGL t) v i = (t i : k) * v i

decls.name: TauCeti.stdRep_diagGL_apply_basisFun
decls.doc: Every standard basis vector is an eigenvector for a diagonal matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem stdRep_diagGL_apply_basisFun (t : Fin n → kˣ) (i : Fin n) :
    stdRep k n (diagGL t) (Pi.basisFun k (Fin n) i) =
      (t i : k) • Pi.basisFun k (Fin n) i

decls.name: TauCeti.extPowerRep
decls.doc: The `d`th exterior power of the standard representation of `GL n k`.
decls.statement:
abbrev extPowerRep :
    Representation k (GL (Fin n) k) (⋀[k]^d (Fin n → k))

decls.name: TauCeti.extPowerFDRep
decls.doc: The exterior power of the standard representation, bundled as an object of `FDRep`.
decls.statement: abbrev extPowerFDRep : FDRep k (GL (Fin n) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.char_extPowerRep_diagonal
decls.doc:
The character of the `d`th exterior power on a diagonal matrix is the `d`th elementary
symmetric polynomial in its diagonal entries.
decls.statement:
theorem char_extPowerRep_diagonal (t : Fin n → kˣ) :
    (extPowerRep k n d).character (diagGL t) =
      MvPolynomial.eval (fun i => (t i : k)) (MvPolynomial.esymm (Fin n) k d)

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonalGroupToGL
decls.doc: The canonical inclusion of the orthogonal group into the general linear group.
decls.statement: def orthogonalGroupToGL : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) k →* GL (Fin n) k

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonalGroupToGL_coe
decls.doc: The orthogonal-to-general-linear inclusion has the original matrix as its underlying matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonalGroupToGL_coe (g : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) k) :
    (orthogonalGroupToGL k n g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k) = g

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonalGroupToGL_injective
decls.doc: The canonical inclusion of the orthogonal group into the general linear group is injective.
decls.statement: theorem orthogonalGroupToGL_injective : Function.Injective (orthogonalGroupToGL k n)

decls.name: TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep
decls.doc: The standard representation of the orthogonal group on column vectors.
decls.statement: def stdOrthogonalRep : Representation k (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) k) (Fin n → k)

decls.name: TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep_apply
decls.doc: The standard orthogonal action is multiplication by the underlying matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem stdOrthogonalRep_apply (g : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) k) :
    stdOrthogonalRep k n g = Matrix.mulVecLin (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep_apply_apply
decls.doc: Evaluation of the standard orthogonal action is matrix-vector multiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem stdOrthogonalRep_apply_apply (g : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) k) (v : Fin n → k) :
    stdOrthogonalRep k n g v = (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k) *ᵥ v

decls.name: TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep_dotProduct_stdOrthogonalRep

decls.name: TauCeti.commute_permTensorAction_tensorPowerRep
decls.doc:
The actions of `GL n k` and the symmetric group on the tensor power commute.

This is the commuting-actions half of Schur--Weyl duality, the first Layer 2 target of the
classical-groups roadmap; it makes no double-centralizer claim.
decls.statement:
theorem commute_permTensorAction_tensorPowerRep (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    Commute (permTensorAction k n d σ) (tensorPowerRep k n d g)

decls.name: TauCeti.commute_permTensorActionAlgHom_tensorPowerRep
decls.doc:
The whole group algebra `k[S_d]` commutes with the general-linear action on the tensor power,
so a Young symmetrizer cuts out a `GL n k`-subrepresentation.
decls.statement:
theorem commute_permTensorActionAlgHom_tensorPowerRep
    (a : MonoidAlgebra k (Equiv.Perm (Fin d))) (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    Commute (permTensorActionAlgHom k n d a) (tensorPowerRep k n d g)

decls.name: TauCeti.char_tensorPowerRep
decls.doc:
The character of the tensor power is the corresponding power of the standard character.

This is intentionally not a simp lemma: `Representation.char_tensorPower` and `char_stdRep`
already normalize its left-hand side, so registering this specialization would violate `simpNF`.
decls.statement:
theorem char_tensorPowerRep (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    (tensorPowerRep k n d).character g =
      Matrix.trace (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k) ^ d

decls.name: TauCeti.char_tensorPowerFDRep
decls.doc: The character of the bundled tensor power is the corresponding power of the matrix trace.
decls.statement:
theorem char_tensorPowerFDRep (g : GL (Fin n) k) :
    (tensorPowerFDRep k n d).character g =
      Matrix.trace (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k) ^ d

decls.name: TauCeti.detRowAlternating_stdSLRep
decls.doc:
The standard action of `SL(n, k)` preserves the standard-basis determinant form.

This is deliberately not a `simp` lemma: `stdSLRep_apply` already rewrites `stdSLRep k n g` to
`Matrix.mulVecLin ↑g`, so the left-hand side here is not in `simp` normal form and the rewrite
could never fire. Use `TauCeti.Matrix.detRowAlternating_mulVec` for the `simp`-normal statement.
decls.statement:
theorem detRowAlternating_stdSLRep (g : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) k)
    (v : Fin n → Fin n → k) :
    Matrix.detRowAlternating (fun i => stdSLRep k n g (v i)) =
      Matrix.detRowAlternating v

decls.name: TauCeti.haarAverage
decls.doc:
Averaging a continuous vector-valued function against normalized Haar measure, as a
continuous linear map.
decls.statement: def haarAverage [CompleteSpace V] : C(G, V) →L[𝕜] V

decls.name: TauCeti.haarAverage_apply
decls.doc:
The Haar average is the Bochner integral against normalized Haar measure.

Not a `simp` lemma: `haarAverage` is the normal form here, so that the constant, translation
and inversion lemmas below can be `simp` lemmas. Unfold explicitly with `rw`/`simp` when the
underlying integral is wanted.
decls.statement:
theorem haarAverage_apply [CompleteSpace V] (f : C(G, V)) :
    haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) f = ∫ g, f g ∂haarProb G

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_haarAverage_le_one
decls.doc: The operator norm of Haar averaging is at most one.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_haarAverage_le_one [CompleteSpace V] :
    ‖haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) (V := V)‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_haarAverage_apply_le
decls.doc: Haar averaging is norm-nonincreasing for the uniform norm on continuous maps.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_haarAverage_apply_le [CompleteSpace V] (f : C(G, V)) :
    ‖haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) f‖ ≤ ‖f‖

decls.name: TauCeti.haarAverage_const
decls.doc: The Haar average of a constant function is that constant.
decls.statement:
theorem haarAverage_const [CompleteSpace V] (v : V) :
    haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) (ContinuousMap.const G v) = v

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_haarAverage_eq_one
decls.doc: On a nonzero target, Haar averaging has operator norm one.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_haarAverage_eq_one [Nontrivial V] [CompleteSpace V] :
    ‖haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) (V := V)‖ = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.haarAverage_comp_mulLeft
decls.doc: Haar averaging is unchanged by left translation of the argument.
decls.statement:
theorem haarAverage_comp_mulLeft [CompleteSpace V] (f : C(G, V)) (g : G) :
    haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) (f.comp (ContinuousMap.mulLeft g)) =
      haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) f

decls.name: TauCeti.haarAverage_comp_mulRight
decls.doc: Haar averaging is unchanged by right translation of the argument.
decls.statement:
theorem haarAverage_comp_mulRight [CompleteSpace V] (f : C(G, V)) (g : G) :
    haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) (f.comp (ContinuousMap.mulRight g)) =
      haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) f

decls.name: TauCeti.haarAverage_comp_inv
decls.doc: Haar averaging is unchanged by inversion of the argument.
decls.statement:
theorem haarAverage_comp_inv [CompleteSpace V] (f : C(G, V)) :
    haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) (f.comp (Homeomorph.inv G : C(G, G))) =
      haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) f

decls.name: ContinuousLinearMap.haarAverage_comp_comm
decls.doc:
Continuous linear maps commute with Haar averaging.

The scalars are assumed to be `RCLike` because Mathlib states
`ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm` under that hypothesis.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.ContinuousLinearMap.haarAverage_comp_comm {W : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup W]
    [NormedSpace ℝ W] [NormedSpace 𝕜 W] [SMulCommClass ℝ 𝕜 W] [CompleteSpace V] [CompleteSpace W]
    (L : V →L[𝕜] W) (f : C(G, V)) :
    haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) ((L : C(V, W)).comp f) = L (haarAverage G (𝕜 := 𝕜) f)

decls.name: TauCeti.haar_univ_ne_zero
decls.doc: Haar measure of a nonempty locally compact group has nonzero total mass.
decls.statement: theorem haar_univ_ne_zero : (Measure.haar : Measure G) univ ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isMulRightInvariant_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure
decls.doc: Every probability Haar measure on a locally compact group is right-invariant.
decls.statement:
theorem isMulRightInvariant_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure (μ : Measure G)
    [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : μ.IsMulRightInvariant

decls.name: TauCeti.isInvInvariant_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure
decls.doc: Every probability Haar measure on a locally compact group is invariant under inversion.
decls.statement:
theorem isInvInvariant_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure (μ : Measure G)
    [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : μ.IsInvInvariant

decls.name: TauCeti.haar_univ_lt_top
decls.doc: Haar measure of a compact group has finite total mass.
decls.statement: theorem haar_univ_lt_top : (Measure.haar : Measure G) univ < ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.haarFinite
decls.statement: def haarFinite : FiniteMeasure G

decls.name: TauCeti.haarFinite_toMeasure
decls.doc: The finite measure used to normalize Haar measure has underlying measure `Measure.haar`.
decls.statement: theorem haarFinite_toMeasure : (haarFinite G : Measure G) = Measure.haar

decls.name: TauCeti.haarFinite_ne_zero
decls.statement: theorem haarFinite_ne_zero : haarFinite G ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.haarProb
decls.doc: Haar probability measure on a compact topological group.
decls.statement: def haarProb : Measure G

decls.name: TauCeti.haarProb_def
decls.doc: The definition of normalized Haar measure as a rescaling of Mathlib's Haar measure.
decls.statement:
theorem haarProb_def :
    haarProb G = ((Measure.haar : Measure G) univ)⁻¹ • Measure.haar

decls.name: TauCeti.isProbabilityMeasure_haarProb
decls.statement: instance isProbabilityMeasure_haarProb : IsProbabilityMeasure (haarProb G)

decls.name: TauCeti.haarProb_apply_univ
decls.doc:
Normalized Haar measure has total mass one.

Not a `simp` lemma: `simp` already closes this goal from the `IsProbabilityMeasure` instance
via `MeasureTheory.measure_univ`.
decls.statement: theorem haarProb_apply_univ : haarProb G univ = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.isMulLeftInvariant_haarProb
decls.statement: instance isMulLeftInvariant_haarProb : (haarProb G).IsMulLeftInvariant

decls.name: TauCeti.isHaarMeasure_haarProb
decls.statement: instance isHaarMeasure_haarProb : (haarProb G).IsHaarMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.isMulRightInvariant_haarProb
decls.doc: Normalized Haar measure is invariant under right multiplication.
decls.statement: instance isMulRightInvariant_haarProb : (haarProb G).IsMulRightInvariant

decls.name: TauCeti.isInvInvariant_haarProb
decls.doc: Normalized Haar measure is invariant under inversion.
decls.statement: instance isInvInvariant_haarProb : (haarProb G).IsInvInvariant

decls.name: TauCeti.eq_haarProb_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure
decls.doc: A probability Haar measure on a compact group is the normalized Haar measure.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_haarProb_of_isHaarMeasure_of_isProbabilityMeasure (μ : Measure G)
    [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : μ = haarProb G

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp
decls.doc:
The matrix coefficient `g ↦ ⟪π g v, w⟫` as an element of `L²(G)` for normalized Haar measure.

A matrix coefficient is continuous and `G` is compact, so `ContinuousMap.toLp` applies; the
normalization of Haar measure to a probability measure is what makes the resulting `L²` norms
comparable to the uniform norm without a measure-dependent constant.
decls.statement:
def matrixCoeffLp (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) (hπ : Continuous π)
    (v w : V) : Lp 𝕜 2 (haarProb G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_def
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_def (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w = ContinuousMap.toLp 2 (haarProb G) 𝕜 (matrixCoeff π hπ v w)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.coeFn_matrixCoeffLp
decls.doc:
A matrix coefficient in `L²` is represented, almost everywhere, by the function it comes
from.
decls.statement:
theorem coeFn_matrixCoeffLp (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w =ᵐ[haarProb G] fun g ↦ ⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_zero_left
decls.statement: theorem matrixCoeffLp_zero_left (w : V) : matrixCoeffLp π hπ 0 w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_zero_right
decls.statement: theorem matrixCoeffLp_zero_right (v : V) : matrixCoeffLp π hπ v 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_add_left
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_add_left (v₁ v₂ w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ (v₁ + v₂) w = matrixCoeffLp π hπ v₁ w + matrixCoeffLp π hπ v₂ w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_add_right
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_add_right (v w₁ w₂ : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ v (w₁ + w₂) = matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w₁ + matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w₂

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_smul_left
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_smul_left (c : 𝕜) (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ (c • v) w = (starRingEnd 𝕜) c • matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_smul_right
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_smul_right (v : V) (c : 𝕜) (w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ v (c • w) = c • matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLpₛₗ
decls.doc:
The `L²` matrix coefficients of a fixed representation, bundled as a sesquilinear map:
conjugate linear in the first vector, linear in the second, exactly as Mathlib's `innerₛₗ`.

This is `matrixCoeffₛₗ` postcomposed with the linear map `ContinuousMap.toLp`, so the
sesquilinearity is inherited rather than reproved; bundling supplies the remaining additive
identities (`map_neg`, `map_sub`, `map_sum`) through the `LinearMap` API.
decls.statement: def matrixCoeffLpₛₗ : V →ₗ⋆[𝕜] V →ₗ[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 (haarProb G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLpₛₗ_apply_apply
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLpₛₗ_apply_apply (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLpₛₗ π hπ v w = matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
A matrix coefficient vanishes in `L²` exactly when the continuous function it comes from is
the zero function: `ContinuousMap.toLp` is injective for a measure that is positive on nonempty
open sets, and normalized Haar measure is one.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_eq_zero_iff (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w = 0 ↔ matrixCoeff π hπ v w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_eq_zero_iff_forall
decls.doc: A matrix coefficient vanishes in `L²` exactly when it vanishes identically.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_eq_zero_iff_forall (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w = 0 ↔ ∀ g : G, ⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.inner_matrixCoeffLp
decls.doc:
The `L²` inner product of two matrix coefficients is the Haar integral of their pointwise
product. Mathlib's inner product is conjugate linear in its first argument and unfolds as
`⟪F, H⟫ = ∫ H · conj F`, which is where the conjugation sits below; this placement is what the
Schur orthogonality relations are stated against.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_matrixCoeffLp (ρ : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G W) (hρ : Continuous ρ) (v w : V)
    (v' w' : W) :
    ⟪matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w, matrixCoeffLp ρ hρ v' w'⟫_𝕜
      = ∫ g, ⟪ρ g v', w'⟫_𝕜 * (starRingEnd 𝕜) ⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜 ∂(haarProb G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.norm_matrixCoeffLp_sq
decls.doc: The squared `L²` norm of a matrix coefficient is the Haar integral of its squared modulus.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_matrixCoeffLp_sq (v w : V) :
    ‖matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w‖ ^ 2 = ∫ g, ‖⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜‖ ^ 2 ∂(haarProb G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.norm_matrixCoeffLp_le
decls.doc:
The `L²` norm of a matrix coefficient of a unitary representation is at most the product of the
norms of its defining vectors, with no constant: normalized Haar measure has total mass one, so
`ContinuousMap.toLp` is a contraction from the uniform norm, where `norm_matrixCoeff_le` is the
matching bound.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_matrixCoeffLp_le (hunitary : IsUnitary π) (v w : V) :
    ‖matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.norm_matrixCoeffLp_trivial
decls.doc:
The matrix coefficients of the trivial representation are constants, and normalized Haar
measure gives a constant its own norm. This is the sanity check that `matrixCoeffLp` carries the
probability normalization rather than an unnormalized one.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_matrixCoeffLp_trivial (v w : V) :
    ‖matrixCoeffLp (ContRepresentation.trivial 𝕜 G V) continuous_const v w‖ = ‖⟪v, w⟫_𝕜‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_subrepresentation
decls.doc:
A matrix coefficient of an invariant submodule is the matrix coefficient of the ambient
representation at the underlying vectors, so passing to a subrepresentation creates no new
elements of `L²(G)`.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffLp_subrepresentation {U : Submodule 𝕜 V} (hU : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ U, π g v ∈ U)
    (v w : U) :
    matrixCoeffLp (subrepresentation π U hU) (continuous_subrepresentation hπ) v w
      = matrixCoeffLp π hπ (v : V) (w : V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.exists_pos_mul_norm_le_norm_map
decls.doc:
The action operators of a continuous representation of a compact group are uniformly
bounded below: there is a `c > 0` with `c * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖π g v‖` for every `g` and `v`.

The bound comes from applying the inverse operator `π g⁻¹`, whose norm is bounded uniformly in `g`
because `G` is compact and `π` is continuous. Only the normed-space structure is involved, so this
is stated before the inner product enters.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_pos_mul_norm_le_norm_map (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) (hπ : Continuous π) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (g : G) (v : V), c * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖π g v‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.gramFamily
decls.doc:
The family `g ↦ (π g)† ∘ (π g)` of positive operators, as a continuous map on the group.

This is the integrand of the unitarian trick: its value at `g` is the Gram operator of the
pulled-back form `(v, w) ↦ ⟪π g v, π g w⟫`.
decls.statement: def gramFamily : C(G, V →L[𝕜] V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.gramOperator
decls.doc:
The Gram operator of the Haar-averaged inner product
`⟪v, w⟫_G = ∫ g, ⟪π g v, π g w⟫ ∂(haarProb G)` of a continuous representation of a compact group.

The averaged form is recorded through this operator rather than as a second
`InnerProductSpace` structure: Lean fixes one inner product on `V`, and it is the operator identity
`(π g)† ∘ gramOperator π hπ ∘ (π g) = gramOperator π hπ` that expresses `G`-invariance of the
averaged form.
decls.statement: def gramOperator : V →L[𝕜] V

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.inner_gramOperator
decls.doc: The defining property of the Gram operator: it represents the Haar-averaged inner product.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_gramOperator (v w : V) :
    ⟪v, gramOperator π hπ w⟫_𝕜 = ∫ g, ⟪π g v, π g w⟫_𝕜 ∂haarProb G

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.inner_gramOperator_left
decls.doc: The Gram operator represents the Haar-averaged inner product, written on the left.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_gramOperator_left (v w : V) :
    ⟪gramOperator π hπ v, w⟫_𝕜 = ∫ g, ⟪π g v, π g w⟫_𝕜 ∂haarProb G

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isSymmetric_gramOperator
decls.doc: The averaged form is Hermitian: the Gram operator is symmetric.
decls.statement: theorem isSymmetric_gramOperator : (gramOperator π hπ : V →ₗ[𝕜] V).IsSymmetric

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isSelfAdjoint_gramOperator
decls.doc: The Gram operator of the averaged form is self-adjoint.
decls.statement: theorem isSelfAdjoint_gramOperator : IsSelfAdjoint (gramOperator π hπ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.integrable_norm_sq
decls.doc:
Integrability of `g ↦ ‖π g v‖ ^ 2`: the integrand is continuous on a compact group carrying a
measure that is finite on compact sets.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_norm_sq (v : V) :
    Integrable (fun g ↦ ‖π g v‖ ^ 2) (haarProb G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.inner_gramOperator_self
decls.doc: The averaged form evaluated on the diagonal is the average of `‖π g v‖ ^ 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_gramOperator_self (v : V) :
    ⟪gramOperator π hπ v, v⟫_𝕜 = ((∫ g, ‖π g v‖ ^ 2 ∂haarProb G : ℝ) : 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isPositive_gramOperator
decls.doc: The Gram operator of the averaged form is a positive operator.
decls.statement: theorem isPositive_gramOperator : (gramOperator π hπ).IsPositive

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.re_inner_gramOperator_self_pos
decls.doc:
**Positive definiteness of the averaged form.** For a nonzero vector the averaged norm square
is strictly positive; this is what makes `⟪v, w⟫_G = ⟪gramOperator π hπ v, w⟫` an inner product
rather than merely a positive semidefinite form.
decls.title: Positive definiteness of the averaged form
decls.statement:
theorem re_inner_gramOperator_self_pos {v : V} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    0 < re ⟪gramOperator π hπ v, v⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.gramOperator_injective
decls.doc: The averaged form is nondegenerate, so the Gram operator is injective.
decls.statement: theorem gramOperator_injective : Function.Injective (gramOperator π hπ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.conjAction
decls.doc:
Conjugation `S ↦ (π g)† ∘ S ∘ (π g)` by an action operator, packaged as a continuous linear
map on operators.

Bundling it this way is what lets it commute with Haar averaging, via
`ContinuousLinearMap.haarAverage_comp_comm`.
decls.statement: def conjAction (g : G) : (V →L[𝕜] V) →L[𝕜] V →L[𝕜] V

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.conjAction_apply
decls.doc: `conjAction` is conjugation, unfolded.
decls.statement:
theorem conjAction_apply (g : G) (S : V →L[𝕜] V) :
    conjAction π g S = (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)).comp (S.comp (π g))

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.conjAction_comp_gramFamily
decls.doc:
Conjugating by `π g` translates the integrand of the unitarian trick on the right by `g`:
`(π g)† ∘ ((π h)† ∘ (π h)) ∘ (π g) = (π (h * g))† ∘ (π (h * g))`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjAction_comp_gramFamily (g : G) :
    (conjAction π g : C(V →L[𝕜] V, V →L[𝕜] V)).comp (gramFamily π hπ) =
      (gramFamily π hπ).comp (ContinuousMap.mulRight g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.adjoint_comp_gramOperator_comp
decls.doc:
**The operator form of `G`-invariance of the averaged form:** `(π g)† ∘ S ∘ (π g) = S`.

Conjugation by `π g` is a continuous linear map on operators, so it commutes with Haar averaging,
and on the integrand it is right translation by `g`, which the Haar average does not see.
decls.title: The operator form of `G`-invariance of the averaged form
decls.statement:
theorem adjoint_comp_gramOperator_comp (g : G) :
    (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)).comp ((gramOperator π hπ).comp (π g)) =
      gramOperator π hπ

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.inner_gramOperator_map_map
decls.doc:
**The averaged form is `G`-invariant.** This is the whole point of the unitarian trick: `π` is
unitary for `⟪v, w⟫_G = ⟪gramOperator π hπ v, w⟫`, even when it is not unitary for the inner
product `V` was given.
decls.title: The averaged form is `G`-invariant
decls.statement:
theorem inner_gramOperator_map_map (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪π g v, gramOperator π hπ (π g w)⟫_𝕜 = ⟪v, gramOperator π hπ w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitarizable
decls.doc:
**Weyl's unitarian trick.** Every continuous representation of a compact group on a Hilbert
space carries a `G`-invariant positive-definite Hermitian form, represented by a positive-definite
self-adjoint operator `S` with `(π g)† ∘ S ∘ (π g) = S`.

This operator is the input to unitarization: retopologizing `V` by `⟪S ·, ·⟫`, or conjugating `π`
by `S ^ (1 / 2)`, makes every `π g` unitary. Neither construction is carried out here, so this file
does not itself produce an `IsUnitary` representation.
decls.title: Weyl's unitarian trick
decls.statement:
theorem isUnitarizable :
    ∃ S : V →L[𝕜] V, IsSelfAdjoint S ∧ (∀ v : V, v ≠ 0 → 0 < re ⟪S v, v⟫_𝕜) ∧
      ∀ g : G, (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)).comp (S.comp (π g)) = S

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.gramOperator_eq_one
decls.doc:
Averaging a form that is already invariant changes nothing: the Gram operator of a unitary
representation is the identity.
decls.statement: theorem gramOperator_eq_one (hunitary : IsUnitary π) : gramOperator π hπ = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.apply_mem_orthogonal
decls.doc:
For a unitary representation of a group, the action carries the orthogonal complement of an
invariant subspace into itself.
decls.statement:
theorem apply_mem_orthogonal (hπ : IsUnitary π) (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) (g : G) {v : V}
    (hv : v ∈ Wᗮ) : π g v ∈ Wᗮ

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.orthogonal_mem_invtSubmodule
decls.doc:
**Invariant complements.** For a unitary representation of a group, the orthogonal complement
of an invariant submodule is again invariant.
decls.title: Invariant complements
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonal_mem_invtSubmodule (hπ : IsUnitary π)
    (hW : W ∈ π.toRepresentation.invtSubmodule) : Wᗮ ∈ π.toRepresentation.invtSubmodule

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.orthogonalSubrepresentation
decls.doc:
The orthogonal complement of a subrepresentation of a unitary representation, as a
subrepresentation.
decls.statement:
def orthogonalSubrepresentation (hπ : IsUnitary π) (σ : Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation) :
    Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.toSubmodule_orthogonalSubrepresentation
decls.statement:
theorem toSubmodule_orthogonalSubrepresentation (hπ : IsUnitary π)
    (σ : Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation) :
    (hπ.orthogonalSubrepresentation σ).toSubmodule = σ.toSubmoduleᗮ

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.starProjection_apply_comm
decls.doc:
The orthogonal projection onto an invariant subspace of a unitary representation commutes with
the action.
decls.statement:
theorem starProjection_apply_comm (hπ : IsUnitary π) (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) (g : G)
    (v : V) : W.starProjection (π g v) = π g (W.starProjection v)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.starProjectionIntertwiner
decls.doc:
The orthogonal projection onto an invariant subspace of a unitary representation, as a
continuous intertwining map.
decls.statement:
def starProjectionIntertwiner (hπ : IsUnitary π)
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) : ContIntertwiningMap π π

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.toContinuousLinearMap_starProjectionIntertwiner
decls.statement:
theorem toContinuousLinearMap_starProjectionIntertwiner (hπ : IsUnitary π)
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) :
    (hπ.starProjectionIntertwiner hW).toContinuousLinearMap = W.starProjection

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.starProjectionIntertwiner_apply
decls.statement:
theorem starProjectionIntertwiner_apply (hπ : IsUnitary π) (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) (v : V) :
    hπ.starProjectionIntertwiner hW v = W.starProjection v

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.isCompl_orthogonalSubrepresentation
decls.doc:
A subrepresentation of a unitary representation is complemented by its orthogonal complement,
as soon as it admits an orthogonal projection.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompl_orthogonalSubrepresentation (hπ : IsUnitary π)
    (σ : Subrepresentation π.toRepresentation) [σ.toSubmodule.HasOrthogonalProjection] :
    IsCompl σ (hπ.orthogonalSubrepresentation σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.isSemisimpleRepresentation
decls.doc:
**Complete reducibility.** A finite-dimensional unitary continuous representation of a group is
semisimple: every subrepresentation has a complement.
decls.title: Complete reducibility
decls.statement:
theorem isSemisimpleRepresentation (hπ : IsUnitary π) :
    Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation π.toRepresentation

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.isSemisimpleModule_asModule
decls.doc:
**Complete reducibility, algebraic form.** The group-algebra module of a finite-dimensional
unitary continuous representation of a group is semisimple.
decls.title: Complete reducibility, algebraic form
decls.statement:
theorem isSemisimpleModule_asModule (hπ : IsUnitary π) :
    IsSemisimpleModule (MonoidAlgebra 𝕜 G) π.toRepresentation.asModule

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff
decls.doc:
The matrix coefficient `g ↦ ⟪π g v, w⟫` of a representation with continuous
operator-valued action.
decls.statement:
def matrixCoeff (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) (hπ : Continuous π)
    (v w : V) : C(G, 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_apply
decls.doc: Evaluation of a matrix coefficient.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_apply (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) (hπ : Continuous π)
    (v w : V) (g : G) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v w g = ⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_apply_one
decls.doc: A matrix coefficient at the identity is the inner product of its defining vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_apply_one (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) (hπ : Continuous π)
    (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v w 1 = ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_zero_left
decls.statement: theorem matrixCoeff_zero_left (w : V) : matrixCoeff π hπ 0 w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_zero_right
decls.statement: theorem matrixCoeff_zero_right (v : V) : matrixCoeff π hπ v 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_add_left
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_add_left (v₁ v₂ w : V) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ (v₁ + v₂) w = matrixCoeff π hπ v₁ w + matrixCoeff π hπ v₂ w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_add_right
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_add_right (v w₁ w₂ : V) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v (w₁ + w₂) = matrixCoeff π hπ v w₁ + matrixCoeff π hπ v w₂

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_smul_left
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_smul_left (c : 𝕜) (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ (c • v) w = (starRingEnd 𝕜) c • matrixCoeff π hπ v w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_smul_right
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_smul_right (v : V) (c : 𝕜) (w : V) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v (c • w) = c • matrixCoeff π hπ v w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffₛₗ
decls.doc:
The matrix coefficients of a fixed representation, bundled as a sesquilinear map: conjugate
linear in the first vector, linear in the second, exactly as Mathlib's `innerₛₗ`.

Bundling records the sesquilinearity in the form the span of the matrix coefficients is built from,
and supplies the remaining additive identities (`map_neg`, `map_sub`, `map_sum`) through the
`LinearMap` API.
decls.statement: def matrixCoeffₛₗ : V →ₗ⋆[𝕜] V →ₗ[𝕜] C(G, 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffₛₗ_apply_apply
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeffₛₗ_apply_apply (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeffₛₗ π hπ v w = matrixCoeff π hπ v w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_apply_mul_right
decls.doc:
Translating the argument of a matrix coefficient on the right moves the action onto the first
vector. The pointwise statement needs no continuity of the multiplication of `G`.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_apply_mul_right (v w : V) (g g₀ : G) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v w (g * g₀) = matrixCoeff π hπ (π g₀ v) w g

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_apply_mul_eq_sum
decls.doc:
Matrix coefficients multiply like matrices: expanding the intermediate vector `π h v` in an
orthonormal basis writes the coefficient at a product as a sum of products of coefficients. In the
basis notation `π_{ij}(g) = ⟪π g eⱼ, eᵢ⟫` this is `π_{ik}(g * h) = ∑ j, π_{ij}(g) · π_{jk}(h)`.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_apply_mul_eq_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (e : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 V)
    (v w : V) (g h : G) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v w (g * h) =
      ∑ i, matrixCoeff π hπ (e i) w g * matrixCoeff π hπ v (e i) h

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_trivial
decls.doc:
A matrix coefficient of the trivial representation is the constant function at the inner
product of its defining vectors; the trivial action is constant, so `continuous_const` is its
continuity witness. Which constants arise depends on `V`: they are the values of the inner product,
so all of `𝕜` when some `⟪v, w⟫ ≠ 0`, and only `0` when `V` is trivial.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_trivial (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeff (ContRepresentation.trivial 𝕜 G V) continuous_const v w =
      ContinuousMap.const G ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_subrepresentation
decls.doc:
A matrix coefficient of an invariant submodule is the matrix coefficient of the ambient
representation at the underlying vectors, so passing to a subrepresentation creates no new
matrix coefficients; `continuous_subrepresentation hπ` is the continuity witness of the restricted
action.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_subrepresentation {W : Submodule 𝕜 V} (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W)
    (v w : W) :
    matrixCoeff (subrepresentation π W hW) (continuous_subrepresentation hπ) v w =
      matrixCoeff π hπ (v : V) (w : V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_restrict
decls.doc:
Restricting a representation along a continuous homomorphism precomposes its matrix
coefficients; the restricted action is `π ∘ φ`, so `hπ.comp hφ` is its continuity witness.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_restrict {H : Type*} [Monoid H] [TopologicalSpace H] (φ : H →* G)
    (hφ : Continuous φ) (v w : V) :
    matrixCoeff (π.restrict φ) (hπ.comp hφ) v w = (matrixCoeff π hπ v w).comp ⟨φ, hφ⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_comp_mulRight
decls.doc:
The right translate of a matrix coefficient of `π` is again a matrix coefficient of `π`: the
translation is absorbed into the first vector.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_comp_mulRight (v w : V) (g₀ : G) :
    (matrixCoeff π hπ v w).comp (ContinuousMap.mulRight g₀) = matrixCoeff π hπ (π g₀ v) w

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_apply_mul_left
decls.doc:
Translating the argument of a matrix coefficient of a unitary representation on the left moves
the action of the inverse onto the second vector.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_apply_mul_left (hπ : Continuous π) (hunitary : IsUnitary π) (v w : V)
    (g₀ g : G) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v w (g₀ * g) = matrixCoeff π hπ v (π g₀⁻¹ w) g

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_apply_inv
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_apply_inv (hπ : Continuous π) (hunitary : IsUnitary π) (v w : V) (g : G) :
    matrixCoeff π hπ v w g⁻¹ = (starRingEnd 𝕜) (matrixCoeff π hπ w v g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.matrixCoeff_comp_mulLeft
decls.doc:
The left translate of a matrix coefficient of a unitary representation is again a matrix
coefficient: the translation is absorbed into the second vector.
decls.statement:
theorem matrixCoeff_comp_mulLeft [SeparatelyContinuousMul G] (hπ : Continuous π)
    (hunitary : IsUnitary π) (v w : V) (g₀ : G) :
    (matrixCoeff π hπ v w).comp (ContinuousMap.mulLeft g₀) = matrixCoeff π hπ v (π g₀⁻¹ w)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.star_matrixCoeff
decls.doc:
The conjugate of a matrix coefficient of a unitary representation is the matrix coefficient
with its vectors swapped, precomposed with inversion. So the span of the matrix coefficients of a
unitary representation is stable under the star operation of `C(G, 𝕜)` followed by inversion of the
argument.
decls.statement:
theorem star_matrixCoeff [ContinuousInv G] (hπ : Continuous π) (hunitary : IsUnitary π)
    (v w : V) :
    star (matrixCoeff π hπ v w) =
      (matrixCoeff π hπ w v).comp ⟨Inv.inv, continuous_inv⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.norm_matrixCoeff_le
decls.doc:
The uniform norm of a matrix coefficient of a unitary representation is at most the product
of the norms of its defining vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_matrixCoeff_le (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) (hπ : Continuous π)
    (hunitary : IsUnitary π) (v w : V) :
    ‖matrixCoeff π hπ v w‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.subrepresentation
decls.doc:
The restriction of a continuous representation to an invariant submodule. This is the
continuous counterpart of `Representation.subrepresentation`.
decls.statement:
def subrepresentation (π : ContRepresentation R G V) (W : Submodule R V)
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) : ContRepresentation R G W

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.coe_subrepresentation_apply
decls.doc: The restricted action is the ambient action, read on the underlying vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_subrepresentation_apply (g : G) (v : W) :
    ((subrepresentation π W hW g v : W) : V) = π g (v : V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.toRepresentation_subrepresentation
decls.doc:
The underlying representation of a restricted continuous representation is the restriction of
the underlying representation.
decls.statement:
theorem toRepresentation_subrepresentation :
