    (subrepresentation π W hW).toRepresentation
      = π.toRepresentation.subrepresentation W fun g _ hv => hW g _ hv

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.continuous_subrepresentation
decls.doc:
Restricting a continuous representation to an invariant submodule preserves continuity: from
continuity of `g ↦ π g` as a map into the continuous linear endomorphisms of `V`, the restricted
action `g ↦ subrepresentation π W hW g` is continuous into those of `W`. This supplies the
continuity argument that `matrixCoeff` and the rest of the continuous-representation API take
explicitly, so a subrepresentation can be used wherever a continuous representation is expected.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_subrepresentation (hπ : Continuous π) :
    Continuous (subrepresentation π W hW)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.self_inv_apply
decls.doc:
Applying a continuous group representation at an element and then at its inverse cancels.

This restates `Representation.self_inv_apply` for the continuous action coercion, which `simp` does
not otherwise reach; it is an implementation detail of the inverse-transfer proofs below.
decls.statement:
theorem self_inv_apply (π : ContRepresentation R G V) (g : G) (v : V) :
    π g (π g⁻¹ v) = v

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary
decls.doc:
A continuous representation is unitary when every action operator preserves the inner
product.
decls.statement: def IsUnitary (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitary_iff_norm_map
decls.doc: A representation is unitary exactly when every action map preserves norms.
decls.statement:
theorem isUnitary_iff_norm_map (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
    IsUnitary π ↔ ∀ g v, ‖π g v‖ = ‖v‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitary_iff_isometry
decls.doc: A representation is unitary exactly when every action map is an isometry.
decls.statement:
theorem isUnitary_iff_isometry (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
    IsUnitary π ↔ ∀ g, Isometry (π g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.inner_map_map
decls.doc: A unitary representation preserves the inner product.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_map_map (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪π g v, π g w⟫_𝕜 = ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.norm_map
decls.doc: Every action map of a unitary representation preserves norms.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_map (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v : V) :
    ‖π g v‖ = ‖v‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.isometry
decls.doc: Every action map of a unitary representation is an isometry.
decls.statement: theorem isometry (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) : Isometry (π g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.injective
decls.doc: Every action map of a unitary representation is injective.
decls.statement: theorem injective (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) : Function.Injective (π g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.restrict
decls.doc: Restriction along a monoid homomorphism preserves unitarity.
decls.statement:
theorem restrict {H : Type*} [Monoid H] (hπ : IsUnitary π) (φ : H →* G) :
    IsUnitary (π.restrict φ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.subrepresentation
decls.doc: The restriction of a unitary representation to an invariant submodule is unitary.
decls.statement:
theorem subrepresentation (hπ : IsUnitary π) {W : Submodule 𝕜 V}
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, π g v ∈ W) : IsUnitary (subrepresentation π W hW)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.norm_inner_map_le
decls.doc:
A matrix coefficient of a unitary representation is bounded by the product of the vector
norms.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_inner_map_le (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ‖⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.adjoint_comp_self
decls.doc: The adjoint of a unitary action operator is a left inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem adjoint_comp_self (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)).comp (π g) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitary_trivial
decls.doc: The trivial continuous representation is unitary.
decls.statement:
theorem isUnitary_trivial :
    IsUnitary (ContRepresentation.trivial 𝕜 G V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitary_iff_mem_unitary
decls.doc:
For a group representation, inner-product preservation is equivalent to every action operator
belonging to Mathlib's unitary submonoid.
decls.statement:
theorem isUnitary_iff_mem_unitary (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
    IsUnitary π ↔ ∀ g, π g ∈ unitary (V →L[𝕜] V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.mem_unitary
decls.doc:
Every action operator of a unitary group representation belongs to Mathlib's `unitary`
submonoid.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_unitary (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    π g ∈ unitary (V →L[𝕜] V)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.self_comp_adjoint
decls.doc: The adjoint of a unitary action operator is a right inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem self_comp_adjoint (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    (π g).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.inner_map_left
decls.doc:
Moving a unitary action from the first inner-product argument to the second replaces the group
element by its inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_map_left (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪π g v, w⟫_𝕜 = ⟪v, π g⁻¹ w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.inner_map_right
decls.doc:
Moving a unitary action from the second inner-product argument to the first replaces the group
element by its inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem inner_map_right (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) (v w : V) :
    ⟪v, π g w⟫_𝕜 = ⟪π g⁻¹ v, w⟫_𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.adjoint_eq_inv
decls.doc: The adjoint of a unitary action operator is the action of the inverse group element.
decls.statement:
theorem adjoint_eq_inv (hπ : IsUnitary π) (g : G) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (π g) = π g⁻¹

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPower
decls.doc: The action induced by a representation on its `d`th exterior power.
decls.statement:
def exteriorPower (ρ : Representation R G M) (d : ℕ) :
    Representation R G (⋀[R]^d M)

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPower_apply
decls.doc: The action on an exterior power is induced by the action on the original representation.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_apply (ρ : Representation R G M) (d : ℕ) (g : G) :
    ρ.exteriorPower d g = _root_.exteriorPower.map d (ρ g)

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPower_apply_ιMulti
decls.doc:
The exterior-power action applies the original action to every factor of a pure wedge.

This is intentionally not a simp lemma: `exteriorPower_apply` followed by Mathlib's
`exteriorPower.map_apply_ιMulti` already performs this simplification.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_apply_ιMulti (ρ : Representation R G M) (d : ℕ) (g : G) (m : Fin d → M) :
    ρ.exteriorPower d g (_root_.exteriorPower.ιMulti R d m) =
      _root_.exteriorPower.ιMulti R d (ρ g ∘ m)

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPowerZeroEquiv
decls.doc: The zeroth exterior power is equivalent to the trivial representation on the scalars.
decls.statement:
def exteriorPowerZeroEquiv (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    (ρ.exteriorPower 0).Equiv (trivial R G R)

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPowerZeroEquiv_toLinearEquiv
decls.doc:
The underlying linear equivalence is Mathlib's identification of the zeroth exterior power
with the scalars.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPowerZeroEquiv_toLinearEquiv (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    ρ.exteriorPowerZeroEquiv.toLinearEquiv = _root_.exteriorPower.zeroEquiv R M

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPowerOneEquiv
decls.doc: The first exterior power is equivalent to the original representation.
decls.statement:
def exteriorPowerOneEquiv (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    (ρ.exteriorPower 1).Equiv ρ

decls.name: Representation.exteriorPowerOneEquiv_toLinearEquiv
decls.doc:
The underlying linear equivalence is Mathlib's identification of the first exterior power
with the module itself.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPowerOneEquiv_toLinearEquiv (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    ρ.exteriorPowerOneEquiv.toLinearEquiv = _root_.exteriorPower.oneEquiv R M

decls.name: Representation.IntertwiningMap.exteriorPower
decls.doc: An intertwining map induces an intertwining map on every exterior power.
decls.statement:
def exteriorPower (f : IntertwiningMap ρ σ) (d : ℕ) :
    IntertwiningMap (ρ.exteriorPower d) (σ.exteriorPower d)

decls.name: Representation.IntertwiningMap.exteriorPower_toLinearMap
decls.doc: The underlying linear map is the usual map induced on exterior powers.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_toLinearMap (f : IntertwiningMap ρ σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (f.exteriorPower d).toLinearMap = _root_.exteriorPower.map d f.toLinearMap

decls.name: Representation.IntertwiningMap.exteriorPower_apply_ιMulti
decls.doc: The induced map sends a pure wedge to the wedge of the images of its factors.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_apply_ιMulti (f : IntertwiningMap ρ σ) (d : ℕ) (m : Fin d → M) :
    f.exteriorPower d (_root_.exteriorPower.ιMulti R d m) =
      _root_.exteriorPower.ιMulti R d (f ∘ m)

decls.name: Representation.IntertwiningMap.exteriorPower_id
decls.doc: Exterior powers preserve identity intertwining maps.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_id (d : ℕ) :
    (IntertwiningMap.id ρ).exteriorPower d = IntertwiningMap.id (ρ.exteriorPower d)

decls.name: Representation.IntertwiningMap.exteriorPower_comp
decls.doc: Exterior powers preserve composition of intertwining maps.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_comp {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    {τ : Representation R G P} (f : IntertwiningMap ρ σ) (g : IntertwiningMap σ τ) (d : ℕ) :
    (g.comp f).exteriorPower d = (g.exteriorPower d).comp (f.exteriorPower d)

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPowerLinearEquiv
decls.doc:
The linear equivalence induced on `d`th exterior powers by an equivalence of representations.

This is built from the explicit inverse `exteriorPower.map d e.symm.toLinearMap` rather than from
bijectivity of `exteriorPower.map d e.toLinearMap`, so that the inverse is *definitionally* the
map induced by `e.symm`; that is what makes `exteriorPowerLinearEquiv_symm_toLinearMap`, and hence
`exteriorPower_symm`, hold. Mathlib builds `TensorProduct.congr` the same way.
decls.statement:
def exteriorPowerLinearEquiv (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (⋀[R]^d M) ≃ₗ[R] (⋀[R]^d N)

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPowerLinearEquiv_toLinearMap
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPowerLinearEquiv_toLinearMap (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (exteriorPowerLinearEquiv e d).toLinearMap =
      _root_.exteriorPower.map d e.toLinearMap

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPowerLinearEquiv_symm_toLinearMap
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPowerLinearEquiv_symm_toLinearMap (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (exteriorPowerLinearEquiv e d).symm.toLinearMap =
      _root_.exteriorPower.map d e.symm.toLinearMap

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower
decls.doc: An equivalence of representations induces an equivalence of every exterior power.
decls.statement:
def exteriorPower (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (ρ.exteriorPower d).Equiv (σ.exteriorPower d)

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower_toLinearEquiv
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_toLinearEquiv (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (e.exteriorPower d).toLinearEquiv = exteriorPowerLinearEquiv e d

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower_toLinearMap
decls.doc: The underlying linear map is the usual map induced on exterior powers.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_toLinearMap (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    (e.exteriorPower d).toLinearMap = _root_.exteriorPower.map d e.toLinearMap

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower_apply_ιMulti
decls.doc: The induced equivalence sends a pure wedge to the wedge of the images of its factors.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_apply_ιMulti (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) (m : Fin d → M) :
    e.exteriorPower d (_root_.exteriorPower.ιMulti R d m) =
      _root_.exteriorPower.ιMulti R d (e ∘ m)

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower_refl
decls.doc: Exterior powers preserve identity equivalences.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_refl (d : ℕ) :
    (Equiv.refl ρ).exteriorPower d = .refl (ρ.exteriorPower d)

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower_symm
decls.doc: Exterior powers preserve inverses of equivalences.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_symm (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (d : ℕ) :
    e.symm.exteriorPower d = (e.exteriorPower d).symm

decls.name: Representation.Equiv.exteriorPower_trans
decls.doc: Exterior powers preserve composition of equivalences.
decls.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_trans {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    {τ : Representation R G P} (e : ρ.Equiv σ) (f : σ.Equiv τ) (d : ℕ) :
    (e.trans f).exteriorPower d = (e.exteriorPower d).trans (f.exteriorPower d)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.RightCosets
decls.statement: abbrev RightCosets (S : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.quotientRightRelEquivQuotientLeftRel_mk
decls.doc:
The right-to-left-coset equivalence sends the right coset of `x` to the left coset of
`x⁻¹`. Mathlib does not currently expose a computation lemma for this equivalence, so keep
the necessary unfolding of its `Quotient.map'` implementation isolated here.
decls.statement:
theorem quotientRightRelEquivQuotientLeftRel_mk (S : Subgroup G) (x : G) :
    QuotientGroup.quotientRightRelEquivQuotientLeftRel S (Quotient.mk'' x) =
      QuotientGroup.mk x⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.inducedCharacterTerm
decls.doc: The contribution of a group element to the induced-character sum at a representative `x`.
decls.statement:
def inducedCharacterTerm {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (ρ : Representation k S V) (g x : G) : k

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.inducedCharacterTerm_mul
decls.doc:
The induced-character summand is unchanged on replacing a representative by another
representative of the same left coset.
decls.statement:
theorem inducedCharacterTerm_mul {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (ρ : Representation k S V) (g x : G) (s : S) :
    inducedCharacterTerm ρ g (x * s) = inducedCharacterTerm ρ g x

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.inducedCharacterTerm_eq_of_mk_eq
decls.doc: The induced-character summand depends only on the left coset of its representative.
decls.statement:
theorem inducedCharacterTerm_eq_of_mk_eq {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    (ρ : Representation k S V) (g x y : G)
    (hxy : (QuotientGroup.mk x : G ⧸ S) = QuotientGroup.mk y) :
    inducedCharacterTerm ρ g x = inducedCharacterTerm ρ g y

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.trace_ind_eq_sum_rightCosets
decls.doc: The trace of the induced action, computed on the right-coset model.
decls.statement:
theorem trace_ind_eq_sum_rightCosets [S.FiniteIndex] [Fintype (RightCosets S)]
    (A : Rep.{u} k S)
    [FiniteDimensional k A] (g : G) :
    LinearMap.trace k (Rep.ind S.subtype A) ((Rep.ind S.subtype A).ρ g) =
      ∑ q : RightCosets S,
        if Quotient.mk'' (q.out * g) = q then
          LinearMap.trace k A (A.ρ (rightCosetFactor (S := S) (q.out * g)))
        else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.trace_ind_eq_sum_terms
decls.doc:
The trace computation expressed as the standard character summand, still indexed by right
cosets.
decls.statement:
theorem trace_ind_eq_sum_terms [S.FiniteIndex] [Fintype (RightCosets S)]
    (A : Rep.{u} k S) [FiniteDimensional k A] (g : G) :
    LinearMap.trace k (Rep.ind S.subtype A) ((Rep.ind S.subtype A).ρ g) =
      ∑ q : RightCosets S, inducedCharacterTerm A.ρ g q.out⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.instFiniteDimensionalVObjFDRepRepForget₂HomSubtypeFGModuleCatLinearMapIdCarrierObjModuleCatIsFGVIntertwiningMapρ_tauCeti
decls.doc:
Forgetting finite-dimensionality keeps the same underlying module, so it keeps the
`FiniteDimensional` instance.
decls.statement: instance : FiniteDimensional k ((forget₂ (FDRep k G) (Rep k G)).obj A)

decls.name: TauCeti.character_forget₂
decls.doc: The forgetful functor `FDRep k G ⥤ Rep k G` preserves characters.
decls.statement:
theorem character_forget₂ (g : G) :
    ((forget₂ (FDRep k G) (Rep k G)).obj A).ρ.character g = A.character g

decls.name: TauCeti.character_indFDRep_sum_quotient
decls.doc:
The induced character at `g` is the sum of the original character over those left coset
representatives `t` for which `t⁻¹ g t` belongs to the subgroup.
decls.statement:
theorem character_indFDRep_sum_quotient {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G]
    {S : Subgroup G} [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) (g : G) :
    (indFDRep (k := k) (G := G) A).character g =
      letI

decls.name: TauCeti.character_ind
decls.doc:
The induced character at `g`, written as an average over the whole group. The subgroup
order must be invertible in the coefficient field; without this hypothesis,
`character_indFDRep_sum_quotient` is the division-free formula to use.
decls.statement:
theorem character_ind {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [Fintype G] (hS : IsUnit (Nat.card S : k)) (A : FDRep k S) (g : G) :
    (indFDRep (k := k) (G := G) A).character g =
      (Nat.card S : k)⁻¹ * ∑ x : G,
        if h : x⁻¹ * g * x ∈ S then A.character ⟨x⁻¹ * g * x, h⟩ else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_conj_smul
decls.doc: Membership in `sHs⁻¹`, expressed using the conjugation convention used by `conjRep`.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_conj_smul (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) (x : G) :
    x ∈ (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G) ↔ s⁻¹ * x * s ∈ H

decls.name: TauCeti.conjSubgroupEquiv
decls.doc: The canonical multiplicative equivalence `sHs⁻¹ ≃* H`, given by `x ↦ s⁻¹xs`.
decls.statement:
def conjSubgroupEquiv (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G) ≃* H

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_conjSubgroupEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_conjSubgroupEquiv_apply (s : G) (H : Subgroup G)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    (conjSubgroupEquiv s H x : G) = s⁻¹ * (x : G) * s

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_conjSubgroupEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_conjSubgroupEquiv_symm_apply (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) (x : H) :
    ((conjSubgroupEquiv s H).symm x : G) = s * (x : G) * s⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepFunctor
decls.doc:
Conjugating representations by `s` is restriction along the isomorphism
`sHs⁻¹ ≃* H`.
decls.statement:
def conjRepFunctor [Semiring k] (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    Rep k H ⥤ Rep k (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep
decls.doc: The conjugate representation `{}^s A` of `sHs⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
def conjRep [Semiring k] (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H) :
    Rep k (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep_V
decls.doc: Conjugation preserves the underlying module of a representation.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRep_V [Semiring k] (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H) :
    (conjRep s A).V = A.V

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepFunctor_map_hom_toLinearMap
decls.doc: Conjugation preserves the underlying linear map of a representation morphism.

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep_ρ
decls.doc:
The conjugate action, as a heterogeneous equality: `conjRep` is opaque, so
`(conjRep s A).V` and `A.V` are equal only via `conjRep_V`, not definitionally.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRep_ρ [Semiring k] (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    HEq ((conjRep s A).ρ x) (A.ρ (conjSubgroupEquiv s H x))

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep_ρ_apply
decls.doc: The conjugate action on elements, transported along `conjRep_V`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRep_ρ_apply [Semiring k] (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) (v : A.V) :
    cast (conjRep_V s A) ((conjRep s A).ρ x (cast (conjRep_V s A).symm v)) =
      A.ρ (conjSubgroupEquiv s H x) v

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep_ρ_mk
decls.doc: The action of the conjugate representation, written directly in the ambient group.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRep_ρ_mk [Semiring k] (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    HEq ((conjRep s A).ρ x)
      (A.ρ ⟨s⁻¹ * (x : G) * s, (mem_conj_smul s H x).mp x.2⟩)

decls.name: TauCeti.conj_one_smul
decls.doc: Conjugating a subgroup by `1` leaves it unchanged.
decls.statement: theorem conj_one_smul (H : Subgroup G) : MulAut.conj (1 : G) • H = H

decls.name: TauCeti.conj_mul_smul
decls.doc: Conjugating a subgroup by `s * t` is conjugating by `t` and then by `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem conj_mul_smul (s t : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    MulAut.conj (s * t) • H = MulAut.conj s • (MulAut.conj t • H)

decls.name: TauCeti.conj_inv_smul_smul
decls.doc: Conjugating a subgroup by `s⁻¹` undoes conjugating it by `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem conj_inv_smul_smul (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    MulAut.conj s⁻¹ • (MulAut.conj s • H) = H

decls.name: TauCeti.conjSubgroupEquiv_one
decls.doc:
The transported form of `conjSubgroupEquiv 1`: conjugating by `1` is the identification of
`1 · H · 1⁻¹` with `H`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjSubgroupEquiv_one (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjSubgroupEquiv (1 : G) H).toMonoidHom =
      (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_one_smul H)).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjSubgroupEquiv_inv_comp_subgroupCongr
decls.doc:
Conjugating by `s⁻¹`, after identifying `H` with `s⁻¹(sHs⁻¹)s`, is the identification
`H →* sHs⁻¹` inverse to the one `{}^s` restricts along.  This is what makes the inverse of the
conjugation equivalence conjugation by `s⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjSubgroupEquiv_inv_comp_subgroupCongr (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjSubgroupEquiv s⁻¹ (MulAut.conj s • H)).toMonoidHom.comp
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_inv_smul_smul s H).symm).toMonoidHom =
      (conjSubgroupEquiv s H).symm.toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjSubgroupEquiv_mul
decls.doc:
The homomorphism `(st)H(st)⁻¹ →* H` underlying `{}^{st}` is the one underlying `{}^t`
composed with the one underlying `{}^s`, after identifying `(st)H(st)⁻¹` with `s(tHt⁻¹)s⁻¹`.
This is the sole computation behind the coherence statements below: `(st)⁻¹ x (st) = t⁻¹(s⁻¹ x s)t`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjSubgroupEquiv_mul (s t : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjSubgroupEquiv (s * t) H).toMonoidHom =
      ((conjSubgroupEquiv t H).toMonoidHom.comp
          (conjSubgroupEquiv s (MulAut.conj t • H)).toMonoidHom).comp
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_mul_smul s t H)).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepFunctor_one
decls.doc:
Conjugating by `1` does nothing, once `1 · H · 1⁻¹` is identified with `H`: an equality of
functors, of which `conjRep_one` is the evaluation at a representation.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRepFunctor_one (H : Subgroup G) :
    conjRepFunctor (k := k) (1 : G) H =
      Rep.resFunctor (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_one_smul H)).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepFunctor_mul
decls.doc:
**Cocycle coherence for conjugation**, at the level of functors: `{}^{st}(-) = {}^s({}^t(-))`,
once `(st)H(st)⁻¹` is identified with `s(tHt⁻¹)s⁻¹`.  Being an equality of functors this also
pins down the behaviour on morphisms, which the evaluation `conjRep_mul` does not see.

Together with `conjRepFunctor_one` this is what makes `s ↦ {}^s(-)` an action of `G`; both Mackey
theory (where a double-coset representative may be replaced by another) and Clifford theory
consume it.
decls.title: Cocycle coherence for conjugation
decls.statement:
theorem conjRepFunctor_mul (s t : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    conjRepFunctor (k := k) (s * t) H =
      conjRepFunctor t H ⋙ conjRepFunctor s (MulAut.conj t • H) ⋙
        Rep.resFunctor (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_mul_smul s t H)).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep_one
decls.doc: Conjugating by `1` does nothing, once `1 · H · 1⁻¹` is identified with `H`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRep_one {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H) :
    conjRep (1 : G) A =
      Rep.res (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_one_smul H)).toMonoidHom A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRep_mul
decls.doc:
**Cocycle coherence for conjugation**: `{}^{st} A = {}^s({}^t A)`, once `(st)H(st)⁻¹` is
identified with `s(tHt⁻¹)s⁻¹`.  The evaluation of `conjRepFunctor_mul` at `A`.
decls.title: Cocycle coherence for conjugation
decls.statement:
theorem conjRep_mul (s t : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : Rep k H) :
    conjRep (s * t) A =
      Rep.res (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_mul_smul s t H)).toMonoidHom
        (conjRep s (conjRep t A))

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepEquiv
decls.doc:
**Conjugation is an equivalence of categories** `Rep k H ≌ Rep k (sHs⁻¹)`: it is restriction
along the isomorphism `conjSubgroupEquiv s H`, and `resFunctorEquiv` makes any such restriction an
equivalence.  Its inverse is conjugation by `s⁻¹`, read through `s⁻¹(sHs⁻¹)s = H`
(`conjRepEquiv_inverse_eq_conjRepFunctor`).

`conjNormalRepEquiv` is the normal-subgroup form, where source and target coincide, so that the
equivalence is an autoequivalence and the coherence below becomes an action.
decls.title: Conjugation is an equivalence of categories
decls.statement:
def conjRepEquiv (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    Rep k H ≌ Rep k (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepEquiv_functor
decls.statement:
theorem conjRepEquiv_functor (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjRepEquiv (k := k) s H).functor = conjRepFunctor s H

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepEquiv_inverse
decls.statement:
theorem conjRepEquiv_inverse (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjRepEquiv (k := k) s H).inverse =
      Rep.resFunctor (conjSubgroupEquiv s H).symm.toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjRepEquiv_inverse_eq_conjRepFunctor
decls.doc:
The inverse of the conjugation equivalence is conjugation by `s⁻¹`, once `s⁻¹(sHs⁻¹)s` is
identified with `H`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjRepEquiv_inverse_eq_conjRepFunctor (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjRepEquiv (k := k) s H).inverse =
      conjRepFunctor s⁻¹ (MulAut.conj s • H) ⋙
        Rep.resFunctor (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_inv_smul_smul s H).symm).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepFunctor
decls.doc:
Conjugating finite-dimensional representations by `s` is restriction along the isomorphism
`sHs⁻¹ ≃* H`.  The `FDRep` mirror of `conjRepFunctor`: `FDRep k H` is by definition
`Action (FGModuleCat k) H`, so the restriction functor is Mathlib's `Action.res`.
decls.statement:
def conjFDRepFunctor (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    FDRep k H ⥤ FDRep k (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRep
decls.doc: The conjugate of a finite-dimensional representation.
decls.statement:
def conjFDRep (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H) :
    FDRep k (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRep_V
decls.doc: Conjugation preserves the underlying module of a finite-dimensional representation.
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRep_V (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H) :
    (conjFDRep s A).V = A.V

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepFunctor_one
decls.doc:
Conjugating by `1` does nothing, as an equality of functors.  The `FDRep` mirror of
`conjRepFunctor_one`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRepFunctor_one (H : Subgroup G) :
    conjFDRepFunctor (k := k) (1 : G) H =
      Action.res (FGModuleCat k) (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_one_smul H)).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepFunctor_mul
decls.doc:
**Cocycle coherence** for finite-dimensional representations, at the level of functors.  The
`FDRep` mirror of `conjRepFunctor_mul`, and the form in which the character computations of Mackey
and Clifford theory use it.
decls.title: Cocycle coherence
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRepFunctor_mul (s t : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    conjFDRepFunctor (k := k) (s * t) H =
      conjFDRepFunctor t H ⋙ conjFDRepFunctor s (MulAut.conj t • H) ⋙
        Action.res (FGModuleCat k) (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_mul_smul s t H)).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRep_one
decls.doc:
Conjugating a finite-dimensional representation by `1` does nothing, once `1 · H · 1⁻¹` is
identified with `H`.  The `FDRep` mirror of `conjRep_one`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRep_one {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H) :
    conjFDRep (1 : G) A =
      (Action.res (FGModuleCat k)
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_one_smul H)).toMonoidHom).obj A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRep_mul
decls.doc:
**Cocycle coherence** for finite-dimensional representations: `{}^{st} A = {}^s({}^t A)`, once
`(st)H(st)⁻¹` is identified with `s(tHt⁻¹)s⁻¹`.  The evaluation of `conjFDRepFunctor_mul` at
`A`.
decls.title: Cocycle coherence
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRep_mul (s t : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H) :
    conjFDRep (s * t) A =
      (Action.res (FGModuleCat k)
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_mul_smul s t H)).toMonoidHom).obj
          (conjFDRep s (conjFDRep t A))

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepEquiv
decls.doc:
**Conjugation is an equivalence** `FDRep k H ≌ FDRep k (sHs⁻¹)`.  The `FDRep` mirror of
`conjRepEquiv`; here `FDRep k H` is `Action (FGModuleCat k) H`, so this is Mathlib's
`Action.resEquiv` for `conjSubgroupEquiv s H`.
decls.title: Conjugation is an equivalence
decls.statement:
def conjFDRepEquiv (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    FDRep k H ≌ FDRep k (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepEquiv_functor
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRepEquiv_functor (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjFDRepEquiv (k := k) s H).functor = conjFDRepFunctor s H

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepEquiv_inverse
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRepEquiv_inverse (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjFDRepEquiv (k := k) s H).inverse =
      Action.res (FGModuleCat k) (conjSubgroupEquiv s H).symm.toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRepEquiv_inverse_eq_conjFDRepFunctor
decls.doc:
The inverse of the conjugation equivalence is conjugation by `s⁻¹`, once `s⁻¹(sHs⁻¹)s` is
identified with `H`.  The `FDRep` mirror of `conjRepEquiv_inverse_eq_conjRepFunctor`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRepEquiv_inverse_eq_conjFDRepFunctor (s : G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    (conjFDRepEquiv (k := k) s H).inverse =
      conjFDRepFunctor s⁻¹ (MulAut.conj s • H) ⋙
        Action.res (FGModuleCat k)
          (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (conj_inv_smul_smul s H).symm).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRep_ρ
decls.doc: The conjugate finite-dimensional action, as a heterogeneous equality.
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRep_ρ (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    HEq ((conjFDRep s A).ρ x) (A.ρ (conjSubgroupEquiv s H x))

decls.name: TauCeti.conjFDRep_ρ_cast
decls.doc: The conjugate action, transported along `conjFDRep_V`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjFDRep_ρ_cast (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    cast (congrArg (fun V : FGModuleCat k => V →ₗ[k] V) (conjFDRep_V s A))
      ((conjFDRep s A).ρ x) = A.ρ (conjSubgroupEquiv s H x)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_conjFDRep
decls.doc: Conjugation preserves the dimension (finrank) of a finite-dimensional representation.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_conjFDRep (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H) :
    Module.finrank k (conjFDRep s A) = Module.finrank k A

decls.name: TauCeti.char_conjFDRep
decls.doc: The character of a conjugate representation is evaluated through `conjSubgroupEquiv`.
decls.statement:
theorem char_conjFDRep (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    (conjFDRep s A).character x = A.character (conjSubgroupEquiv s H x)

decls.name: TauCeti.char_conjFDRep_mk
decls.doc: The conjugate-character formula `({}^s χ)(x) = χ(s⁻¹xs)`.
decls.statement:
theorem char_conjFDRep_mk (s : G) {H : Subgroup G} (A : FDRep k H)
    (x : (MulAut.conj s • H : Subgroup G)) :
    (conjFDRep s A).character x =
      A.character ⟨s⁻¹ * (x : G) * s, (mem_conj_smul s H x).mp x.2⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormal_inv_one
decls.doc:
Conjugating a normal subgroup by `1` is the identity automorphism.  The `MulAut.conjNormal`
form of `conj_one_smul`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormal_inv_one :
    (MulAut.conjNormal ((1 : G)⁻¹) : MulAut N).toMonoidHom = MonoidHom.id N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormal_inv_mul
decls.doc:
Conjugating a normal subgroup by `s * t` is conjugating by `t` after conjugating by `s`.  The
`MulAut.conjNormal` form of `conj_mul_smul`; note the order, which is the one `Rep.res` reverses
into a left action.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormal_inv_mul (s t : G) :
    (MulAut.conjNormal ((s * t)⁻¹) : MulAut N).toMonoidHom =
      (MulAut.conjNormal (t⁻¹) : MulAut N).toMonoidHom.comp
        (MulAut.conjNormal (s⁻¹) : MulAut N).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjSubgroupEquiv_comp_subgroupCongr
decls.doc:
On a normal subgroup, the homomorphism `N →* gNg⁻¹ →* N` that `conjRep` restricts along is
`MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjSubgroupEquiv_comp_subgroupCongr (g : G) :
    (conjSubgroupEquiv g N).toMonoidHom.comp
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self g N).symm).toMonoidHom =
      (MulAut.conjNormal (g⁻¹) : MulAut N).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepFunctor
decls.doc:
Conjugation by `g` as an endofunctor of `Rep k N`: for a normal subgroup the conjugated
subgroup is `N` again, so `conjRepFunctor` becomes an endofunctor, namely restriction along
Mathlib's `MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹`.  It is an autoequivalence; see `conjNormalRepEquiv`.

`@[expose]` because the whole point of the normal-subgroup case is that the carrier is `A.V` on
the nose, which is what lets `conjNormalRep_ρ` and its consequences be plain equalities rather
than the heterogeneous ones `conjRep_ρ` is forced into.
decls.statement: def conjNormalRepFunctor (g : G) : Rep k N ⥤ Rep k N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRep
decls.doc:
The conjugate `{}^g A` of a representation of a **normal** subgroup `N`, again a
representation of `N`: the element `x : N` acts by `A.ρ (g⁻¹ x g)`.

This is `conjRep` with the conjugated subgroup identified with `N`, as `res_conjRep` records; the
conjugating automorphism is Mathlib's `MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹`.
decls.statement: def conjNormalRep (g : G) (A : Rep k N) : Rep k N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRep_V
decls.doc:
Conjugation on a normal subgroup preserves the underlying module.  Not a `simp` lemma: it is
`rfl`, and as a rewrite it fires inside the *type* of the left-hand side of `conjNormalRep_ρ`.
decls.statement: theorem conjNormalRep_V (g : G) (A : Rep k N) : (conjNormalRep g A).V = A.V

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRep_ρ
decls.doc:
The conjugate action on a normal subgroup.  Unlike `conjRep_ρ` this is an honest equality:
the two representations are representations of the same group, on the same module.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRep_ρ (g : G) (A : Rep k N) (x : N) :
    (conjNormalRep g A).ρ x = A.ρ (MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹ x)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRep_ρ_mk
decls.doc: The conjugate action on a normal subgroup, written in the ambient group.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRep_ρ_mk (g : G) (A : Rep k N) (x : N) :
    (conjNormalRep g A).ρ x = A.ρ ⟨g⁻¹ * (x : G) * g, hN.conj_mem' (x : G) x.2 g⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.res_conjRepFunctor
decls.doc:
On a normal subgroup, the conjugation functor `conjRepFunctor`, read through the
identification `gNg⁻¹ = N`, is `conjNormalRepFunctor`.
decls.statement:
theorem res_conjRepFunctor (g : G) :
    conjRepFunctor (k := k) g N ⋙
        Rep.resFunctor
          (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self g N).symm).toMonoidHom =
      conjNormalRepFunctor g

decls.name: TauCeti.res_conjRep
decls.doc:
On a normal subgroup, `conjNormalRep` is the general conjugate representation `conjRep`, read
through the identification `gNg⁻¹ = N`.
decls.statement:
theorem res_conjRep (g : G) (A : Rep k N) :
    Rep.res (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self g N).symm).toMonoidHom
        (conjRep g A) = conjNormalRep g A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepFunctor_one
decls.doc: Conjugating by `1` is the identity endofunctor.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRepFunctor_one :
    conjNormalRepFunctor (k := k) (N := N) (1 : G) = 𝟭 (Rep k N)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepFunctor_mul
decls.doc: Conjugation is a left action, as an equality of endofunctors: `{}^{st}(-) = {}^s({}^t(-))`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRepFunctor_mul (s t : G) :
    conjNormalRepFunctor (k := k) (N := N) (s * t) =
      conjNormalRepFunctor t ⋙ conjNormalRepFunctor s

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRep_one
decls.doc: Conjugating by `1` is the identity.
decls.statement: theorem conjNormalRep_one (A : Rep k N) : conjNormalRep (1 : G) A = A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRep_mul
decls.doc: Conjugation is a left action: `{}^{st} A = {}^s({}^t A)`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRep_mul (s t : G) (A : Rep k N) :
    conjNormalRep (s * t) A = conjNormalRep s (conjNormalRep t A)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepEquiv
decls.doc:
Conjugation by `g` is an autoequivalence of `Rep k N`, with inverse conjugation by `g⁻¹`: the
autoequivalence the roadmap asks for.  Conjugation on a normal subgroup is restriction along the
automorphism `MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹`, so this is `resFunctorEquiv` for that automorphism, exactly
as `conjNormalFDRepEquiv` is Mathlib's `Action.resEquiv` for it.

The body is sealed; `conjNormalRepEquiv_functor` and `conjNormalRepEquiv_inverse` are the
interface identifying it with conjugation.
decls.statement: def conjNormalRepEquiv (g : G) : Rep k N ≌ Rep k N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepEquiv_functor
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRepEquiv_functor (g : G) :
    (conjNormalRepEquiv (k := k) (N := N) g).functor = conjNormalRepFunctor g

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepEquiv_inverse
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalRepEquiv_inverse (g : G) :
    (conjNormalRepEquiv (k := k) (N := N) g).inverse = conjNormalRepFunctor g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalRepMulAction
decls.doc:
Conjugation is a left action of `G` on `Rep k N`: `g • A` is `conjNormalRep g A`.  Clifford
theory's inertia group of `A` is the stabilizer of the isomorphism class of `A`,
`{g | {}^g A ≅ A}`, rather than `MulAction.stabilizer G A`, which asks for `{}^g A = A` on the
nose; the induced action on isomorphism classes is not constructed here.
decls.statement: instance conjNormalRepMulAction : MulAction G (Rep k N)

decls.name: TauCeti.smul_eq_conjNormalRep
decls.statement: theorem smul_eq_conjNormalRep (g : G) (A : Rep k N) : g • A = conjNormalRep g A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepFunctor
decls.doc:
Conjugation by `g` as an endofunctor of `FDRep k N`.  The `FDRep` mirror of
`conjNormalRepFunctor`: `FDRep k N` is by definition `Action (FGModuleCat k) N`, so this is
Mathlib's `Action.res` along the conjugating automorphism, and the underlying module of an object
is unchanged on the nose.
decls.statement: def conjNormalFDRepFunctor (g : G) : FDRep k N ⥤ FDRep k N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep
decls.doc:
The conjugate `{}^g A` of a finite-dimensional representation of a **normal** subgroup, again
a finite-dimensional representation of that subgroup.
decls.statement: def conjNormalFDRep (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) : FDRep k N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep_V
decls.doc:
Conjugation on a normal subgroup preserves the underlying module.  Not a `simp` lemma, for the
same reason as `conjNormalRep_V`.
decls.statement: theorem conjNormalFDRep_V (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) : (conjNormalFDRep g A).V = A.V

decls.name: TauCeti.res_conjFDRepFunctor
decls.doc:
On a normal subgroup, the conjugation functor `conjFDRepFunctor`, read through the
identification `gNg⁻¹ = N`, is `conjNormalFDRepFunctor`.  The `FDRep` mirror of
`res_conjRepFunctor`.
decls.statement:
theorem res_conjFDRepFunctor (g : G) :
    conjFDRepFunctor (k := k) g N ⋙
        Action.res (FGModuleCat k)
          (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self g N).symm).toMonoidHom =
      conjNormalFDRepFunctor g

decls.name: TauCeti.res_conjFDRep
decls.doc: On a normal subgroup, `conjNormalFDRep` is `conjFDRep` read through `gNg⁻¹ = N`.
decls.statement:
theorem res_conjFDRep (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) :
    (Action.res (FGModuleCat k)
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self g N).symm).toMonoidHom).obj
      (conjFDRep g A) = conjNormalFDRep g A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepFunctor_one
decls.doc:
Conjugating by `1` is the identity endofunctor.  The `FDRep` mirror of
`conjNormalRepFunctor_one`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRepFunctor_one :
    conjNormalFDRepFunctor (k := k) (N := N) (1 : G) = 𝟭 (FDRep k N)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepFunctor_mul
decls.doc:
Conjugation is a left action, as an equality of endofunctors.  The `FDRep` mirror of
`conjNormalRepFunctor_mul`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRepFunctor_mul (s t : G) :
    conjNormalFDRepFunctor (k := k) (N := N) (s * t) =
      conjNormalFDRepFunctor t ⋙ conjNormalFDRepFunctor s

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep_one
decls.doc: Conjugating by `1` is the identity.
decls.statement: theorem conjNormalFDRep_one (A : FDRep k N) : conjNormalFDRep (1 : G) A = A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep_mul
decls.doc: Conjugation is a left action: `{}^{st} A = {}^s({}^t A)`.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRep_mul (s t : G) (A : FDRep k N) :
    conjNormalFDRep (s * t) A = conjNormalFDRep s (conjNormalFDRep t A)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepEquiv
decls.doc:
Conjugation by `g` is an autoequivalence of `FDRep k N`, with inverse conjugation by `g⁻¹`:
Mathlib's `Action.resEquiv` for the automorphism `MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹` of `N`.

The body is sealed, as for `conjNormalRepEquiv`; `conjNormalFDRepEquiv_functor` and
`conjNormalFDRepEquiv_inverse` are the interface identifying it with conjugation.
decls.statement: def conjNormalFDRepEquiv (g : G) : FDRep k N ≌ FDRep k N

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepEquiv_functor
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRepEquiv_functor (g : G) :
    (conjNormalFDRepEquiv (k := k) (N := N) g).functor = conjNormalFDRepFunctor g

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepEquiv_inverse
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRepEquiv_inverse (g : G) :
    (conjNormalFDRepEquiv (k := k) (N := N) g).inverse = conjNormalFDRepFunctor g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepMulAction
decls.doc:
Conjugation is a left action of `G` on `FDRep k N`.  The `FDRep` mirror of the `MulAction` on
`Rep k N`.
decls.statement: instance conjNormalFDRepMulAction : MulAction G (FDRep k N)

decls.name: TauCeti.smul_eq_conjNormalFDRep
decls.statement: theorem smul_eq_conjNormalFDRep (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) : g • A = conjNormalFDRep g A

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep_ρ
decls.doc: The conjugate finite-dimensional action on a normal subgroup, as an honest equality.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRep_ρ (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) (x : N) :
    (conjNormalFDRep g A).ρ x = A.ρ (MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹ x)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep_ρ_mk
decls.doc: The conjugate finite-dimensional action, written in the ambient group.
decls.statement:
theorem conjNormalFDRep_ρ_mk (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) (x : N) :
    (conjNormalFDRep g A).ρ x = A.ρ ⟨g⁻¹ * (x : G) * g, hN.conj_mem' (x : G) x.2 g⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_conjNormalFDRep
decls.doc: Conjugation on a normal subgroup preserves the dimension.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_conjNormalFDRep (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) :
    Module.finrank k (conjNormalFDRep g A) = Module.finrank k A

decls.name: TauCeti.char_conjNormalFDRep
decls.doc: The character of the conjugate of a representation of a normal subgroup.
decls.statement:
theorem char_conjNormalFDRep (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) (x : N) :
    (conjNormalFDRep g A).character x = A.character (MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹ x)

decls.name: TauCeti.char_conjNormalFDRep_mk
decls.doc: The conjugate-character formula on a normal subgroup: `({}^g χ)(x) = χ(g⁻¹xg)`.
decls.statement:
theorem char_conjNormalFDRep_mk (g : G) (A : FDRep k N) (x : N) :
    (conjNormalFDRep g A).character x =
      A.character ⟨g⁻¹ * (x : G) * g, hN.conj_mem' (x : G) x.2 g⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.rightCosetFactor
decls.doc: The element of `S` carrying the chosen representative of the right coset of `g` to `g`.
decls.statement: def rightCosetFactor (g : G) : S

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.rightCoset_mk_mul
decls.doc: Left multiplication by an element of `S` does not change a right coset.
decls.statement:
theorem rightCoset_mk_mul (s : S) (g : G) :
    Quotient.mk'' ((s : G) * g) =
      (Quotient.mk'' g : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S))

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.rightCosetFactor_mul
decls.doc: The right-coset factor is equivariant under left multiplication by `S`.
decls.statement:
theorem rightCosetFactor_mul (s : S) (g : G) :
    rightCosetFactor (S := S) ((s : G) * g) = s * rightCosetFactor (S := S) g

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.rightCosetFactor_mul_out
decls.doc: The right-coset factor carries the chosen representative back to the original element.
decls.statement:
theorem rightCosetFactor_mul_out (g : G) :
    (rightCosetFactor (S := S) g : G) *
        Quotient.out (Quotient.mk'' g :
          Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S)) = g

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.rightCosetFactor_out
decls.doc: The right-coset factor of a chosen representative is trivial.
decls.statement:
theorem rightCosetFactor_out (q : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S)) :
    rightCosetFactor (S := S) q.out = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.coindSubtypeEquivPi
decls.doc:
Coinduction from a subgroup is linearly equivalent to a product of copies of the original
representation indexed by the right cosets. The forward map evaluates an equivariant function at
the chosen representative of each right coset.

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.coindSubtypeEquivPi_apply
decls.doc: The coset model evaluates a coinduced function at the chosen representative.
decls.statement:
theorem coindSubtypeEquivPi_apply (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S)
    (f : Rep.coind S.subtype A) (q : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S)) :
    coindSubtypeEquivPi A f q = f.1 q.out

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.coindSubtypeEquivPi_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse coset model extends a value from each representative by `S`-equivariance.
decls.statement:
theorem coindSubtypeEquivPi_symm_apply (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S)
    (x : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S) → A) (g : G) :
    ((coindSubtypeEquivPi A).symm x).1 g =
      A.ρ (rightCosetFactor (S := S) g) (x (Quotient.mk'' g))

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.coindSubtypeEquivPi_ρ_apply
decls.doc:
In the coset model the `G`-action on coinduction is the coordinate permutation
`q ↦ ⟦q.out * g⟧` followed by the action of the coset factor of `q.out * g`.

Not a `simp` lemma: Mathlib's `@[simps]` on `Representation.coind` rewrites
`(Rep.coind φ A).ρ g` to its underlying `LinearMap`, so this left-hand side is not in `simp`
normal form. Mathlib states its own action lemma `Representation.ind_mk` the same way.
decls.statement:
theorem coindSubtypeEquivPi_ρ_apply (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S) (g : G)
    (f : Rep.coind S.subtype A) (q : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S)) :
    coindSubtypeEquivPi A ((Rep.coind S.subtype A).ρ g f) q =
      A.ρ (rightCosetFactor (S := S) (q.out * g))
        (coindSubtypeEquivPi A f (Quotient.mk'' (q.out * g)))

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.indSubtypeEquivPi
decls.doc:
The underlying vector space of induction from a finite-index subgroup is a product of copies
of the original representation indexed by the right cosets.

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.indSubtypeEquivPi_apply
decls.doc:
The coset model of induction transports along `Rep.indCoindIso` and then evaluates at the
chosen representative of each right coset.

Not a `simp` lemma: its right-hand side names `Rep.indCoindIso`, so rewriting with it replaces
the coset model by the comparison isomorphism it is built from. The intended interface is
`indSubtypeEquivPi_ρ_apply`, which stays inside the coset model.
decls.statement:
theorem indSubtypeEquivPi_apply [S.FiniteIndex] (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S)
    (x : Rep.ind S.subtype A) (q : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S)) :
    indSubtypeEquivPi A x q =
      ((letI : DecidableRel (QuotientGroup.rightRel S) := Classical.decRel _
        Rep.indCoindIso.{max u v w, u, v} A).hom.hom x).1 q.out

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.indSubtypeEquivPi_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse coset model of induction extends by `S`-equivariance and then transports back
along `Rep.indCoindIso`.

Not a `simp` lemma, for the same reason as `indSubtypeEquivPi_apply`: it rewrites the coset
model into the comparison isomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem indSubtypeEquivPi_symm_apply [S.FiniteIndex] (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S)
    (x : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S) → A) :
    (indSubtypeEquivPi A).symm x =
      (letI : DecidableRel (QuotientGroup.rightRel S) := Classical.decRel _
       Rep.indCoindIso.{max u v w, u, v} A).inv.hom
        ((coindSubtypeEquivPi A).symm x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.indSubtypeEquivPi_ρ_apply
decls.doc:
In the coset model of induction the `G`-action is the coordinate permutation
`q ↦ ⟦q.out * g⟧` followed by the action of the coset factor of `q.out * g`. This is the form a
trace computation over the coset model consumes.

Not a `simp` lemma, for the same reason as `coindSubtypeEquivPi_ρ_apply`: `@[simps]` on
`Representation.ind` takes `(Rep.ind φ A).ρ g` out of `simp` normal form.
decls.statement:
theorem indSubtypeEquivPi_ρ_apply [S.FiniteIndex] (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S) (g : G)
    (x : Rep.ind S.subtype A) (q : Quotient (QuotientGroup.rightRel S)) :
    indSubtypeEquivPi A ((Rep.ind S.subtype A).ρ g x) q =
      A.ρ (rightCosetFactor (S := S) (q.out * g))
        (indSubtypeEquivPi A x (Quotient.mk'' (q.out * g)))

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.finiteDimensional_ind
decls.doc: Induction from a finite-index subgroup preserves finite-dimensionality.
decls.statement:
instance finiteDimensional_ind [S.FiniteIndex] (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S)
    [FiniteDimensional k A] : FiniteDimensional k (Rep.ind S.subtype A)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.finrank_ind
decls.doc:
The dimension of induction from a finite-index subgroup is the index times the original
dimension.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_ind [S.FiniteIndex] (A : Rep.{max u v w} k S) [FiniteDimensional k A] :
    Module.finrank k (Rep.ind S.subtype A) = S.index * Module.finrank k A

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRep
decls.doc: The finite-dimensional representation induced from a finite-index subgroup.
decls.statement:
def indFDRep {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) : FDRep k G

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRepForgetIso
decls.doc:
Forgetting finite-dimensionality from `indFDRep` recovers Mathlib's induced representation.
This is the one place where the two objects are identified; everything below about `indFDRep` is
stated and proved through this isomorphism.
decls.statement:
def indFDRepForgetIso {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G]
    {S : Subgroup G} [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) :
    (forget₂ (FDRep k G) (Rep k G)).obj (indFDRep A) ≅
      Rep.ind S.subtype ((forget₂ (FDRep k S) (Rep k S)).obj A)

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRepMap
decls.doc:
Induction of an intertwiner of finite-dimensional representations: Mathlib's `Rep.indFunctor`
on the underlying intertwiner, conjugated by `indFDRepForgetIso` and transported back along the
fully faithful forgetful functor `FDRep k G ⥤ Rep k G`. Its characterizing property is
`forget₂_map_indFDRepMap`; the definition itself is not exposed.
decls.statement:
def indFDRepMap {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [S.FiniteIndex] {A B : FDRep k S} (f : A ⟶ B) : indFDRep A ⟶ indFDRep B

decls.name: TauCeti.forget₂_map_indFDRepMap
decls.doc:
Forgetting finite-dimensionality from `indFDRepMap` gives Mathlib's induced intertwiner,
conjugated by `indFDRepForgetIso`. This is the only fact about `indFDRepMap` used below.
decls.statement:
theorem forget₂_map_indFDRepMap {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [S.FiniteIndex] {A B : FDRep k S} (f : A ⟶ B) :
    (forget₂ (FDRep k G) (Rep k G)).map (indFDRepMap f) =
      (indFDRepForgetIso A).hom ≫
        (Rep.indFunctor k S.subtype).map ((forget₂ (FDRep k S) (Rep k S)).map f) ≫
          (indFDRepForgetIso B).inv

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRepMap_id
decls.doc: Induction of intertwiners preserves identities.
decls.statement:
theorem indFDRepMap_id {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) : indFDRepMap (𝟙 A) = 𝟙 (indFDRep A)

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRepMap_comp
decls.doc: Induction of intertwiners preserves composition.

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRepFunctor
decls.doc:
Induction from a finite-index subgroup, as a functor on finite-dimensional representations.
It acts on objects as `indFDRep` and on intertwiners as `indFDRepMap`.

`@[simps obj map]` supplies the projection lemmas `indFDRepFunctor_obj` and
`indFDRepFunctor_map`. Both are proved by `rfl`, and the type of the second needs
`indFDRepFunctor.obj A` to reduce to `indFDRep A`, so this definition is `@[expose]`. Exposing it
publishes exactly those two projections: the construction of the morphism map lives in
`indFDRepMap`, which stays opaque behind `forget₂_map_indFDRepMap`.
decls.statement:
def indFDRepFunctor {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [S.FiniteIndex] : FDRep k S ⥤ FDRep k G

decls.name: TauCeti.indFDRepForgetNatIso
decls.doc:
Under the forgetful functor to `Rep k G`, `indFDRepFunctor` is naturally isomorphic to
Mathlib's induction functor, componentwise by `indFDRepForgetIso`.
decls.statement:
def indFDRepForgetNatIso {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {S : Subgroup G}
    [S.FiniteIndex] :
    indFDRepFunctor (k := k) (S := S) ⋙ forget₂ (FDRep k G) (Rep k G) ≅
      forget₂ (FDRep k S) (Rep k S) ⋙ Rep.indFunctor k S.subtype

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_indFDRep
decls.doc:
The dimension of an induced representation is the subgroup index times the dimension of the
original representation.

decls.name: TauCeti.indResFDRepHomEquiv
decls.doc:
**Frobenius reciprocity** for finite-dimensional representations, as a `k`-linear equivalence of
intertwining spaces: `Hom_G(Ind_S^G A, B) ≃ₗ[k] Hom_S(A, Res_S B)`.

This is Mathlib's `Rep.indResHomEquiv`, the linear form of the adjunction
`Rep.indResAdjunction`, conjugated by the fully faithful forgetful functor
`FDRep k G ⥤ Rep k G` and by `TauCeti.indFDRepForgetIso`.

It is private: only `finrank_hom_indFDRep` is intended as API.
decls.title: Frobenius reciprocity
decls.statement:
def indResFDRepHomEquiv [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    (indFDRep A ⟶ B) ≃ₗ[k] (A ⟶ resFDRep S B)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_hom_indFDRep
decls.doc:
The intertwining space out of an induced representation has the same dimension as the
intertwining space into the corresponding restriction. This is the quantitative content of
Frobenius reciprocity, and holds over an arbitrary field.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_hom_indFDRep [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    Module.finrank k (indFDRep A ⟶ B) = Module.finrank k (A ⟶ resFDRep S B)

decls.name: TauCeti.resIndFDRepHomEquiv
decls.doc:
**The second reciprocity**, available because induction from a finite-index subgroup is also a
*right* adjoint to restriction: `Hom_S(Res_S B, A) ≃ₗ[k] Hom_G(B, Ind_S^G A)`.

Where `TauCeti.indResFDRepHomEquiv` transports Mathlib's `Rep.indResHomEquiv`, this transports
`Rep.resCoindHomEquiv` along Mathlib's finite-index identification `Rep.indCoindIso` of induction
with coinduction; the pair is the finite-dimensional shadow of `Rep.resIndAdjunction`.

It is private: only `finrank_hom_resFDRep` is intended as API.
decls.title: The second reciprocity
decls.statement:
def resIndFDRepHomEquiv [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    (resFDRep S B ⟶ A) ≃ₗ[k] (B ⟶ indFDRep A)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_hom_resFDRep
decls.doc: The dimension form of the second reciprocity.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_hom_resFDRep [S.FiniteIndex] (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    Module.finrank k (resFDRep S B ⟶ A) = Module.finrank k (B ⟶ indFDRep A)

decls.name: TauCeti.isUnit_natCard_subgroup
decls.doc:
If the order of a finite group is invertible in `k`, then so is the order of any subgroup,
because the two differ by the index.
decls.statement:
theorem isUnit_natCard_subgroup [Finite G] (S : Subgroup G)
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k)) : IsUnit (Nat.card S : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.frobenius_reciprocity
decls.doc:
**Frobenius reciprocity as a character identity.**  The scalar product over `G` of an induced
character with a character of `G` equals the scalar product over `S` of the original character with
the restricted character.

Both sides are written as explicit normalized sums, so the statement does not depend on the name of
any particular pairing; `TauCeti.characterPairing_indFDRep` is the same identity phrased against
`TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing`.  The hypothesis `hG` is what makes the normalizing factors
meaningful; it also supplies the invertibility of `Nat.card S`.
decls.title: Frobenius reciprocity as a character identity
decls.statement:
theorem frobenius_reciprocity [Fintype G] (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k))
    (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, (indFDRep A).character g * B.character g⁻¹ =
      (Nat.card S : k)⁻¹ * ∑ s : S, A.character s * B.character ((s : G)⁻¹)

decls.name: TauCeti.characterPairing_indFDRep
decls.doc:
Frobenius reciprocity, phrased against the normalized pairing of class functions used by the
character-theory development.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_indFDRep [Fintype G] (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k))
    (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    ClassFunction.characterPairing (ClassFunction.ofFDRep (indFDRep A))
        (ClassFunction.ofFDRep B) =
      ClassFunction.characterPairing (ClassFunction.ofFDRep A)
        (ClassFunction.ofFDRep (resFDRep S B))

decls.name: TauCeti.characterPairing_resFDRep
decls.doc:
The reciprocity in the other direction, phrased against
`TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing`.  The pairing is symmetric, so this is
`characterPairing_indFDRep` with both sides flipped.
decls.statement:
theorem characterPairing_resFDRep [Fintype G] (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k))
    (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    ClassFunction.characterPairing (ClassFunction.ofFDRep (resFDRep S B))
        (ClassFunction.ofFDRep A) =
      ClassFunction.characterPairing (ClassFunction.ofFDRep B)
        (ClassFunction.ofFDRep (indFDRep A))

decls.name: TauCeti.frobenius_reciprocity_resFDRep
decls.doc:
**Frobenius reciprocity in the other direction**: the scalar product over `S` of a restricted
character with a character of `S` equals the scalar product over `G` of the original character with
the induced character.  This is `characterPairing_resFDRep` with the pairing unfolded.
decls.title: Frobenius reciprocity in the other direction
decls.statement:
theorem frobenius_reciprocity_resFDRep [Fintype G] (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k))
    (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) :
    (Nat.card S : k)⁻¹ * ∑ s : S, B.character (s : G) * A.character s⁻¹ =
      (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, B.character g * (indFDRep A).character g⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.card_inv_mul_sum_character_indFDRep
decls.doc:
Reciprocity against the trivial representation: the normalized average of an induced character
over `G` is the normalized average of the original character over `S`.  Equivalently, by
`FDRep.average_char_eq_finrank_invariants`, inducing does not change the dimension of the space of
invariants.
decls.statement:
theorem card_inv_mul_sum_character_indFDRep [Fintype G]
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k)) (A : FDRep k S) :
    (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g : G, (indFDRep A).character g =
      (Nat.card S : k)⁻¹ * ∑ s : S, A.character s

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialSource
decls.doc:
The `H`-representation on `k[G] ⊗[k] k` whose coinvariants define `Ind_H^G (trivial)`:
left translation by `H` on `k[G]`, and the trivial action on `k`.
decls.statement: abbrev indTrivialSource : Representation k H (k[G] ⊗[k] k)

decls.name: TauCeti.mapDomain_inv_comp_leftRegular
decls.doc: Sending `x : G` to the coset `⟦x⁻¹⟧` turns left translation by `H` into the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem mapDomain_inv_comp_leftRegular (s : H) :
    MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainLinearMap k k (fun x : G ↦ (QuotientGroup.mk x⁻¹ : G ⧸ H)) ∘ₗ
        Representation.leftRegular k G (s : G) =
      MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainLinearMap k k (fun x : G ↦ (QuotientGroup.mk x⁻¹ : G ⧸ H))

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialLift
decls.doc:
The linear map `k[G] ⊗[k] k →ₗ[k] k[G ⧸ H]` sending `single x r ⊗ₜ a` to
`single ⟦x⁻¹⟧ (a • r)`.
decls.statement: def indTrivialLift : (k[G] ⊗[k] k) →ₗ[k] k[G ⧸ H]

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialLift_tmul
decls.statement:
theorem indTrivialLift_tmul (x : G) (r a : k) :
    indTrivialLift k H (MonoidAlgebra.single x r ⊗ₜ a) =
      MonoidAlgebra.single (QuotientGroup.mk x⁻¹ : G ⧸ H) (a • r)

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialLift_comp
decls.statement:
theorem indTrivialLift_comp (s : H) :
    indTrivialLift k H ∘ₗ indTrivialSource k H s = indTrivialLift k H

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialToQuotient
decls.doc: The forward map of `TauCeti.indTrivialEquiv`, from `Ind_H^G (trivial)` to `k[G ⧸ H]`.
decls.statement:
def indTrivialToQuotient :
    IndV H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) →ₗ[k] k[G ⧸ H]

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialToQuotient_mk
decls.statement:
theorem indTrivialToQuotient_mk (x : G) (a : k) :
    indTrivialToQuotient k H (IndV.mk H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) x a) =
      MonoidAlgebra.single (QuotientGroup.mk x⁻¹ : G ⧸ H) a

decls.name: TauCeti.indV_mk_smul
decls.doc: Left translation by `H` is invisible in `Ind_H^G (trivial)`.
decls.statement:
theorem indV_mk_smul (s : H) (x : G) (a : k) :
    IndV.mk H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) ((s : G) * x) a =
      IndV.mk H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) x a

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialMk
decls.doc: The image of a coset `⟦x⟧` in `Ind_H^G (trivial)`, namely `⟦single x⁻¹ 1 ⊗ₜ 1⟧`.
decls.statement:
def indTrivialMk (q : G ⧸ H) :
    IndV H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k)

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialMk_mk
decls.statement:
theorem indTrivialMk_mk (x : G) :
    indTrivialMk k H (QuotientGroup.mk x) =
      IndV.mk H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) x⁻¹ (1 : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.quotientToIndTrivial
decls.doc: The inverse map of `TauCeti.indTrivialEquiv`, from `k[G ⧸ H]` to `Ind_H^G (trivial)`.
decls.statement:
def quotientToIndTrivial :
    k[G ⧸ H] →ₗ[k] IndV H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k)

decls.name: TauCeti.quotientToIndTrivial_single
decls.statement:
theorem quotientToIndTrivial_single (q : G ⧸ H) (r : k) :
    quotientToIndTrivial k H (MonoidAlgebra.single q r) = r • indTrivialMk k H q

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialEquiv
decls.doc:
**The permutation representation.** Inducing the trivial representation of a subgroup `H ≤ G`
along `H.subtype` gives the permutation representation of `G` on the left cosets `G ⧸ H`.
decls.title: The permutation representation

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialEquiv_apply_mk
decls.doc:
The generator computation rule for `indTrivialEquiv`. Not a `simp` lemma: `simp` unfolds the
reducible `Representation.IndV.mk`, so the left-hand side is not in `simp`-normal form.
decls.statement:
theorem indTrivialEquiv_apply_mk (x : G) (a : k) :
    indTrivialEquiv k H (IndV.mk H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) x a) =
      MonoidAlgebra.single (QuotientGroup.mk x⁻¹ : G ⧸ H) a

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialEquiv_symm_apply_single
decls.doc: The generator computation rule for the inverse of `indTrivialEquiv`.
decls.statement:
theorem indTrivialEquiv_symm_apply_single (x : G) (r : k) :
    (indTrivialEquiv k H).symm (MonoidAlgebra.single (QuotientGroup.mk x : G ⧸ H) r) =
      r • IndV.mk H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k) x⁻¹ (1 : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.indTrivialIso
decls.doc:
**The permutation representation**, in `Rep k G`: inducing the trivial representation of a
subgroup `H ≤ G` gives the permutation representation on the left cosets `G ⧸ H`.
decls.title: The permutation representation
decls.statement:
def indTrivialIso :
    Rep.ind H.subtype (Rep.trivial k H k) ≅ Rep.ofMulAction k G (G ⧸ H)

decls.name: TauCeti.instFiniteIndTrivial
decls.doc:
`Ind_H^G (trivial)` is a finite module whenever `H` has finite index, by transport along
`TauCeti.indTrivialEquiv`; over a field this is the `FiniteDimensional` instance that lets one
even state its character.
decls.statement:
instance instFiniteIndTrivial [Finite (G ⧸ H)] :
    Module.Finite k (IndV H.subtype (Representation.trivial k H k))

decls.name: TauCeti.ofMulAction_basis
decls.doc: A permutation representation permutes the standard basis of `k[X]`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofMulAction_basis (X : Type w) [MulAction G X] (g : G) (x : X) :
    Representation.ofMulAction k G X g (MonoidAlgebra.basis X k x) =
      MonoidAlgebra.basis X k (g • x)

decls.name: TauCeti.toMatrix_ofMulAction_diag
decls.doc: The diagonal entries of a permutation representation record which points are fixed.
decls.statement:
theorem toMatrix_ofMulAction_diag (X : Type w) [MulAction G X] [Fintype X]
    [DecidableEq X] (g : G) (x : X) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (MonoidAlgebra.basis X k) (MonoidAlgebra.basis X k)
      (Representation.ofMulAction k G X g) x x = if g • x = x then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.char_ofMulAction
decls.doc:
**The permutation character.** The character of the permutation representation `k[X]` at `g`
is the number of points of `X` fixed by `g`, cast into `k`.
decls.title: The permutation character
decls.statement:
theorem char_ofMulAction (X : Type w) [MulAction G X] [Finite X] (g : G) :
    (Representation.ofMulAction k G X).character g = Nat.card {x : X // g • x = x}

decls.name: TauCeti.char_ind_trivial
decls.doc:
**The permutation character of an induced trivial representation.** The character of
`Ind_H^G (trivial)` at `g` is the number of cosets in `G ⧸ H` fixed by `g`, cast into `k`.
decls.title: The permutation character of an induced trivial representation

decls.name: TauCeti.resFunctor_comp
decls.doc:
Restricting representations along a composite homomorphism is restricting twice over.
Mathlib has no equality of this shape (`Action.resComp` is the natural isomorphism for `Action`),
so we record the equality form, which keeps the reduction out of proofs that state equalities of
restriction functors.
decls.statement:
theorem resFunctor_comp (φ : K →* L) (ψ : H →* K) :
    Rep.resFunctor (k := k) (φ.comp ψ) = Rep.resFunctor φ ⋙ Rep.resFunctor ψ

decls.name: TauCeti.actionRes_comp
decls.doc:
The `Action` form of `resFunctor_comp`, which is the one that applies to `FDRep`; the equality
strengthens Mathlib's natural isomorphism `Action.resComp`.
decls.statement:
theorem actionRes_comp {V : Type*} [Category V] (φ : K →* L) (ψ : H →* K) :
    Action.res V (φ.comp ψ) = Action.res V φ ⋙ Action.res V ψ

decls.name: TauCeti.resFunctor_id
decls.doc: Restricting along the identity is the identity functor.
decls.statement: theorem resFunctor_id : Rep.resFunctor (k := k) (MonoidHom.id H) = 𝟭 (Rep k H)

decls.name: TauCeti.resFunctorEquiv
decls.doc:
Restriction along a monoid isomorphism is an equivalence of categories, with inverse
restriction along the inverse isomorphism.  This is the `Rep` analogue of Mathlib's
`Action.resEquiv`, which does not apply because `Rep` is a structure rather than an `Action`.

The body is sealed; `resFunctorEquiv_functor` and `resFunctorEquiv_inverse` are the interface
identifying its two functors with restriction.
decls.statement: def resFunctorEquiv (e : H ≃* K) : Rep k K ≌ Rep k H

decls.name: TauCeti.resFunctorEquiv_functor
decls.statement:
theorem resFunctorEquiv_functor (e : H ≃* K) :
    (resFunctorEquiv (k := k) e).functor = Rep.resFunctor e.toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.resFunctorEquiv_inverse
decls.statement:
theorem resFunctorEquiv_inverse (e : H ≃* K) :
    (resFunctorEquiv (k := k) e).inverse = Rep.resFunctor e.symm.toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.resFDRep
decls.doc:
Restriction of a finite-dimensional representation of `G` to a subgroup `S`: Mathlib's
`Action.res` along `S.subtype`, under the definitional identification
`FDRep k G = Action (FGModuleCat k) G`.

This is a reducible abbreviation, so Mathlib's `Action.res` API applies to it unchanged; in
particular `(Action.res (FGModuleCat k) S.subtype).map f : resFDRep S B ⟶ resFDRep S B'`
restricts an intertwiner, and is functorial by `Functor.map_id` and `Functor.map_comp`.
decls.statement: abbrev resFDRep (S : Subgroup G) (B : FDRep k G) : FDRep k S

decls.name: TauCeti.forget₂_obj_resFDRep
decls.doc:
Restriction commutes with forgetting finite-dimensionality: after forgetting, `resFDRep` is
Mathlib's `Rep.res`, on the nose rather than up to isomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem forget₂_obj_resFDRep (S : Subgroup G) (B : FDRep k G) :
    (forget₂ (FDRep k S) (Rep k S)).obj (resFDRep S B) =
      Rep.res S.subtype ((forget₂ (FDRep k G) (Rep k G)).obj B)

decls.name: TauCeti.character_resFDRep
decls.doc: The character of a restriction is the restriction of the character.
decls.statement:
theorem character_resFDRep (S : Subgroup G) (B : FDRep k G) (s : S) :
    (resFDRep S B).character s = B.character (s : G)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.resFunctorCompIso
decls.doc:
Restriction along two composable group homomorphisms is naturally isomorphic to restriction
along their composite.  The two functors are in fact equal (`TauCeti.resFunctor_comp`), so this is
that equality read as an isomorphism.
decls.statement:
def resFunctorCompIso (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) :
    _root_.Rep.resFunctor.{max u v w x} (k := k) ψ ⋙
      _root_.Rep.resFunctor.{max u v w x} (k := k) φ ≅
        _root_.Rep.resFunctor.{max u v w x} (k := k) (ψ.comp φ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.resFunctorCompIso_hom_app_apply
decls.doc: The forward component of `resFunctorCompIso` acts as the identity on vectors.
decls.statement:
lemma resFunctorCompIso_hom_app_apply (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) (A : _root_.Rep k K) (x : A.V) :
    ((resFunctorCompIso φ ψ).hom.app A) x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.resFunctorCompIso_inv_app_apply
decls.doc: The inverse component of `resFunctorCompIso` acts as the identity on vectors.
decls.statement:
lemma resFunctorCompIso_inv_app_apply (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) (A : _root_.Rep k K) (x : A.V) :
    ((resFunctorCompIso φ ψ).inv.app A) x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.indFunctorCompIso
decls.doc:
Induction in stages: induction along a composite is naturally isomorphic to successive
inductions along the two group homomorphisms.
decls.statement:
def indFunctorCompIso (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) :
    _root_.Rep.indFunctor.{max u v w x} k φ ⋙
      _root_.Rep.indFunctor.{max u v w x} k ψ ≅
        _root_.Rep.indFunctor.{max u v w x} k (ψ.comp φ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.conjugateEquiv_indFunctorCompIso_inv
decls.doc:
The induction-in-stages isomorphism is characterized by the restriction-composition
isomorphism under the adjunction equivalence.
decls.statement:
lemma conjugateEquiv_indFunctorCompIso_inv (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) :
    conjugateEquiv
      ((_root_.Rep.indResAdjunction.{max u v w x} k φ).comp
        (_root_.Rep.indResAdjunction.{max u v w x} k ψ))
      (_root_.Rep.indResAdjunction.{max u v w x} k (ψ.comp φ))
      (indFunctorCompIso φ ψ).inv =
        (resFunctorCompIso φ ψ).hom

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.coindFunctorCompIso
decls.doc:
Coinduction in stages: successive coinductions are naturally isomorphic to coinduction along
the composite homomorphism.
decls.statement:
def coindFunctorCompIso (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) :
    _root_.Rep.coindFunctor.{max u v w x} k φ ⋙
      _root_.Rep.coindFunctor.{max u v w x} k ψ ≅
        _root_.Rep.coindFunctor.{max u v w x} k (ψ.comp φ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Rep.conjugateEquiv_symm_coindFunctorCompIso_hom
decls.doc:
The coinduction-in-stages isomorphism is characterized by the inverse
restriction-composition isomorphism under the inverse adjunction equivalence.
decls.statement:
lemma conjugateEquiv_symm_coindFunctorCompIso_hom (φ : G →* H) (ψ : H →* K) :
    ((conjugateEquiv
      ((_root_.Rep.resCoindAdjunction.{max u v w x} k ψ).comp
        (_root_.Rep.resCoindAdjunction.{max u v w x} k φ))
      (_root_.Rep.resCoindAdjunction.{max u v w x} k (ψ.comp φ))).symm
      (coindFunctorCompIso φ ψ).hom) =
    (resFunctorCompIso φ ψ).inv

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic
decls.doc: A quiver is acyclic if every closed path is trivial.
decls.statement: def Quiver.IsAcyclic (V : Type u) [Quiver.{v} V] : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.isAcyclic_def
decls.doc: The defining closed-path condition for an acyclic quiver.
decls.statement:
theorem Quiver.isAcyclic_def :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V ↔ ∀ ⦃a : V⦄ (p : Path a a), p = Path.nil

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.eq_nil
decls.doc: Every closed path in an acyclic quiver is trivial.
decls.statement: theorem eq_nil (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) {a : V} (p : Path a a) : p = Path.nil

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.iff_forall_length_eq_zero
decls.doc: A quiver is acyclic exactly when every closed path has length zero.
decls.statement:
theorem iff_forall_length_eq_zero :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V ↔ ∀ ⦃a : V⦄ (p : Path a a), p.length = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.length_eq_zero
decls.doc: In an acyclic quiver, every closed path has length zero.
decls.statement:
theorem length_eq_zero (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) {a : V} (p : Path a a) :
    p.length = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.not_length_pos
decls.doc: An acyclic quiver has no closed path of positive length.
decls.statement:
theorem not_length_pos (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) {a : V} (p : Path a a) :
    ¬0 < p.length

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.iff_forall_not_length_pos
decls.doc: A quiver is acyclic exactly when it has no closed path of positive length.
decls.statement:
theorem iff_forall_not_length_pos :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V ↔ ∀ ⦃a : V⦄ (p : Path a a), ¬0 < p.length

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.iff_not_exists_ne_nil
decls.doc: A quiver is acyclic exactly when it has no nontrivial closed path.
decls.statement:
theorem iff_not_exists_ne_nil :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V ↔ ¬∃ (a : V) (p : Path a a), p ≠ Path.nil

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.comp_eq_nil
decls.doc: The composition of paths in opposite directions is trivial in an acyclic quiver.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.length_eq_zero_of_paths_left
decls.doc: If paths run in both directions in an acyclic quiver, the forward path has length zero.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.length_eq_zero_of_paths_right
decls.doc: If paths run in both directions in an acyclic quiver, the reverse path has length zero.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.eq_of_paths
decls.doc: Vertices joined by paths in both directions in an acyclic quiver are equal.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.vertices_nodup
decls.doc: The vertices encountered by a path in an acyclic quiver are pairwise distinct.
decls.statement:
theorem vertices_nodup (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) {a b : V} (p : Path a b) :
    p.vertices.Nodup

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.not_nonempty_path_and_nonempty_path
decls.doc: Between distinct vertices of an acyclic quiver, paths cannot exist in both directions.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.isEmpty_path_of_path
decls.doc: A path between distinct vertices of an acyclic quiver excludes every reverse path.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.isEmpty_hom_self
decls.doc: An acyclic quiver has no loops.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_hom_self (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) (a : V) :
    IsEmpty (a ⟶ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.isEmpty_hom_of_hom
decls.doc: In an acyclic quiver, an arrow excludes every reverse arrow.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmpty_hom_of_hom (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) {a b : V}
    (e : a ⟶ b) : IsEmpty (b ⟶ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.subsingleton_path_self
decls.doc: Closed paths in an acyclic quiver form a subsingleton.
decls.statement:
theorem subsingleton_path_self (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) (a : V) :
    Subsingleton (Path a a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.of_isEmpty_hom
decls.doc: A quiver with no arrows is acyclic.
decls.statement:
theorem of_isEmpty_hom [∀ a b : V, IsEmpty (a ⟶ b)] :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.of_mapPath_self_injective
decls.doc:
A quiver mapping to an acyclic quiver is acyclic if the induced map on each closed-path
type is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem of_mapPath_self_injective {W : Type*} [Quiver W] (F : V ⥤q W)
    (hW : Quiver.IsAcyclic W)
    (hinj : ∀ ⦃a : V⦄, Function.Injective (F.mapPath : Path a a → Path (F.obj a) (F.obj a))) :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.of_mapPath_injective
decls.doc:
A quiver is acyclic if its induced maps on all path types are injective and its target is
acyclic.
decls.statement:
theorem of_mapPath_injective {W : Type*} [Quiver W] (F : V ⥤q W)
    (hW : Quiver.IsAcyclic W)
    (hinj : ∀ ⦃a b : V⦄, Function.Injective (F.mapPath : Path a b → Path (F.obj a) (F.obj b))) :
    Quiver.IsAcyclic V

decls.name: TauCeti.finite_boundedPaths
decls.doc: Paths of a fixed bounded length are finite when vertices and arrow types are finite.
decls.statement:
theorem finite_boundedPaths [Finite V] [∀ a b : V, Finite (a ⟶ b)] (n : ℕ) (a b : V) :
    Finite (_root_.Quiver.Path.BoundedPaths a b n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.length_lt_card
decls.doc: Every path in an acyclic finite quiver has length strictly below the number of vertices.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.finite_paths
decls.statement:
theorem finite_paths [Finite V] [∀ a b : V, Finite (a ⟶ b)] (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) :
    Finite (Σ a b : V, _root_.Quiver.Path a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.finite_paths_of_isAcyclic
decls.doc: A finite acyclic quiver with finite arrow types has finitely many paths.
decls.statement:
theorem finite_paths_of_isAcyclic [Finite V] [∀ a b : V, Finite (a ⟶ b)]
    (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic V) : Finite (Σ a b : V, _root_.Quiver.Path a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_pathAlgebra_of_isAcyclic
decls.doc: The path algebra of a finite acyclic quiver is finite-dimensional.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_pathAlgebra_of_isAcyclic (k : Type w) (Q : Type u) [DivisionRing k]
    [Quiver.{v} Q] [Finite Q] [∀ a b : Q, Finite (a ⟶ b)] (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic Q) :
    FiniteDimensional k (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm
decls.doc: The Euler (or Ringel) form of a finite quiver. Arrows are counted with multiplicity.
decls.statement: def eulerForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ (Q → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_def
decls.doc: The defining sum for the Euler form.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_def (d e : Q → ℤ) :
    eulerForm Q d e =
      (∑ v : Q, d v * e v) - ∑ a : Q, ∑ b : Q, ∑ _ : a ⟶ b, d a * e b

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_eq_sum_card
decls.doc: The Euler form with the arrows between each pair of vertices counted by cardinality.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_eq_sum_card (d e : Q → ℤ) :
    eulerForm Q d e =
      (∑ v : Q, d v * e v)
        - ∑ a : Q, ∑ b : Q, (Fintype.card (a ⟶ b) : ℤ) * (d a * e b)

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm
decls.doc: The Tits form of a finite quiver, the diagonal of its Euler form.
decls.statement: def titsForm : QuadraticMap ℤ (Q → ℤ) ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_def
decls.doc: The defining equation for the Tits form.
decls.statement: theorem titsForm_def (d : Q → ℤ) : titsForm Q d = eulerForm Q d d

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm
decls.doc: The symmetric bilinear form obtained by polarizing the Tits form.
decls.statement: def titsPolarForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ (Q → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_def
decls.doc: The defining equation for the polarized Tits form.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_def (d e : Q → ℤ) :
    titsPolarForm Q d e = eulerForm Q d e + eulerForm Q e d

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_add
decls.doc: The Tits form evaluated at a sum.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_add (d e : Q → ℤ) :
