    titsForm Q (d + e) = titsForm Q d + titsForm Q e + titsPolarForm Q d e

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_sub
decls.doc: The Tits form evaluated at a difference.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_sub (d e : Q → ℤ) :
    titsForm Q (d - e) = titsForm Q d + titsForm Q e - titsPolarForm Q d e

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_comm
decls.doc: The polarized Tits form is symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_comm (d e : Q → ℤ) :
    titsPolarForm Q d e = titsPolarForm Q e d

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_card_path_left
decls.doc:
**The Euler form against a path-count vector is evaluation.** Pairing the vector counting the
paths out of `i` against any `e : Q → ℤ` returns `eᵢ`: at each vertex `b` the path count `#(i → b)`
cancels the arrow-weighted sum `∑ₐ #(a ⟶ b) · #(i → a)` up to the trivial path, by the last-arrow
recursion `TauCeti.card_path_eq_ite_add_sum`.
decls.title: The Euler form against a path-count vector is evaluation
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_card_path_left (i : Q) [∀ a : Q, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)] (e : Q → ℤ) :
    eulerForm Q (fun v ↦ (Nat.card (Quiver.Path i v) : ℤ)) e = e i

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_single_left
decls.doc: The Euler form with a simple dimension vector on the left counts the arrows out of `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_single_left (i : Q) (e : Q → ℤ) :
    eulerForm Q (Pi.single i 1) e = e i - ∑ b : Q, (Fintype.card (i ⟶ b) : ℤ) * e b

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_single_right
decls.doc: The Euler form with a simple dimension vector on the right counts the arrows into `j`.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_single_right (d : Q → ℤ) (j : Q) :
    eulerForm Q d (Pi.single j 1) = d j - ∑ a : Q, (Fintype.card (a ⟶ j) : ℤ) * d a

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_single_single
decls.doc: The Euler form in the simple dimension vectors: `⟨αᵢ, αⱼ⟩ = δᵢⱼ - #(i ⟶ j)`.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_single_single (i j : Q) :
    eulerForm Q (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1)
      = (if i = j then 1 else 0) - (Fintype.card (i ⟶ j) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_single
decls.doc: The Tits form of a simple dimension vector is one minus the number of loops at that vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_single (i : Q) :
    titsForm Q (Pi.single i 1) = 1 - (Fintype.card (i ⟶ i) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_single_of_isEmpty
decls.doc: A loopless vertex has a simple dimension vector of Tits norm one, that is, `αᵢ` is a root.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_single_of_isEmpty {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) :
    titsForm Q (Pi.single i 1) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_single_left
decls.doc: The polarized Tits form against a simple dimension vector, in coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_single_left (i : Q) (d : Q → ℤ) :
    titsPolarForm Q (Pi.single i 1) d
      = 2 * d i - ∑ v : Q, ((Fintype.card (i ⟶ v) : ℤ) + (Fintype.card (v ⟶ i) : ℤ)) * d v

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_single_right
decls.doc: The polarized Tits form against a simple dimension vector on the right, in coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_single_right (d : Q → ℤ) (i : Q) :
    titsPolarForm Q d (Pi.single i 1)
      = 2 * d i - ∑ v : Q, ((Fintype.card (i ⟶ v) : ℤ) + (Fintype.card (v ⟶ i) : ℤ)) * d v

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_single_single
decls.doc:
The Gram matrix of the polarized Tits form in the simple dimension vectors is
`2·I - (A + Aᵀ)`, for `A` the matrix of arrow counts: the symmetrized Cartan matrix of `Q`.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_single_single (i j : Q) :
    titsPolarForm Q (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1)
      = 2 * (if i = j then 1 else 0)
        - ((Fintype.card (i ⟶ j) : ℤ) + (Fintype.card (j ⟶ i) : ℤ))

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_single_self_of_isEmpty
decls.doc:
A loopless vertex has `⟨αᵢ, αᵢ⟩ = 2` for the polarized Tits form: the normalization that
makes the simple reflection at `i` an involution.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_single_self_of_isEmpty {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) :
    titsPolarForm Q (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single i 1) = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.pathLastArrowEquiv
decls.doc:
**The last-arrow decomposition of a path.** A path `i → b` is either trivial, and then `i = b`,
or a path `i → a` followed by a last arrow `a ⟶ b`, uniquely so.
decls.title: The last-arrow decomposition of a path
decls.statement:
def pathLastArrowEquiv (i b : V) :
    Quiver.Path i b ≃ (PLift (i = b) ⊕ Σ a : V, Quiver.Path i a × (a ⟶ b))

decls.name: TauCeti.pathLastArrowEquiv_nil
decls.doc: The trivial path is the left summand of the last-arrow decomposition.
decls.statement:
theorem pathLastArrowEquiv_nil (i : V) :
    pathLastArrowEquiv i i Quiver.Path.nil = Sum.inl ⟨rfl⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.pathLastArrowEquiv_cons
decls.doc: A path with a last arrow is the right summand of the last-arrow decomposition.
decls.statement:
theorem pathLastArrowEquiv_cons {i a b : V} (p : Quiver.Path i a) (e : a ⟶ b) :
    pathLastArrowEquiv i b (p.cons e) = Sum.inr ⟨a, p, e⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.pathLastArrowEquiv_symm_inl
decls.doc: The left summand of the last-arrow decomposition recomposes to the trivial path.
decls.statement:
theorem pathLastArrowEquiv_symm_inl (i : V) :
    (pathLastArrowEquiv i i).symm (Sum.inl ⟨rfl⟩) = Quiver.Path.nil

decls.name: TauCeti.pathLastArrowEquiv_symm_inr
decls.doc: The right summand of the last-arrow decomposition recomposes by appending the last arrow.
decls.statement:
theorem pathLastArrowEquiv_symm_inr {i b : V} (a : V) (p : Quiver.Path i a) (e : a ⟶ b) :
    (pathLastArrowEquiv i b).symm (Sum.inr ⟨a, p, e⟩) = p.cons e

decls.name: TauCeti.card_path_eq_ite_add_sum
decls.doc:
**The last-arrow recursion for path counts.** The paths `i → b` are the trivial one, present
exactly when `i = b`, together with a path `i → a` and an arrow `a ⟶ b`. All three cardinalities
are honest counts only when the paths out of `i` are finite, which is what the hypothesis
`[∀ a, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)]` provides. The only arrows counted are those into `b`, so
`[∀ a, Finite (a ⟶ b)]` suffices for the arrow factors.
decls.title: The last-arrow recursion for path counts
decls.statement:
theorem card_path_eq_ite_add_sum [DecidableEq V] [Fintype V] (i : V)
    [∀ a : V, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)] (b : V) [∀ a : V, Finite (a ⟶ b)] :
    Nat.card (Quiver.Path i b)
      = (if i = b then 1 else 0)
        + ∑ a : V, Nat.card (Quiver.Path i a) * Nat.card (a ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop
decls.doc: The quiver with one vertex and one loop.
decls.statement: inductive OneLoop : Type

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.instFintype
decls.statement: instance : Fintype OneLoop

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.instUnique
decls.statement: instance : Unique OneLoop

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.instQuiver
decls.statement: instance : _root_.Quiver OneLoop

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.instSubsingletonHom
decls.statement: instance (a b : OneLoop) : Subsingleton (a ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.loop
decls.doc: The unique loop in the one-loop quiver.
decls.statement: def loop : (vertex : OneLoop) ⟶ vertex

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.pathOfLength
decls.doc: The path of a prescribed length in the one-loop quiver.
decls.statement: def pathOfLength : ℕ → _root_.Quiver.Path (vertex : OneLoop) vertex

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.length_pathOfLength
decls.statement: theorem length_pathOfLength (n : ℕ) : (pathOfLength n).length = n

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.length_toList
decls.statement:
theorem length_toList {a b : OneLoop}
    (p : _root_.Quiver.Path a b) : p.toList.length = p.length

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.path_eq_pathOfLength
decls.statement:
theorem path_eq_pathOfLength
    (p : _root_.Quiver.Path (vertex : OneLoop) vertex) :
    p = pathOfLength p.length

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath
decls.doc:
The total space of the paths of a quiver: a path together with its source and target. This is
the index type of the path basis of the path algebra.
decls.statement: abbrev Quiver.TotalPath (Q : Type u) [Quiver.{v} Q] : Type _

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.OneLoop.totalPathEquivNat
decls.doc: Paths in the one-loop quiver are classified by their length.
decls.statement: def totalPathEquivNat : Quiver.TotalPath OneLoop ≃ ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?
decls.doc:
Concatenation of indexed paths in the *later factor first* order used by the path algebra:
`x.mul? y` traces `y` and then `x`, and is `none` unless `y` ends where `x` starts.
decls.statement: def mul? (x y : TotalPath Q) : Option (TotalPath Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_mk
decls.doc: Composable indexed paths concatenate, the later factor written first.
decls.statement:
theorem mul?_mk {a b c : Q} (p : _root_.Quiver.Path a b) (q : _root_.Quiver.Path c a) :
    mul? (⟨a, b, p⟩ : TotalPath Q) ⟨c, a, q⟩ = some ⟨c, b, q.comp p⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_eq_none
decls.doc: Indexed paths that do not meet have no concatenation.
decls.statement: theorem mul?_eq_none {x y : TotalPath Q} (h : y.2.1 ≠ x.1) : mul? x y = none

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_eq_none_iff
decls.doc: The concatenation of two indexed paths is undefined exactly when they do not meet.
decls.statement: theorem mul?_eq_none_iff {x y : TotalPath Q} : mul? x y = none ↔ y.2.1 ≠ x.1

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_nil_left
decls.doc: The trivial path at the target of `x` is a left unit for `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem mul?_nil_left (x : TotalPath Q) :
    mul? (⟨x.2.1, x.2.1, _root_.Quiver.Path.nil⟩ : TotalPath Q) x = some x

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_nil_right
decls.doc: The trivial path at the source of `x` is a right unit for `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem mul?_nil_right (x : TotalPath Q) :
    mul? x (⟨x.1, x.1, _root_.Quiver.Path.nil⟩ : TotalPath Q) = some x

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_assoc
decls.doc: Concatenation of indexed paths is associative as a partial operation.
decls.statement:
theorem mul?_assoc (x y z : TotalPath Q) :
    ((x.mul? y).bind fun w => w.mul? z) = (y.mul? z).bind fun w => x.mul? w

decls.name: TauCeti.pathAlgebra
decls.doc:
The path algebra of a quiver `Q` over `k`: the free `k`-module on the paths of `Q`, with
multiplication the concatenation of composable paths in the *later factor first* order, and `0` on
non-composable pairs.

This is a semireducible type synonym so that instance search does not confuse the path
multiplication with the pointwise multiplication of `Finsupp`.
decls.statement: def pathAlgebra (k : Type w) (Q : Type u) [Semiring k] [Quiver.{v} Q] : Type _

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instAddCommMonoidPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : AddCommMonoid (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instModulePathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : Module k (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instInhabitedPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : Inhabited (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single
decls.doc: The basis element of the path algebra attached to a path, with a coefficient.
decls.statement: def single (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (c : k) : pathAlgebra k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_def
decls.doc: A basis path is the corresponding `Finsupp.single`, read through the type synonym.
decls.statement:
theorem single_def (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (c : k) :
    (single x c : pathAlgebra k Q) = Finsupp.single x c

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_zero
decls.doc: A basis path with coefficient zero is zero.
decls.statement: theorem single_zero (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) : (single x (0 : k) : pathAlgebra k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_add
decls.doc: Basis paths are additive in their coefficient.
decls.statement:
theorem single_add (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (c d : k) :
    (single x (c + d) : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x c + single x d

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.smul_single
decls.doc: Scaling a basis path scales its coefficient.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_single (r : k) (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (c : k) :
    r • (single x c : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x (r * c)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.induction_linear
decls.doc: Additive induction on the path algebra: it suffices to treat `0`, sums, and basis paths.
decls.statement:
theorem induction_linear {motive : pathAlgebra k Q → Prop} (f : pathAlgebra k Q)
    (zero : motive 0) (add : ∀ f g, motive f → motive g → motive (f + g))
    (single : ∀ x c, motive (PathAlgebra.single x c)) : motive f

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.singleOption
decls.doc:
`Finsupp.single` at an optional index, the zero function at `none`. It spells the product of
two basis paths uniformly: a single path when they are composable, and `0` otherwise.
decls.statement:
def singleOption (o : Option (Quiver.TotalPath Q)) (c : k) :
    Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.singleOption_none
decls.doc: An absent index contributes nothing.
decls.statement: theorem singleOption_none (c : k) : singleOption (Q := Q) none c = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.singleOption_some
decls.doc: A present index contributes the corresponding basis path.
decls.statement:
theorem singleOption_some (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (c : k) :
    singleOption (some x) c = Finsupp.single x c

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.singleOption_zero
decls.doc: The coefficient zero contributes nothing.
decls.statement:
theorem singleOption_zero (o : Option (Quiver.TotalPath Q)) :
    singleOption o (0 : k) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.singleOption_add
decls.doc: `singleOption` is additive in its coefficient.
decls.statement:
theorem singleOption_add (o : Option (Quiver.TotalPath Q)) (c d : k) :
    singleOption o (c + d) = singleOption o c + singleOption o d

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.smul_singleOption
decls.doc: `singleOption` absorbs scalars into its coefficient.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_singleOption (r : k) (o : Option (Quiver.TotalPath Q)) (c : k) :
    r • singleOption o c = singleOption o (r * c)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'
decls.doc: The multiplication of the path algebra, at the level of finitely supported functions.
decls.statement: def mul' (f g : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_zero_left
decls.doc: The multiplication kills zero on the left.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_zero_left (g : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' (0 : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) g = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_zero_right
decls.doc: The multiplication kills zero on the right.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_zero_right (f : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' f (0 : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_add_left
decls.doc: The multiplication is additive in its left argument.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_add_left (f₁ f₂ g : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' (f₁ + f₂) g = mul' f₁ g + mul' f₂ g

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_add_right
decls.doc: The multiplication is additive in its right argument.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_add_right (f g₁ g₂ : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' f (g₁ + g₂) = mul' f g₁ + mul' f g₂

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_single_single
decls.doc: The multiplication on basis paths is the partial concatenation of their indices.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_single_single (x y : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (a b : k) :
    mul' (Finsupp.single x a) (Finsupp.single y b) = singleOption (x.mul? y) (a * b)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_singleOption_single
decls.doc: Multiplying an optional basis path by a basis path binds the two indices.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_singleOption_single (o : Option (Quiver.TotalPath Q)) (c : k)
    (y : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (b : k) :
    mul' (singleOption o c) (Finsupp.single y b)
      = singleOption (o.bind fun w => w.mul? y) (c * b)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_single_singleOption
decls.doc: Multiplying a basis path by an optional basis path binds the two indices.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_single_singleOption (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (a : k)
    (o : Option (Quiver.TotalPath Q)) (c : k) :
    mul' (Finsupp.single x a) (singleOption o c)
      = singleOption (o.bind fun w => x.mul? w) (a * c)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_assoc
decls.doc: The multiplication is associative, by associativity of path concatenation.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_assoc (f g t : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' (mul' f g) t = mul' f (mul' g t)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.smul_mul'
decls.doc: The multiplication is homogeneous in its left argument.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_mul' (r : k) (f g : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' (r • f) g = r • mul' f g

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instMulPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : Mul (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul_def
decls.doc:
The multiplication of the path algebra is `mul'`, read through the type synonym. This is the
only place the identification is used; every product below is computed from it.
decls.statement: theorem mul_def (f g : pathAlgebra k Q) : f * g = mul' f g

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instNonUnitalNonAssocSemiringPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instNonUnitalSemiringPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : NonUnitalSemiring (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_mul_single
decls.doc:
The defining product of two basis paths: their concatenation, later factor first, when they
are composable, and `0` otherwise.
decls.statement:
theorem single_mul_single (x y : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (a b : k) :
    (single x a * single y b : pathAlgebra k Q)
      = (x.mul? y).elim 0 fun z => single z (a * b)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_mul_single_of_comp
decls.doc: Multiplying two composable basis paths concatenates them, later factor first.
decls.statement:
theorem single_mul_single_of_comp {a b c : Q} (p : _root_.Quiver.Path a b)
    (q : _root_.Quiver.Path c a) (r s : k) :
    (single (⟨a, b, p⟩ : Quiver.TotalPath Q) r * single ⟨c, a, q⟩ s : pathAlgebra k Q)
      = single ⟨c, b, q.comp p⟩ (r * s)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_mul_single_of_not_composable
decls.doc: The product of two basis paths that are not composable vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem single_mul_single_of_not_composable {x y : Quiver.TotalPath Q} (h : y.2.1 ≠ x.1) (r s : k) :
    (single x r * single y s : pathAlgebra k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofPath
decls.doc: The basis element of the path algebra attached to a path.
decls.statement: def ofPath (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) : pathAlgebra k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofPath_eq_single
decls.doc: A path is the basis element it indexes, with coefficient one.
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_eq_single (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) :
    (ofPath x : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofPath_mul_ofPath_of_comp
decls.doc: Two composable paths multiply to their concatenation, later factor first.
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_mul_ofPath_of_comp {a b c : Q} (p : _root_.Quiver.Path a b)
    (q : _root_.Quiver.Path c a) :
    (ofPath (⟨a, b, p⟩ : Quiver.TotalPath Q) * ofPath ⟨c, a, q⟩ : pathAlgebra k Q)
      = ofPath ⟨c, b, q.comp p⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofPath_mul_ofPath_of_not_composable
decls.doc: Two paths that do not meet multiply to zero.
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_mul_ofPath_of_not_composable {x y : Quiver.TotalPath Q} (h : y.2.1 ≠ x.1) :
    (ofPath x * ofPath y : pathAlgebra k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent
decls.doc: The idempotent of the path algebra attached to a vertex: the trivial path at that vertex.
decls.statement: def vertexIdempotent (v : Q) : pathAlgebra k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent_eq_single
decls.doc: The vertex idempotent is the basis element of the trivial path, with coefficient one.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexIdempotent_eq_single (v : Q) :
    vertexIdempotent k v
      = single (⟨v, v, _root_.Quiver.Path.nil⟩ : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (1 : k)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent_mul_single
decls.doc: The vertex idempotent at the target of a path is a left unit for it.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexIdempotent_mul_single (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (r : k) :
    (vertexIdempotent k x.2.1 * single x r : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x r

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_mul_vertexIdempotent
decls.doc: The vertex idempotent at the source of a path is a right unit for it.
decls.statement:
theorem single_mul_vertexIdempotent (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (r : k) :
    (single x r * vertexIdempotent k x.1 : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x r

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent_mul_ofPath
decls.doc: The vertex idempotent at the target of a path is a left unit for its canonical element.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexIdempotent_mul_ofPath {a b : Q} (p : _root_.Quiver.Path a b) :
    (vertexIdempotent k b * ofPath ⟨a, b, p⟩ : pathAlgebra k Q) = ofPath ⟨a, b, p⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofPath_mul_vertexIdempotent
decls.doc: The vertex idempotent at the source of a path is a right unit for its canonical element.
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_mul_vertexIdempotent {a b : Q} (p : _root_.Quiver.Path a b) :
    (ofPath ⟨a, b, p⟩ * vertexIdempotent k a : pathAlgebra k Q) = ofPath ⟨a, b, p⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent_mul_ofPath_of_ne
decls.doc:
A vertex idempotent not at the target of a path annihilates its canonical element on the
left.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexIdempotent_mul_ofPath_of_ne {v : Q} (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (h : v ≠ x.2.1) :
    (vertexIdempotent k v * ofPath x : pathAlgebra k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofPath_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne
decls.doc:
A vertex idempotent not at the source of a path annihilates its canonical element on the
right.
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne {v : Q} (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (h : v ≠ x.1) :
    (ofPath x * vertexIdempotent k v : pathAlgebra k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne
decls.doc: Distinct vertex idempotents are orthogonal.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexIdempotent_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne {u v : Q} (h : u ≠ v) :
    (vertexIdempotent k u * vertexIdempotent k v : pathAlgebra k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.vertexIdempotent_mul_self
decls.doc: The vertex idempotents are idempotent.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexIdempotent_mul_self (v : Q) :
    (vertexIdempotent k v * vertexIdempotent k v : pathAlgebra k Q) = vertexIdempotent k v

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instOnePathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : One (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.one_def
decls.doc:
The unit of the path algebra is the sum of the vertex idempotents: the vertex idempotents are
a decomposition of the unit.
decls.statement: theorem one_def [Fintype Q] : (1 : pathAlgebra k Q) = ∑ v : Q, vertexIdempotent k v

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.one_mul_single
decls.doc: The sum of the vertex idempotents is a left unit on basis paths.
decls.statement:
theorem one_mul_single (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (r : k) :
    ((1 : pathAlgebra k Q) * single x r : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x r

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.single_mul_one
decls.doc: The sum of the vertex idempotents is a right unit on basis paths.
decls.statement:
theorem single_mul_one (x : Quiver.TotalPath Q) (r : k) :
    (single x r * (1 : pathAlgebra k Q) : pathAlgebra k Q) = single x r

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instSemiringPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : Semiring (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instAddCommGroupPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : AddCommGroup (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instRingPathAlgebraOfFinite
decls.statement: instance [Finite Q] : Ring (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.mul'_smul
decls.doc: Over a commutative base the multiplication is homogeneous in its right argument.
decls.statement:
theorem mul'_smul (r : k) (f g : Quiver.TotalPath Q →₀ k) :
    mul' f (r • g) = r • mul' f g

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.instAlgebraPathAlgebra
decls.statement: instance : Algebra k (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.algebraMap_apply
decls.doc: The image of a scalar in the path algebra spreads it over the vertex idempotents.
decls.statement:
theorem algebraMap_apply [Fintype Q] (r : k) :
    algebraMap k (pathAlgebra k Q) r = ∑ v : Q, r • vertexIdempotent k v

decls.name: TauCeti.pathAlgebraBasis
decls.doc: The paths of `Q` are a `k`-basis of the path algebra.
decls.statement:
def pathAlgebraBasis :
    Module.Basis (Quiver.TotalPath Q) k (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_pathAlgebraBasis
decls.doc: The path basis consists of the basis paths.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_pathAlgebraBasis :
    ⇑(pathAlgebraBasis k Q)
      = fun x : Quiver.TotalPath Q => (PathAlgebra.ofPath x : pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.module_finite_pathAlgebra
decls.doc: The path algebra of a quiver with finitely many paths is a finite `k`-module.
decls.statement:
theorem module_finite_pathAlgebra [Finite (Quiver.TotalPath Q)] :
    Module.Finite k (pathAlgebra k Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_pathAlgebra
decls.doc: The dimension of the path algebra is the number of paths of `Q`.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_pathAlgebra [Fintype (Quiver.TotalPath Q)] :
    Module.finrank k (pathAlgebra k Q) = Fintype.card (Quiver.TotalPath Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofArrow
decls.doc: The path-algebra element attached to an arrow.
decls.statement: def ofArrow {a b : Q} (e : a ⟶ b) : pathAlgebra k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.ofArrow_eq_ofPath
decls.doc: An arrow is the basis element indexed by its length-one path.
decls.statement:
theorem ofArrow_eq_ofPath {a b : Q} (e : a ⟶ b) :
    (ofArrow e : pathAlgebra k Q) = ofPath ⟨a, b, e.toPath⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.adjoin_vertexIdempotents_union_arrows
decls.doc:
The vertex idempotents and arrows generate the path algebra. Vertex idempotents are necessary:
arrows alone do not generate the path algebra of, for example, a discrete multi-vertex quiver.
decls.statement:
theorem adjoin_vertexIdempotents_union_arrows :
    Algebra.adjoin k
        (Set.range (vertexIdempotent k) ∪
          Set.range fun e : Σ a b : Q, a ⟶ b => ofArrow e.2.2) =
      ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.oneLoopLinearEquiv
decls.statement:
def oneLoopLinearEquiv :
    pathAlgebra k Quiver.OneLoop ≃ₗ[k] AddMonoidAlgebra k ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.oneLoopLinearEquiv_ofPath
decls.statement:
theorem oneLoopLinearEquiv_ofPath (x : Quiver.TotalPath Quiver.OneLoop) :
    oneLoopLinearEquiv k (PathAlgebra.ofPath x) =
      AddMonoidAlgebra.single (Quiver.OneLoop.totalPathEquivNat x) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.oneLoopLinearEquiv_single
decls.statement:
theorem oneLoopLinearEquiv_single (x : Quiver.TotalPath Quiver.OneLoop) (c : k) :
    oneLoopLinearEquiv k (single x c) =
      AddMonoidAlgebra.single (Quiver.OneLoop.totalPathEquivNat x) c

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.oneLoopLinearEquiv_map_one
decls.statement:
theorem oneLoopLinearEquiv_map_one :
    oneLoopLinearEquiv k (1 : pathAlgebra k Quiver.OneLoop) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.oneLoopLinearEquiv_map_mul
decls.statement:
theorem oneLoopLinearEquiv_map_mul
    (f g : pathAlgebra k Quiver.OneLoop) :
    oneLoopLinearEquiv k (f * g) = oneLoopLinearEquiv k f * oneLoopLinearEquiv k g

decls.name: TauCeti.PathAlgebra.oneLoopAlgEquiv
decls.doc:
The path algebra of the quiver with one vertex and one loop is the additive monoid algebra on
`ℕ` (equivalently, the polynomial algebra in one variable).
decls.statement:
def oneLoopAlgEquiv :
    pathAlgebra k Quiver.OneLoop ≃ₐ[k] AddMonoidAlgebra k ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.not_finiteDimensional_pathAlgebra_oneLoop
decls.doc: Over a division ring, the path algebra of the one-loop quiver is infinite-dimensional.
decls.statement:
theorem not_finiteDimensional_pathAlgebra_oneLoop
    (k : Type w) [DivisionRing k] :
    ¬ FiniteDimensional k (pathAlgebra k Quiver.OneLoop)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.exists_isSink
decls.doc:
A nonempty finite acyclic quiver has a sink: were every vertex to carry an outgoing arrow,
paths could be extended indefinitely, past the bound of
`TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.length_lt_card`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsAcyclic.exists_isSink [Finite V] [Nonempty V] (h : IsAcyclic V) :
    ∃ i : V, IsSink i

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.exists_isSource
decls.doc: A nonempty finite acyclic quiver has a source.
decls.statement:
theorem IsAcyclic.exists_isSource [Finite V] [Nonempty V] (h : IsAcyclic V) :
    ∃ i : V, IsSource i

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.exists_path_of_isSink
decls.doc:
Away from a sink, a path of the reflected quiver comes from a path of the original quiver of
the same length; in particular it cannot reach the sink.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_path_of_isSink {i : V} (h : IsSink i) {a b : Reflect V i} (ha : a ≠ i)
    (p : Path a b) : b ≠ i ∧ ∃ q : @Path V _ a b, q.length = p.length

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.reflect_of_isSink
decls.doc: Reflecting an acyclic quiver at a sink leaves it acyclic.
decls.statement:
theorem IsAcyclic.reflect_of_isSink {i : V} (hV : IsAcyclic V) (h : IsSink i) :
    IsAcyclic (Reflect V i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.exists_path_of_isSource
decls.doc:
Away from a source, a path of the reflected quiver comes from a path of the original quiver of
the same length; in particular it cannot start at the source.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_path_of_isSource {i : V} (h : IsSource i) {a b : Reflect V i} (hb : b ≠ i)
    (p : Path a b) : a ≠ i ∧ ∃ q : @Path V _ a b, q.length = p.length

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsAcyclic.reflect_of_isSource
decls.doc: Reflecting an acyclic quiver at a source leaves it acyclic.
decls.statement:
theorem IsAcyclic.reflect_of_isSource {i : V} (hV : IsAcyclic V) (h : IsSource i) :
    IsAcyclic (Reflect V i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSink
decls.doc: A vertex of a quiver is a *sink* if no arrow leaves it.
decls.statement: def Quiver.IsSink (i : V) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSource
decls.doc: A vertex of a quiver is a *source* if no arrow enters it.
decls.statement: def Quiver.IsSource (i : V) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSink_def
decls.doc: The defining condition for a sink.
decls.statement: theorem IsSink_def (i : V) : IsSink i ↔ ∀ b : V, IsEmpty (i ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSource_def
decls.doc: The defining condition for a source.
decls.statement: theorem IsSource_def (i : V) : IsSource i ↔ ∀ a : V, IsEmpty (a ⟶ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSink.isEmpty_hom
decls.doc: No arrow leaves a sink.
decls.statement: theorem IsSink.isEmpty_hom {i : V} (h : IsSink i) (b : V) : IsEmpty (i ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSource.isEmpty_hom
decls.doc: No arrow enters a source.
decls.statement: theorem IsSource.isEmpty_hom {i : V} (h : IsSource i) (a : V) : IsEmpty (a ⟶ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSink.isEmpty_hom_self
decls.doc: A sink carries no loop.
decls.statement: theorem IsSink.isEmpty_hom_self {i : V} (h : IsSink i) : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSource.isEmpty_hom_self
decls.doc: A source carries no loop.
decls.statement: theorem IsSource.isEmpty_hom_self {i : V} (h : IsSource i) : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSink.eq_of_path
decls.doc: A path out of a sink is trivial, so it ends where it started.
decls.statement: theorem IsSink.eq_of_path {i b : V} (h : IsSink i) (p : Path i b) : i = b

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSource.eq_of_path
decls.doc: A path into a source is trivial, so it starts where it ends.
decls.statement: theorem IsSource.eq_of_path {i a : V} (h : IsSource i) (p : Path a i) : a = i

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.reflectHom
decls.doc:
The arrows from `a` to `b` in the quiver obtained from `V` by reversing every arrow incident
to the vertex `i`. Arrows between two vertices other than `i` are untouched, an arrow `b ⟶ i`
becomes an arrow `i ⟶ b`, and the loops at `i` are reversed among themselves.
decls.statement: def reflectHom (i a b : V) : Type v

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.reflectHom_left
decls.doc: The arrows out of `i` in the reflected quiver are the arrows into `i` in the original one.
decls.statement: theorem reflectHom_left (i b : V) : reflectHom i i b = (b ⟶ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.reflectHom_right
decls.doc: The arrows into `i` in the reflected quiver are the arrows out of `i` in the original one.
decls.statement: theorem reflectHom_right (i a : V) : reflectHom i a i = (i ⟶ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.reflectHom_of_ne_of_ne
decls.doc: Away from `i` the reflected quiver has the arrows of the original one.
decls.statement:
theorem reflectHom_of_ne_of_ne {i a b : V} (ha : a ≠ i) (hb : b ≠ i) :
    reflectHom i a b = (a ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.instFintypeReflectHom
decls.statement:
instance instFintypeReflectHom [∀ a b : V, Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (i a b : V) :
    Fintype (reflectHom i a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.Reflect
decls.doc:
The reflection of a quiver at a vertex `i`: a type synonym for the vertex type, carrying the
quiver in which every arrow incident to `i` is reversed.
decls.statement: def Reflect (V : Type u) (_i : V) : Type u

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.reflectQuiver
decls.statement: instance reflectQuiver (i : V) : _root_.Quiver.{v} (Reflect V i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.instDecidableEqReflect
decls.statement: instance (i : V) [DecidableEq V] : DecidableEq (Reflect V i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.instFintypeReflect
decls.statement: instance (i : V) [Fintype V] : Fintype (Reflect V i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.instNonemptyReflect
decls.statement: instance (i : V) [Nonempty V] : Nonempty (Reflect V i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.instFintypeHomReflect
decls.statement:
instance (i : V) [∀ a b : V, Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (a b : Reflect V i) :
    Fintype (a ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.hom_reflect
decls.doc:
The arrow types of the reflected quiver are the ones computed by
`TauCeti.Quiver.reflectHom`.
decls.statement: theorem hom_reflect (i : V) (a b : Reflect V i) : (a ⟶ b) = reflectHom i a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSink.isSource_reflect
decls.doc: Reflecting at a sink turns it into a source: no arrow of the reflected quiver enters `i`.
decls.statement: theorem IsSink.isSource_reflect {i : V} (h : IsSink i) : @IsSource (Reflect V i) _ i

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.IsSource.isSink_reflect
decls.doc: Reflecting at a source turns it into a sink: no arrow of the reflected quiver leaves `i`.
decls.statement: theorem IsSource.isSink_reflect {i : V} (h : IsSource i) : @IsSink (Reflect V i) _ i

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.hom_reflect_reflect
decls.doc:
Reflecting twice at the same vertex restores the original arrow types: reflection at a vertex
is an involution on quivers.

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.card_reflectHom_left
decls.doc: The reflected quiver has as many arrows `i ⟶ b` as the original has arrows `b ⟶ i`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_reflectHom_left (i b : V) :
    Fintype.card (reflectHom i i b) = Fintype.card (b ⟶ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.card_reflectHom_right
decls.doc: The reflected quiver has as many arrows `a ⟶ i` as the original has arrows `i ⟶ a`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_reflectHom_right (i a : V) :
    Fintype.card (reflectHom i a i) = Fintype.card (i ⟶ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.card_reflectHom_of_ne_of_ne
decls.doc: Away from `i` the reflected quiver has the same arrow counts as the original.
decls.statement:
theorem card_reflectHom_of_ne_of_ne {i a b : V} (ha : a ≠ i) (hb : b ≠ i) :
    Fintype.card (reflectHom i a b) = Fintype.card (a ⟶ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.card_reflectHom_add_swap
decls.doc:
Reflection at a vertex preserves the number of arrows joining any two vertices in either
direction: it changes the orientation of the quiver, not its underlying graph.
decls.statement:
theorem card_reflectHom_add_swap (i a b : V) :
    Fintype.card (reflectHom i a b) + Fintype.card (reflectHom i b a)
      = Fintype.card (a ⟶ b) + Fintype.card (b ⟶ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Quiver.card_reflectHom_right_of_isSink
decls.doc: Reflecting at a sink leaves no arrow into `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_reflectHom_right_of_isSink {i : V} (h : IsSink i) (a : V) :
    Fintype.card (reflectHom i a i) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection
decls.doc:
The simple reflection `sᵢ` at a vertex `i`, acting on dimension vectors by
`d ↦ d - ⟨αᵢ, d⟩ αᵢ` for the polarized Tits form and the simple dimension vector
`αᵢ = Pi.single i 1`.

No hypothesis on `i` is imposed here, following `Module.preReflection`; the reflection identities
hold at a loopless vertex, where `⟨αᵢ, αᵢ⟩ = 2`, and there `vertexReflection` packages this map
as an automorphism.
decls.statement: def vertexPreReflection (i : Q) : Module.End ℤ (Q → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_apply
decls.doc: The defining formula for the simple reflection at a vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_apply (i : Q) (d : Q → ℤ) :
    vertexPreReflection Q i d = d - titsPolarForm Q (Pi.single i 1) d • Pi.single i 1

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_apply_of_ne
decls.doc: Away from `i`, the simple reflection at `i` leaves a dimension vector unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_apply_of_ne (i : Q) (d : Q → ℤ) {v : Q} (hv : v ≠ i) :
    vertexPreReflection Q i d v = d v

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_apply_self
decls.doc: The coordinate of the simple reflection at the reflected vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_apply_self (i : Q) (d : Q → ℤ) :
    vertexPreReflection Q i d i
      = -d i + ∑ v : Q, ((Fintype.card (i ⟶ v) : ℤ) + (Fintype.card (v ⟶ i) : ℤ)) * d v

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_apply_self_of_isEmpty
decls.doc:
At a loopless vertex the reflected coordinate is the classical formula
`-dᵢ + ∑_{v ≠ i} (#(i ⟶ v) + #(v ⟶ i)) d_v`, the sum running over the neighbours of `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_apply_self_of_isEmpty {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) (d : Q → ℤ) :
    vertexPreReflection Q i d i
      = -d i + ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
          ((Fintype.card (i ⟶ v) : ℤ) + (Fintype.card (v ⟶ i) : ℤ)) * d v

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_single_self
decls.doc:
The simple reflection at a loopless vertex negates the corresponding simple dimension
vector.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_single_self {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) :
    vertexPreReflection Q i (Pi.single i 1) = -Pi.single i 1

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_single_of_ne
decls.doc:
The simple reflection at `i` adds a multiple of `αᵢ` to any other simple dimension vector, the
multiple being the number of arrows joining the two vertices in either direction.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_single_of_ne (i : Q) {j : Q} (hj : j ≠ i) :
    vertexPreReflection Q i (Pi.single j 1)
      = Pi.single j 1
        + ((Fintype.card (i ⟶ j) : ℤ) + (Fintype.card (j ⟶ i) : ℤ)) • Pi.single i 1

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_apply_of_titsPolarForm_eq_zero
decls.doc:
The simple reflection fixes every dimension vector orthogonal to `αᵢ` for the polarized Tits
form.

decls.name: TauCeti.involutive_vertexPreReflection
decls.doc: The simple reflection at a loopless vertex is an involution.
decls.statement:
theorem involutive_vertexPreReflection {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) :
    Function.Involutive (vertexPreReflection Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexReflection
decls.doc:
The simple reflection at a loopless vertex, as a linear automorphism of the dimension-vector
lattice.
decls.statement: def vertexReflection {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) : (Q → ℤ) ≃ₗ[ℤ] (Q → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_vertexReflection
decls.statement:
theorem coe_vertexReflection {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) :
    ⇑(vertexReflection Q h) = ⇑(vertexPreReflection Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexReflection_symm
decls.doc: The simple reflection at a loopless vertex is its own inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexReflection_symm {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) :
    (vertexReflection Q h).symm = vertexReflection Q h

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_vertexPreReflection
decls.doc: The simple reflection at a loopless vertex preserves the Tits form.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_vertexPreReflection {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) (d : Q → ℤ) :
    titsForm Q (vertexPreReflection Q i d) = titsForm Q d

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_vertexPreReflection
decls.doc: The simple reflection at a loopless vertex preserves the polarized Tits form.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_vertexPreReflection {i : Q} (h : IsEmpty (i ⟶ i)) (d e : Q → ℤ) :
    titsPolarForm Q (vertexPreReflection Q i d) (vertexPreReflection Q i e)
      = titsPolarForm Q d e

decls.name: TauCeti.bijOn_vertexPreReflection
decls.doc:
The simple reflection at a loopless vertex permutes every level set of the Tits form; taking
the level `1` this says that it permutes the roots of `Q`.

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_sum_eq_of_add_swap_eq
decls.doc: A double sum over a finite type is determined by the symmetrization of its summand.

decls.name: TauCeti.sub_sum_sum_eq_of_reflect_data
decls.doc:
The arithmetic heart of the reflection identity for the Euler form. Here `N` plays the role of
the arrow-count matrix of the quiver, whose `i`-th row vanishes because `i` is a sink, and `N'`
that of the quiver reflected at `i`; `d'` and `e'` are the reflections of `d` and `e`.
decls.statement:
theorem sub_sum_sum_eq_of_reflect_data {W : Type*} [Fintype W] (i : W)
    (N N' : W → W → ℤ) (d e d' e' : W → ℤ)
    (hN : ∀ b : W, N i b = 0) (hN'row : ∀ b : W, N' i b = N b i)
    (hN'col : ∀ a : W, N' a i = 0)
    (hN' : ∀ a b : W, a ≠ i → b ≠ i → N' a b = N a b)
    (hd : ∀ w : W, w ≠ i → d' w = d w) (he : ∀ w : W, w ≠ i → e' w = e w)
    (hdi : d' i = (∑ w : W, N w i * d w) - d i)
    (hei : e' i = (∑ w : W, N w i * e w) - e i) :
    (∑ w : W, d' w * e' w) - ∑ a : W, ∑ b : W, N' a b * (d' a * e' b)
      = (∑ w : W, d w * e w) - ∑ a : W, ∑ b : W, N a b * (d a * e b)

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_sum_transpose
decls.doc: Transposing an arrow-count matrix exchanges the two arguments of its Euler-form sum.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_sum_transpose {W : Type*} [Fintype W] (N : W → W → ℤ) (d e : W → ℤ) :
    ∑ a : W, ∑ b : W, N b a * (e a * d b) = ∑ a : W, ∑ b : W, N a b * (d a * e b)

decls.name: TauCeti.sub_sum_sum_eq_of_reflect_data_of_source
decls.doc:
The source-oriented version of `sub_sum_sum_eq_of_reflect_data`, obtained by transposing the
two arrow-count matrices and exchanging the arguments of the Euler form.
decls.statement:
theorem sub_sum_sum_eq_of_reflect_data_of_source {W : Type*} [Fintype W] (i : W)
    (N N' : W → W → ℤ) (d e d' e' : W → ℤ)
    (hN : ∀ a : W, N a i = 0) (hN'col : ∀ a : W, N' a i = N i a)
    (hN'row : ∀ b : W, N' i b = 0)
    (hN' : ∀ a b : W, a ≠ i → b ≠ i → N' a b = N a b)
    (hd : ∀ w : W, w ≠ i → d' w = d w) (he : ∀ w : W, w ≠ i → e' w = e w)
    (hdi : d' i = (∑ w : W, N i w * d w) - d i)
    (hei : e' i = (∑ w : W, N i w * e w) - e i) :
    (∑ w : W, d' w * e' w) - ∑ a : W, ∑ b : W, N' a b * (d' a * e' b)
      = (∑ w : W, d w * e w) - ∑ a : W, ∑ b : W, N a b * (d a * e b)

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_reflect_eq_sum_card
decls.doc:
`TauCeti.eulerForm_eq_sum_card` for the reflected quiver, with the sums re-indexed by the
vertex type `V` itself and the arrow counts written as `TauCeti.Quiver.reflectHom` counts.

`Quiver.Reflect V i` is a type synonym for `V`, so this is the generic expansion up to
unfolding that synonym and its `Fintype` instances; the point of stating it is that `linarith`
and `ring` compare atoms only up to reducible transparency, and so cannot see a
`Quiver.Reflect V i`-indexed sum and a `V`-indexed one as the same term. Where a tactic does
unfold the synonym (`refine`, in `TauCeti.eulerForm_reflect_vertexPreReflection` below), the
generic lemma is used directly instead.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_reflect_eq_sum_card (i : V) (d e : V → ℤ) :
    eulerForm (Quiver.Reflect V i) d e =
      (∑ w : V, d w * e w)
        - ∑ a : V, ∑ b : V, (Fintype.card (Quiver.reflectHom i a b) : ℤ) * (d a * e b)

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_sum_card_reflectHom
decls.doc:
Reflecting at a vertex leaves unchanged every arrow-weighted double sum whose weight is
symmetric in the two vertices, because reflection preserves the underlying graph.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_sum_card_reflectHom (i : V) (S : V → V → ℤ) (hS : ∀ a b : V, S a b = S b a) :
    ∑ a : V, ∑ b : V, (Fintype.card (Quiver.reflectHom i a b) : ℤ) * S a b
      = ∑ a : V, ∑ b : V, (Fintype.card (a ⟶ b) : ℤ) * S a b

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_reflect
decls.doc:
Reflecting at a vertex leaves the Tits form unchanged: the Tits form depends only on the
underlying graph of the quiver, not on its orientation.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_reflect (i : V) (d : V → ℤ) :
    titsForm (Quiver.Reflect V i) d = titsForm V d

decls.name: TauCeti.titsPolarForm_reflect
decls.doc: Reflecting at a vertex leaves the polarized Tits form unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem titsPolarForm_reflect (i : V) (d e : V → ℤ) :
    titsPolarForm (Quiver.Reflect V i) d e = titsPolarForm V d e

decls.name: TauCeti.vertexPreReflection_reflect_apply
decls.doc:
Reflecting at a vertex leaves every simple reflection on dimension vectors unchanged, since
these are built from the polarized Tits form, which reflection preserves.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexPreReflection_reflect_apply (i j : V) (d : V → ℤ) (w : V) :
    vertexPreReflection (Quiver.Reflect V i) j d w = vertexPreReflection V j d w

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_reflect_vertexPreReflection
decls.doc:
At a sink `i`, the Euler form of the quiver reflected at `i` is carried to the Euler form of
the original quiver by the simple reflection `sᵢ` on dimension vectors:
`⟨sᵢ d, sᵢ e⟩` for `Q.reflect i` equals `⟨d, e⟩` for `Q`.

This is the numerical identity behind the Bernstein-Gelfand-Ponomarev reflection functor at a
sink, which realizes `sᵢ` on dimension vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_reflect_vertexPreReflection {i : V} (h : Quiver.IsSink i) (d e : V → ℤ) :
    eulerForm (Quiver.Reflect V i) (vertexPreReflection V i d) (vertexPreReflection V i e)
      = eulerForm V d e

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_reflect_vertexPreReflection_of_isSource
decls.doc:
At a source `i`, the Euler form of the quiver reflected at `i` is carried to the Euler form of
the original quiver by the simple reflection `sᵢ` on dimension vectors:
`⟨sᵢ d, sᵢ e⟩` for `Q.reflect i` equals `⟨d, e⟩` for `Q`.

This is the numerical identity behind the Bernstein-Gelfand-Ponomarev reflection functor at a
source, which realizes `sᵢ` on dimension vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_reflect_vertexPreReflection_of_isSource {i : V} (h : Quiver.IsSource i)
    (d e : V → ℤ) :
    eulerForm (Quiver.Reflect V i) (vertexPreReflection V i d) (vertexPreReflection V i e)
      = eulerForm V d e

decls.name: TauCeti.QuiverRep
decls.doc: The category of representations of a quiver `Q` over a field `k`.
decls.statement: abbrev QuiverRep (k : Type u) (Q : Type v) [Field k] [Quiver Q]

decls.name: TauCeti.QuiverRep.map_nil
decls.doc:
**The trivial path acts as the identity.** In the free path category `Quiver.Path.nil` is the
identity morphism, so a representation carries it to the identity map. Stated separately because
`Quiver.Path.nil` is what appears when a path is taken apart, while `CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id`
is phrased in terms of `𝟙`: the two agree only by unfolding the semireducible
`CategoryTheory.Paths`, so `simp only [Functor.map_id]` makes no progress on a goal about
`Quiver.Path.nil`, and `simp` cannot compute the action of the trivial path without this lemma.
Mathlib states the same restatement for
functors of the form `CategoryTheory.Paths.lift φ`, as `CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_nil`; that lemma
does not apply to a general representation.
decls.title: The trivial path acts as the identity
decls.statement:
theorem QuiverRep.map_nil {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver.{w} Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q)
    (a : Q) : M.map (Quiver.Path.nil : Quiver.Path a a) = 𝟙 (M.obj a)

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector
decls.doc:
The `Module.finrank` dimension vector of a quiver representation, indexed by the vertices of the
quiver. An infinite-dimensional component has value `0` by convention.
decls.statement: def dimVector (M : QuiverRep k Q) : Q → ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_apply
decls.doc:
The value of the dimension vector at a vertex is the `Module.finrank` of the corresponding
vector space.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_apply (M : QuiverRep k Q) (i : Q) :
    dimVector M i = Module.finrank k (M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i))

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_eq_of_iso
decls.doc: Isomorphic quiver representations have the same dimension vector.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_eq_of_iso {M N : QuiverRep k Q} (e : M ≅ N) :
    dimVector M = dimVector N

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_zero
decls.doc: The zero representation has zero dimension vector.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_zero :
    dimVector (0 : QuiverRep k Q) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_biprod
decls.doc:
The dimension vector is additive on biproducts of pointwise finite-dimensional
representations.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_biprod (M N : QuiverRep k Q)
    (hM : ∀ i : Q, FiniteDimensional k (M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)))
    (hN : ∀ i : Q, FiniteDimensional k (N.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i))) :
    dimVector (M ⊞ N) = dimVector M + dimVector N

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_add_of_shortExact
decls.doc:
In a short exact sequence of pointwise finite-dimensional quiver representations, the middle
dimension vector is the sum of the outer dimension vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_add_of_shortExact {S : ShortComplex (QuiverRep k Q)} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : ∀ i : Q, FiniteDimensional k (S.X₁.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)))
    (h₃ : ∀ i : Q, FiniteDimensional k (S.X₃.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i))) :
    dimVector S.X₂ = dimVector S.X₁ + dimVector S.X₃

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRep
decls.doc:
**The injective representation at a vertex** `Iᵢ`: the `k`-valued functions on the paths
`j → i` at the vertex `j`, an arrow acting by prepending itself to a path. Under the identification
of representations with left modules over the path algebra this is the `k`-dual `D(eᵢ · kQ)` of the
right ideal spanned by the paths ending at `i`.
decls.title: The injective representation at a vertex
decls.statement: def indecInjRep (i : Q) : QuiverRep k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRep_map_toPath
decls.doc:
An arrow acts on `Iᵢ` by prepending it to a path. Private: `indecInjRep_map_apply` is the
public, element-level form, and is what every later proof uses.
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRep_map_toPath (i : Q) {a b : Q} (e : a ⟶ b) :
    (indecInjRep k Q i).map e.toPath
      = ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.funLeft k k fun q : Quiver.Path b i ↦ e.toPath.comp q)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRep_map_apply
decls.doc:
**A path acts on `Iᵢ` by precomposition**: the value of `p · x` on a path `q : b → i` is the
value of `x` on the concatenation `p.comp q`.
decls.title: A path acts on `Iᵢ` by precomposition
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRep_map_apply (i : Q) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b)
    (x : Quiver.Path a i → k) (q : Quiver.Path b i) :
    (indecInjRep k Q i).map p x q = x (p.comp q)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_indecInjRep_obj
decls.doc:
The dimension of the vector space `Iᵢ` puts at `j` is the number of paths `j → i`. With
infinitely many such paths both sides are `0`, by the conventions for `Module.finrank` and
`Nat.card`.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_indecInjRep_obj (i j : Q) :
    Module.finrank k ((indecInjRep k Q i).obj j) = Nat.card (Quiver.Path j i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_indecInjRep_obj
decls.statement:
instance finiteDimensional_indecInjRep_obj (i j : Q) [Finite (Quiver.Path j i)] :
    FiniteDimensional k ((indecInjRep k Q i).obj j)

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_indecInjRep
decls.doc:
The dimension vector of `Iᵢ` counts, at each vertex, the paths from it to `i`. Together with
`TauCeti.dimVector_indecProjRep` this says that the dimension vectors of the injectives are the
transposes of the dimension vectors of the projectives.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_indecInjRep (i j : Q) :
    dimVector (indecInjRep k Q i) j = Nat.card (Quiver.Path j i)

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_indecInjRep_eq_dimVector_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
The dimension vector of `Iᵢ` is the transpose of the dimension vector of `Pⱼ`: both count the
paths `j → i`.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_indecInjRep_eq_dimVector_indecProjRep (i j : Q) :
    dimVector (indecInjRep k Q i) j = dimVector (indecProjRep k Q j) i

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHom
decls.doc:
The morphism `M ⟶ Iᵢ` determined by a linear functional `φ` on `M` at the vertex `i`: at the
vertex `j` it sends `x` to the function reading off `φ` of the action of a path `j → i` on `x`.

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHom_app_apply
decls.doc:
The morphism attached to `φ : Module.Dual k Mᵢ` sends `x` at the vertex `j` to the function
whose value on a path `q : j → i` is `φ` of the action of `q` on `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRepHom_app_apply (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q)
    (φ : Module.Dual k (M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i))) (j : Q)
    (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj j)) (q : Quiver.Path j i) :
    (indecInjRepHom i M φ).app ((Paths.of Q).obj j) x q = φ (M.map q x)

decls.name: TauCeti.hom_indecInjRep_app_apply
decls.doc:
**A morphism into `Iᵢ` is determined by its value on the trivial path at `i`**: naturality
propagates that single functional to every vertex.
decls.title: A morphism into `Iᵢ` is determined by its value on the trivial path at `i`
decls.statement:
theorem hom_indecInjRep_app_apply (i : Q) {M : QuiverRep k Q} (f : M ⟶ indecInjRep k Q i) (j : Q)
    (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj j)) (q : Quiver.Path j i) :
    f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj j) x q =
      f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i) (M.map q x) Quiver.Path.nil

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHom_app_nil_self
decls.doc: A morphism into `Iᵢ` is recovered from the functional it induces at `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRepHom_app_nil_self {i : Q} {M : QuiverRep k Q} (f : M ⟶ indecInjRep k Q i) :
    indecInjRepHom i M
      (LinearMap.proj Quiver.Path.nil ∘ₗ (f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i)).hom) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHomEquiv
decls.doc:
**`Iᵢ` represents the dual of evaluation at `i`.** A morphism into `Iᵢ` is determined by, and
can be prescribed by, the linear functional reading off its value on the trivial path at `i`; the
bijection is `k`-linear. This is the exact dual of `TauCeti.indecProjRepHomEquiv`.
decls.title: `Iᵢ` represents the dual of evaluation at `i`
decls.statement:
def indecInjRepHomEquiv (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q) :
    (M ⟶ indecInjRep k Q i) ≃ₗ[k] Module.Dual k (M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i))

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHomEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRepHomEquiv_apply (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q) (f : M ⟶ indecInjRep k Q i)
    (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)) :
    indecInjRepHomEquiv i M f x =
      f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i) x Quiver.Path.nil

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHomEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRepHomEquiv_symm_apply (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q)
    (φ : Module.Dual k (M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i))) :
    (indecInjRepHomEquiv i M).symm φ = indecInjRepHom i M φ

decls.name: TauCeti.indecInjRepHomEquiv_comp
decls.doc:
The universal property is natural in the source: precomposition with `g` corresponds to
precomposition of functionals with `g` at `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecInjRepHomEquiv_comp (i : Q) {M N : QuiverRep k Q} (g : M ⟶ N)
    (f : N ⟶ indecInjRep k Q i) :
    indecInjRepHomEquiv i M (g ≫ f) =
      indecInjRepHomEquiv i N f ∘ₗ (g.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i)).hom

decls.name: TauCeti.injective_indecInjRep
decls.doc:
**The representations `Iᵢ` are injective.** A morphism into `Iᵢ` is a single linear functional
on the source at `i`, a monomorphism of representations is injective there, and a linear functional
extends along an injective linear map of vector spaces.
decls.title: The representations `Iᵢ` are injective
decls.statement: instance injective_indecInjRep (i : Q) : Injective (indecInjRep k Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_hom_indecInjRep
decls.doc:
Morphisms into `Iᵢ` are as many as the linear functionals on the source at `i`: the dimension
of `Hom(M, Iᵢ)` is the `i`-th entry of the dimension vector of `M`.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_hom_indecInjRep (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q) :
    Module.finrank k (M ⟶ indecInjRep k Q i) = dimVector M i

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_hom_indecInjRep_indecInjRep
decls.doc:
**The path-counting form of the Cartan matrix, read on injectives**: the dimension of
`Hom(Iᵢ, Iⱼ)` is the number of paths `j → i`, the same count as for `Hom(Pⱼ, Pᵢ)`.
decls.title: The path-counting form of the Cartan matrix, read on injectives
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_hom_indecInjRep_indecInjRep (i j : Q) :
    Module.finrank k (indecInjRep k Q i ⟶ indecInjRep k Q j) = Nat.card (Quiver.Path j i)

decls.name: TauCeti.not_isZero_indecInjRep
decls.doc:
The representation `Iᵢ` is nonzero: the function that is `1` on every path is a nonzero element
of `(Iᵢ)_i`, since the trivial path is one of them.
decls.statement: theorem not_isZero_indecInjRep (i : Q) : ¬ IsZero (indecInjRep k Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_end_indecProjRep_of_isAcyclic
decls.doc:
Over an acyclic quiver the endomorphism algebra of `Pᵢ` is one-dimensional, the trivial path at
`i` being the only path `i → i`: the projective `Pᵢ` is a brick.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_end_indecProjRep_of_isAcyclic (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic Q) (i : Q) :
    Module.finrank k (indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ indecProjRep k Q i) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_of_isAcyclic
decls.doc:
**Over an acyclic quiver the dimension vector of `Pᵢ` is a root of the Tits form**: its Tits
norm is `1`, the trivial path being the only closed path at `i`. Acyclicity also supplies the
finiteness of the paths out of `i`, by `TauCeti.finite_paths_of_isAcyclic`, so no path-finiteness
hypothesis is needed.
decls.title: Over an acyclic quiver the dimension vector of `Pᵢ` is a root of the Tits form
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_of_isAcyclic [Fintype Q] [∀ a b : Q, Fintype (a ⟶ b)]
    (h : Quiver.IsAcyclic Q) (i : Q) :
    titsForm Q (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) v : ℤ)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRep
decls.doc:
**The projective representation at a vertex** `Pᵢ`: the free `k`-module on the paths `i → j`
at the vertex `j`, an arrow acting by appending itself to a path. Under the identification of
representations with left modules over the path algebra this is the left ideal `kQ · eᵢ`.
decls.title: The projective representation at a vertex
decls.statement: def indecProjRep (i : Q) : QuiverRep k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRep_map_toPath
decls.doc:
An arrow acts on `Pᵢ` by appending it to a path. Private: its statement names the underlying
finitely supported functions, which the public API hides behind `indecProjRepBasis`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRep_map_toPath (i : Q) {a b : Q} (e : a ⟶ b) :
    (indecProjRep k Q i).map e.toPath
      = ModuleCat.ofHom (Finsupp.lmapDomain k k fun p : Quiver.Path i a ↦ p.cons e)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRep_map_single
decls.doc:
A path carries the basis element of `q : Quiver.Path i a` in `(Pᵢ)_a` to the basis element of
the concatenation `q.comp p`. Private: `indecProjRep_map_basis` is its public form.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRep_map_single (i : Q) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b)
    (q : Quiver.Path i a) (c : k) :
    (indecProjRep k Q i).map p (Finsupp.single q c) = Finsupp.single (q.comp p) c

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRep_map
decls.doc:
A path acts on `Pᵢ` by concatenation on the right. Private: it is the `Finsupp.lmapDomain`
form of `indecProjRep_map_basis`, used below to get at `Finsupp.lmapDomain_linearCombination`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRep_map (i : Q) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) :
    (indecProjRep k Q i).map p
      = ModuleCat.ofHom (Finsupp.lmapDomain k k fun q : Quiver.Path i a ↦ q.comp p)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepBasis
decls.doc:
The paths `i → j` are a `k`-basis of the vector space that `Pᵢ` puts at `j`. This is the handle
on `(Pᵢ)_j`: the construction of `Pᵢ` is opaque, and the lemmas below name the elements of `(Pᵢ)_j`
through this basis.
decls.statement:
def indecProjRepBasis (i j : Q) :
    Module.Basis (Quiver.Path i j) k ((indecProjRep k Q i).obj j)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRep_map_basis
decls.doc:
**A path acts on `Pᵢ` by concatenation**: it carries the basis vector of a path `q : i → a` to
the basis vector of the concatenation `q.comp p`.
decls.title: A path acts on `Pᵢ` by concatenation
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRep_map_basis (i : Q) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) (q : Quiver.Path i a) :
    (indecProjRep k Q i).map p (indecProjRepBasis k i a q) = indecProjRepBasis k i b (q.comp p)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_indecProjRep_obj
decls.statement:
instance finiteDimensional_indecProjRep_obj (i j : Q) [Finite (Quiver.Path i j)] :
    FiniteDimensional k ((indecProjRep k Q i).obj j)

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
The dimension vector of `Pᵢ` counts, at each vertex, the paths from `i` to it. With infinitely
many paths `i → j` both sides are `0`, by the conventions for `Module.finrank` and `Nat.card`.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_indecProjRep (i j : Q) :
    dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) j = Nat.card (Quiver.Path i j)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHom
decls.doc:
The morphism `Pᵢ ⟶ M` determined by an element `x` of `M` at the vertex `i`: it sends the basis
element of a path `p : i → j` to the image of `x` under the action of `p`.

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHom_app_basis
decls.doc:
The morphism attached to `x : Mᵢ` sends the basis vector of a path `p` to the action of `p`
on `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRepHom_app_basis (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q)
    (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)) (j : Q)
    (p : Quiver.Path i j) :
    (indecProjRepHom i M x).app ((Paths.of Q).obj j) (indecProjRepBasis k i j p) = M.map p x

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHom_app_nil
decls.doc: The morphism attached to `x : Mᵢ` sends the basis vector of the trivial path back to `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRepHom_app_nil (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q)
    (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)) :
    (indecProjRepHom i M x).app ((Paths.of Q).obj i)
      (indecProjRepBasis k i i Quiver.Path.nil) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHom_app_nil_self
decls.doc:
A morphism out of `Pᵢ` is determined by the image of the basis vector of the trivial path
at `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRepHom_app_nil_self {i : Q} {M : QuiverRep k Q} (f : indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ M) :
    indecProjRepHom i M
      (f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i) (indecProjRepBasis k i i Quiver.Path.nil)) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHomEquiv
decls.doc:
**`Pᵢ` represents evaluation at `i`.** A morphism out of `Pᵢ` is determined by, and can be
prescribed by, the image of the basis vector of the trivial path at `i`; the bijection is
`k`-linear.
decls.title: `Pᵢ` represents evaluation at `i`
decls.statement:
def indecProjRepHomEquiv (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q) :
    (indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ M) ≃ₗ[k] M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHomEquiv_apply
decls.doc:
The basis vector of the trivial path is the element of `Pᵢ` at `i` that the universal property
picks out.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRepHomEquiv_apply (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q) (f : indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ M) :
    indecProjRepHomEquiv i M f =
      f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i) (indecProjRepBasis k i i Quiver.Path.nil)

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHomEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRepHomEquiv_symm_apply (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q)
    (x : M.obj ((Paths.of Q).obj i)) :
    (indecProjRepHomEquiv i M).symm x = indecProjRepHom i M x

decls.name: TauCeti.indecProjRepHomEquiv_comp
decls.doc:
The universal property is natural in the target: postcomposition with `g` corresponds to
applying `g` at `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem indecProjRepHomEquiv_comp (i : Q) {M N : QuiverRep k Q} (f : indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ M)
    (g : M ⟶ N) :
    indecProjRepHomEquiv i N (f ≫ g) =
      g.app ((Paths.of Q).obj i) (indecProjRepHomEquiv i M f)

decls.name: TauCeti.projective_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
**The representations `Pᵢ` are projective.** A morphism out of `Pᵢ` lifts along any
epimorphism, because it is determined by a single element of the target at `i` and an epimorphism
of representations is surjective there.
decls.title: The representations `Pᵢ` are projective
decls.statement: instance projective_indecProjRep (i : Q) : Projective (indecProjRep k Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_hom_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
Morphisms out of `Pᵢ` are as many as the elements of the target at `i`: the dimension of
`Hom(Pᵢ, M)` is the `i`-th entry of the dimension vector of `M`.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_hom_indecProjRep (i : Q) (M : QuiverRep k Q) :
    Module.finrank k (indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ M) = dimVector M i

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_hom_indecProjRep_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
**The path-counting form of the Cartan matrix of a path algebra**: the dimension of
`Hom(Pᵢ, Pⱼ)` is the number of paths `j → i`.
decls.title: The path-counting form of the Cartan matrix of a path algebra
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_hom_indecProjRep_indecProjRep (i j : Q) :
    Module.finrank k (indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ indecProjRep k Q j) = Nat.card (Quiver.Path j i)

decls.name: TauCeti.not_isZero_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
The representation `Pᵢ` is nonzero: the basis vector of the trivial path at `i` is a nonzero
element of `(Pᵢ)_i`.
decls.statement: theorem not_isZero_indecProjRep (i : Q) : ¬ IsZero (indecProjRep k Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
**The Euler form against the dimension vector of `Pᵢ` is evaluation at `i`.** This is the
homological identity `⟨dim M, dim N⟩ = dim Hom(M, N) - dim Ext¹(M, N)` in the one case where it
needs no `Ext`: the projective `Pᵢ` represents evaluation at `i`.
decls.title: The Euler form against the dimension vector of `Pᵢ` is evaluation at `i`
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep (i : Q) [∀ a : Q, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)] (e : Q → ℤ) :
    eulerForm Q (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) v : ℤ)) e = e i

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_eq_finrank_hom
decls.doc:
**The homological reading of the Euler form at a projective.** For every representation `N`,
`⟨dim Pᵢ, dim N⟩` is the dimension of `Hom(Pᵢ, N)`; the `Ext¹` term of the general identity is
absent because `Pᵢ` is projective.
decls.title: The homological reading of the Euler form at a projective
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_eq_finrank_hom (i : Q) [∀ a : Q, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)]
    (N : QuiverRep k Q) :
    eulerForm Q (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) v : ℤ))
        (fun v ↦ (dimVector N v : ℤ))
      = (Module.finrank k (indecProjRep k Q i ⟶ N) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_indecProjRep
decls.doc:
**The Cartan pairing of two vertex projectives.** `⟨dim Pᵢ, dim Pⱼ⟩` counts the paths `j → i`,
which is `dim Hom(Pᵢ, Pⱼ)`: the Euler form reproduces the path-counting Cartan matrix of a path
algebra.
decls.title: The Cartan pairing of two vertex projectives
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_indecProjRep (i : Q) [∀ a : Q, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)]
    (j : Q) :
    eulerForm Q (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) v : ℤ))
        (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q j) v : ℤ))
      = (Nat.card (Quiver.Path j i) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_single
decls.doc:
**The Euler pairing of a projective against a vertex simple.** `⟨dim Pᵢ, αⱼ⟩ = δᵢⱼ`, the
dimension of `Hom(Pᵢ, Sⱼ)`: the projectives and the simples are dual bases for the Euler form.
decls.title: The Euler pairing of a projective against a vertex simple
decls.statement:
theorem eulerForm_dimVector_indecProjRep_single [DecidableEq Q] (i : Q)
    [∀ a : Q, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)] (j : Q) :
    eulerForm Q (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) v : ℤ)) (Pi.single j 1)
      = if i = j then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.titsForm_dimVector_indecProjRep
decls.doc: The Tits norm of the dimension vector of `Pᵢ` counts the closed paths at `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem titsForm_dimVector_indecProjRep (i : Q) [∀ a : Q, Finite (Quiver.Path i a)] :
    titsForm Q (fun v ↦ (dimVector (indecProjRep k Q i) v : ℤ))
      = (Nat.card (Quiver.Path i i) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep
decls.doc:
The **vertex simple** representation `Sᵢ` of a quiver: the base field `k` at the vertex `i`,
the zero module at every other vertex, and the zero map along every arrow.
decls.statement: def simpleRep (i : Q) : QuiverRep k Q

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_obj_self
decls.doc: At `i`, the vertex simple `Sᵢ` is the base field `k`.
decls.statement: theorem simpleRep_obj_self (i : Q) : (simpleRep k Q i).obj i = ModuleCat.of k k

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_obj_of_ne
decls.doc: Away from `i`, the vertex simple `Sᵢ` is the zero module.
decls.statement: theorem simpleRep_obj_of_ne {i a : Q} (h : a ≠ i) : (simpleRep k Q i).obj a = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isZero_simpleRep_obj
decls.doc: Away from `i`, the vertex simple `Sᵢ` vanishes.
decls.statement: theorem isZero_simpleRep_obj {i a : Q} (h : a ≠ i) : IsZero ((simpleRep k Q i).obj a)

decls.name: TauCeti.simple_simpleRep_obj_self
decls.doc: At `i`, the vertex simple `Sᵢ` is the simple `k`-module `k`.
decls.statement: instance simple_simpleRep_obj_self (i : Q) : Simple ((simpleRep k Q i).obj i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_simpleRep_obj
decls.statement:
instance finiteDimensional_simpleRep_obj (i a : Q) :
    FiniteDimensional k ((simpleRep k Q i).obj a)

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_map_toPath
decls.doc: Every arrow of the quiver acts by zero on the vertex simple `Sᵢ`.
decls.statement:
theorem simpleRep_map_toPath (i : Q) {a b : Q} (e : a ⟶ b) :
    (simpleRep k Q i).map e.toPath = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_map_cons
decls.doc: More generally, every path of positive length acts by zero on the vertex simple `Sᵢ`.
decls.statement:
theorem simpleRep_map_cons (i : Q) {a b c : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) (e : b ⟶ c) :
    (simpleRep k Q i).map (p.cons e) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_map_eq_zero_of_length_ne_zero
decls.doc:
A path of positive length acts by zero on the vertex simple `Sᵢ`; only the trivial paths, which
act by the identity, survive.
decls.statement:
theorem simpleRep_map_eq_zero_of_length_ne_zero (i : Q) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b)
    (hp : p.length ≠ 0) : (simpleRep k Q i).map p = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.hom_simpleRep_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
A morphism into the vertex simple `Sᵢ` vanishes as soon as its component at `i` does: all its
other components land in a zero module.
decls.statement:
theorem hom_simpleRep_eq_zero_iff {i : Q} {M : QuiverRep k Q} (f : M ⟶ simpleRep k Q i) :
    f = 0 ↔ f.app i = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_hom_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
Dually, a morphism out of the vertex simple `Sᵢ` vanishes as soon as its component at `i` does:
all its other components start from a zero module.
decls.statement:
theorem simpleRep_hom_eq_zero_iff {i : Q} {M : QuiverRep k Q} (f : simpleRep k Q i ⟶ M) :
    f = 0 ↔ f.app i = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.simpleRep_simple
decls.doc:
**The vertex simples are simple.** The vertex representation `Sᵢ = simpleRep k Q i` is a simple
object of `TauCeti.QuiverRep k Q`.
decls.title: The vertex simples are simple
decls.statement: instance simpleRep_simple (i : Q) : Simple (simpleRep k Q i)

decls.name: TauCeti.dimVector_simpleRep
decls.doc: The dimension vector of the vertex simple `Sᵢ` is the standard basis vector at `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem dimVector_simpleRep [DecidableEq Q] (i : Q) :
    dimVector (simpleRep k Q i) = Pi.single i 1

decls.name: TauCeti.not_nonempty_simpleRep_iso
decls.doc: Vertex simples at distinct vertices are not isomorphic: their dimension vectors differ.
decls.statement:
theorem not_nonempty_simpleRep_iso {i j : Q} (h : i ≠ j) :
    ¬ Nonempty (simpleRep k Q i ≅ simpleRep k Q j)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_perm_partition_eq
decls.doc: Every partition of the cardinality of a finite type is the partition of a permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_perm_partition_eq {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (p : (Fintype.card α).Partition) :
    ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm α, σ.partition = p

decls.name: TauCeti.permConjClassPartition
decls.doc: The partition of a conjugacy class of permutations.
decls.statement:
def permConjClassPartition {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α) → (Fintype.card α).Partition

decls.name: TauCeti.permConjClassPartition_mk
decls.doc: Taking the partition of the class of a permutation recovers its partition.
decls.statement:
theorem permConjClassPartition_mk {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (σ : Equiv.Perm α) :
    permConjClassPartition (ConjClasses.mk σ) = σ.partition

decls.name: TauCeti.permConjClassPartition_injective
decls.doc: The partition distinguishes conjugacy classes of permutations.
decls.statement:
theorem permConjClassPartition_injective {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    Function.Injective (permConjClassPartition (α := α))

decls.name: TauCeti.permConjClassPartition_surjective
decls.doc: Every partition is attained by a conjugacy class of permutations.
decls.statement:
theorem permConjClassPartition_surjective {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    Function.Surjective (permConjClassPartition (α := α))

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivPermConjClasses
decls.doc:
Partitions of the cardinality of a finite type are equivalent to conjugacy classes of its
permutations.
decls.statement:
def partitionEquivPermConjClasses (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    (Fintype.card α).Partition ≃ ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α)

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivConjClasses
decls.doc: Partitions of `n` are equivalent to conjugacy classes of the symmetric group on `Fin n`.
decls.statement:
def partitionEquivConjClasses (n : ℕ) :
    n.Partition ≃ ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))

decls.name: TauCeti.permConjClassPartition_partitionEquivPermConjClasses
decls.doc: The conjugacy class associated to a partition has that partition.
decls.statement:
theorem permConjClassPartition_partitionEquivPermConjClasses (α : Type*) [Fintype α]
    [DecidableEq α] (p : (Fintype.card α).Partition) :
    permConjClassPartition (partitionEquivPermConjClasses α p) = p

decls.name: TauCeti.permConjClassPartition_partitionEquivConjClasses
decls.doc: The conjugacy class associated to a partition of `n` has that partition.
decls.statement:
theorem permConjClassPartition_partitionEquivConjClasses (n : ℕ) (p : n.Partition) :
    permConjClassPartition (partitionEquivConjClasses n p) =
      Equiv.cast (congrArg Nat.Partition (Fintype.card_fin n).symm) p

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivPermConjClasses_symm_mk
decls.doc: The inverse class-to-partition map sends a representative to its permutation partition.
decls.statement:
theorem partitionEquivPermConjClasses_symm_mk (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (σ : Equiv.Perm α) :
    (partitionEquivPermConjClasses α).symm (ConjClasses.mk σ) = σ.partition

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivConjClasses_symm_mk
decls.doc:
The inverse class-to-partition map for `Fin n` sends a representative to its permutation
partition.
decls.statement:
theorem partitionEquivConjClasses_symm_mk (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (partitionEquivConjClasses n).symm (ConjClasses.mk σ) =
      (Equiv.cast (congrArg Nat.Partition (Fintype.card_fin n).symm)).symm
        σ.partition

decls.name: TauCeti.card_conjClasses_perm_eq_card_partition
decls.doc:
The number of conjugacy classes of permutations of a finite type is the number of partitions
of its cardinality.
decls.statement:
theorem card_conjClasses_perm_eq_card_partition (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    Fintype.card (ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α)) =
      Fintype.card (Fintype.card α).Partition

decls.name: TauCeti.card_conjClasses_perm
decls.doc:
The number of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group on `Fin n` is the number of partitions
of `n`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_conjClasses_perm (n : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) = Fintype.card n.Partition

decls.name: TauCeti.permutationModule
decls.doc:
The Young permutation module `M^μ` over `ℚ`.

Its standard basis is indexed by the left cosets of `youngSubgroup μ`; these cosets are the
`μ`-tabloids, and the symmetric group acts on them by left multiplication.
decls.statement:
abbrev permutationModule {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    Rep ℚ (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))

decls.name: TauCeti.permutationModuleBasis
decls.doc: The standard basis of `M^μ`, indexed by the `μ`-tabloids.
decls.statement:
abbrev permutationModuleBasis {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    Module.Basis (Equiv.Perm (Fin n) ⧸ youngSubgroup μ) ℚ
      (permutationModule μ).V

decls.name: TauCeti.permutationModuleIsoIndTrivial
decls.doc:
The Young permutation module is induction of the trivial representation of the Young
subgroup.
decls.statement:
def permutationModuleIsoIndTrivial {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    permutationModule μ ≅
      Rep.ind (youngSubgroup μ).subtype
        (Rep.trivial ℚ (youngSubgroup μ) ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_permutationModule_eq_index
decls.doc: The dimension of `M^μ` is the index of its Young subgroup.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_permutationModule_eq_index {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    Module.finrank ℚ (permutationModule μ).V = (youngSubgroup μ).index

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_permutationModule
decls.doc:
The dimension of `M^μ` is the multinomial coefficient
`n! / ∏ i, μᵢ!`.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_permutationModule {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    Module.finrank ℚ (permutationModule μ).V =
      n.factorial / (μ.parts.map Nat.factorial).prod

decls.name: TauCeti.char_permutationModule
decls.doc: The character of `M^μ` at `σ` is the number of `μ`-tabloids fixed by `σ`.
decls.statement:
theorem char_permutationModule {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (permutationModule μ).ρ.character σ =
      (Nat.card
        {q : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) ⧸ youngSubgroup μ // σ • q = q} : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.permutationModuleFDRep
decls.doc: The Young permutation module bundled as a finite-dimensional representation.
decls.statement:
abbrev permutationModuleFDRep {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    FDRep ℚ (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_permutationModuleFDRep
decls.doc: The bundled Young permutation module has the same multinomial dimension.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_permutationModuleFDRep {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    Module.finrank ℚ (permutationModuleFDRep μ) =
      n.factorial / (μ.parts.map Nat.factorial).prod

decls.name: TauCeti.char_permutationModuleFDRep
decls.doc: The character of the bundled Young permutation module counts fixed tabloids.
decls.statement:
theorem char_permutationModuleFDRep {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (permutationModuleFDRep μ).character σ =
      (Nat.card
        {q : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) ⧸ youngSubgroup μ // σ • q = q} : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.singleUnit
decls.doc:
The group-algebra basis element of `g`, as a unit whose inverse is the basis element of `g⁻¹`.
Private: this is the group-algebra plumbing for the conjugation computations and for the
right-translation equivalence below.
decls.statement: def singleUnit (g : G) : (MonoidAlgebra ℚ G)ˣ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.coe_singleUnit
decls.statement:
